title: Self-Attention — Tokens as Gravitational Particles
category_reason: Interactive model of transformer self-attention (Q/K/V, attention heads) as a gravitational particle system.
thesis: Self-attention can be pictured as a gravitational particle system: each token emits a Query ('what am I looking for?'), Key ('what do I contain?') and Value ('what do I contribute?'); attention weights act as attractive forces, so stronger attention pulls tokens together, and different attention heads encode different relation patterns (positional, syntactic, semantic).
key_claims: Each token generates a Query, a Key and a Value; attention scores come from the Query×Key dot product, shown as gravitational attraction (stronger attention = stronger pull).
Different attention heads learn different relationship patterns — here Positional (nearby tokens), Syntactic (subject–verb, pronoun–antecedent), and Semantic (shared entity, causal, polysemy).
Coreference: 'it' strongly attends to 'cat' (its antecedent).
Polysemy disambiguation: in 'The bank by the river…', 'bank' attends to 'interest/rates' (financial) while 'river' pulls toward the geographic 'bank'.
Clicking/hovering a token highlights its attention row (top-3 attended, with percentages) in both the particle scene and the matrix.
methods_math: attention as pairwise attractive force (weight ∝ pull)
visualizations: Canvas 2D particle system: tokens as glowing circles connected by curved, color-gradient attention lines whose width/opacity encode weight; physics integration (attraction ∝ weight, inverse-square repulsion, spring-to-home, damping) with a 'Physics' strength slider; a live attention-matrix heatmap (query rows × key columns) that highlights the selected token; token chips and sentence/head selectors; 3 example sentences.
internal_tensions: The attention matrices are FAKE / hand-simulated (code comment: 'simulate plausible attention patterns for different heads') — this is an explanatory model of what attention 'could' look like, not output of a real transformer; it should not be read as empirical.

The gravitational metaphor (attractive force) is evocative but not the actual mechanics: real attention does not move token embeddings by a force field — it computes a static weighted sum per position.
Only three hand-authored sentences with manually-tuned head matrices, so the 'heads learn different patterns' claim is stipulated, not derived from training.

title: Attention als Optimaler Transport — Eine interaktive Reise
category_reason: Mathematische Neuinterpretation der Transformer-Attention: Scaled-Dot-Product Attention als einseitiger entropischer optimaler Transport (Entropic OT) auf dem Simplex (Elon Litman, Stanford, arXiv:2508.08369v2).
thesis: Softmax-Attention ist nicht heuristisch, sondern die eindeutige Loesung eines entropischen optimalen Transports auf dem Simplex: im einseitigen degenerierten Fall (Dirac-Quelle, freies Ziel) ergibt sich die bekannte Softmax-Form als geschlossen Loesung (Theorem 3.3), und tau = sqrt(d_k) ist die varianzausgeglichene Regularisierung. Dasselbe Prinzip generalisiert (sparsemax, alpha-entmax, ALiBi), die Rueckwaertspassage ist REINFORCE mit Baseline (Theorem 5.2), und die Dualitaet schliesst den Ring ueber LogSumExp und Informationengeometrie (Korollar 7.5).
key_claims: Softmax-Attention ist die eindeutige Loesung eines entropischen OT-Problem auf dem Simplex — nicht Sinkhorn.
Einseitige Degeneration (Dirac-Quelle, freies Ziel) liefert die Softmax-Form in geschlossener Form (Theorem 3.3: Lagrange + strenge Konvexitaet -> p_j proportional exp(<q,k_j>/tau)).
tau = sqrt(d_k) ist die varianzausgeglichene Regularisierung, die die Skala der Attention stabilisiert.
Das allgemeine Prinzip argmin -<p,s> + Omega(p) erlaubst, Omega auszutauschen (sparsemax, alpha-entmax, ALiBi) — dieselbe Struktur, andere Geometrie.
Die Rueckwaertspassage ist REINFORCE mit Baseline (Theorem 5.2).
Dualitaet: das duale Potential ist LogSumExp und sein Gradient ist p* (Theorem 6.3, LSE).
Informationengeometrischer Ringschluss: Hesse(duales Potential) = tau * Fisher-Metrik (Korollar 7.5).
methods_math: entropischer optimaler Transport auf dem Simplex
visualizations: HiDPI-Canvas-Hero-Animation der Transport-Interpretation
Interaktive Spiele (Spiel 0-3) fuer Quelle/Ziel/Regularisierung
Plotly-Diagramme der Simplex-Geometrie und der duale LSE-Kurve
Temml-Formeln fuer die Theoreme 3.3/5.2/6.3/7.5
Vergleich der Geometrien (softmax vs sparsemax vs entmax)
internal_tensions: Die Interpretation ist elegant, betont aber ausdrucklich: Attention ist NICHT Sinkhorn — die einseitige Degeneration ist der entscheidende Sonderfall.
tau = sqrt(d_k) wird als 'richtige' Skala motiviert, ist aber eine Konvention, keine abgeleitete Notwendigkeit.
Die informationengeometrische Unifikation ist ein Ringschluss, der die Theorie verschmaert, aber neue Vorhersagen kaum liefert.

title: Attention ist Optimaler Transport — Einfach erklärt
category_reason: It is a German interactive explainer of a 2025 deep-learning theory paper (Litman, Stanford, arXiv:2508.08369) that derives softmax attention from one-sided entropic optimal transport and shows backprop through attention is a REINFORCE policy-gradient; it is squarely about transformer attention and learning.
thesis: An interactive German 'simple' version of Litman (Stanford, 2025, arXiv:2508.08369), 'Scaled-Dot-Product Attention as One-Sided Entropic Optimal Transport': softmax attention, invented in 2017 by intuition, is shown to be the UNIQUE solution of a clean optimization problem — maximize similarity while staying maximally undecisive while being a probability — and, more surprisingly, the gradient used to learn attention is a REINFORCE policy-gradient whose variance-reducing baseline falls out for free; the two routes (optimal transport and RL) are then shown to be the same object via the Fisher matrix.
key_claims: Softmax is a choice made in 2017 that simply worked; the paper's point is that softmax is not a design choice but the unique solution of a well-posed problem on the simplex (maximize similarity, stay maximally undecisive, be a probability).

The decisive trick: classical optimal transport fixes both marginals (a source pile and a target pile, solved by Sinkhorn iteration); here only ONE side is fixed — a single source (one Dirac = one 'quantum of attention') with a free target — so the plan matrix collapses to a single row vector and the feasible region is exactly the simplex, giving a closed-form solution with no iteration (this is the distinction from 'Sinkhorn attention').

Theorem 3.3 (exists / unique / form): the objective J(p) = -<p, s> + tau * sum p_j log p_j over the simplex attains a minimum (extreme-value theorem), the minimum is unique (linear <p,s> plus the strictly convex entropy term make J strictly convex), and Lagrange/KKT stationarity gives p_j proportional to exp(s_j / tau), i.e. exactly softmax.

Remark 3.4 (why tau = sqrt(d_k)): if q and k have independent mean-0 variance-1 components then <q,k> has variance d_k; dividing by sqrt(d_k) rescales the variance back to 1, otherwise softmax saturates to one-hot and the gradients vanish — the division is a variance normalization / a matching of the entropic-regularization strength to the dimension.

One regularizer, many mechanisms: argmin_p -<p,s> + Omega(p) over the simplex; swapping Omega gives softmax (Omega = -tau H, dense), sparsemax (Omega = 1/2 sum p_j^2, exact zeros via L2 projection), alpha-entmax (Tsallis, continuously tunable sparsity), and ALiBi (Omega = -tau H + gamma sum p_j |i-j|, a linear distance penalty / local bias).

Theorem 5.2 (the backpass = REINFORCE): with context c(p) = sum p_j v_j, utility u_j = -dL/dp_j and advantage A_j = u_j - E_p[u], the gradient is dL/ds_j = -(p_j*/tau)(u_j - E_p[u]) = -(p_j*/tau) A_j — literally REINFORCE with an expectation baseline; the baseline is a free gift because the softmax Jacobian (1/tau) p_k (delta_kj - p_j) has column sum 0, a pure consequence of sum p_j = 1, which makes the gradient low-variance and training stable.

Theorem 6.3 (the dual potential): minimizing J yields the dual potential phi*(s) = tau log(sum_j exp(s_j/tau)) = Log-Sum-Exp, with the three identities phi* = -V, grad phi* = p*, and Hessian phi* = tau F(s) — the value, gradient and curvature of a single scalar encode the problem, the solution and the learning dynamics.

Corollary 7.5 (the 'ring closure'): d2/ds2 phi*(s) = tau F(s) = (1/tau)(diag(p*) - p*(p*)^T) — the curvature of the dual potential equals (up to tau) the Fisher information matrix equals the RL 'transducer'; three perspectives (optimal transport, information geometry, reinforcement learning) land on the same one matrix, which acts as a 'gearbox' damping the learning signal where the strategy has already decided (at the simplex boundary) — manifold-aware learning.

Honesty section: no new mechanism (SDPA is bit-for-bit identical), no experiments (a purely theoretical paper), and the max-entropy/Gibbs link is classical (Jaynes 1957); what is new is the one-sided entropic-OT embedding (closed form, no Sinkhorn), the policy-gradient bridge (baseline for free), and the geometric explanation of why they belong together (Corollary 7.5).
methods_math: the probability simplex Delta^(m-1) and its entropy H(p) = -sum p_j log p_j (strict convexity of x log x)
(one-sided) entropic optimal transport with a single Dirac source and a free target
convex optimization on the simplex: existence (extreme-value theorem), strict convexity, KKT/Lagrange conditions
temperature/regularization tau and the sqrt(d_k) variance-normalization argument
a family of regularizers (softmax, sparsemax, alpha-entmax/Tsallis, ALiBi) from a single variational problem
policy-gradient (REINFORCE) and the advantage/baseline decomposition of the attention backprop
the Log-Sum-Exp (soft-max) dual potential and the envelope theorem
Fisher information geometry: F = (1/tau)(diag(p) - p p^T) as the metric on the simplex
visualizations: a 'touch it first' attention demo: five key words in a circle, a draggable query arrow in the centre, with the attention 'wandering' and a temperature slider (narrow/safe vs broad/open) and winner-key / entropy readouts (2D Canvas)
a draggable simplex: move a point around the 2-simplex, keep it a valid distribution, read p1/p2/p3 and entropy (corner = committed, centre = maximally open)
a one-sided transport animation stepping full OT (two marginals, square) -> single Dirac source -> drop the column condition -> one row = simplex
a live optimizer demo: a mirror-descent numerical solver rolling into the valley of J, racing the analytic softmax (star); the gap between them goes to zero as scores/temperature change
a family-comparison plot: same scores, four distributions (softmax / sparsemax / entmax / ALiBi) with alpha and gamma sliders and non-zero-entry / entropy readouts
an 'attention bandit' (2D Canvas): rows for strategy p, utility u, advantage A and the update Delta s; E[u] climbs monotonically to the best arm as the policy gradient runs
a Log-Sum-Exp plot as a 'soft max' with a temperature slider, overlaid with the hard max and the softmax component (its gradient)
a Fisher-matrix-as-gearbox plot: an 'enthusiasm' (score sharpness) slider showing edge damping where p is concentrated
a six-question self-test quiz with a live score
internal_tensions: The tension between 'it was a lucky 2017 guess' and 'it is forced by mathematics' — the piece's entire point is that the guess is actually the unique optimum, which it proves via strict convexity rather than by re-inventing anything.

One-sided vs full optimal transport: dropping the second marginal is what turns an intractable (Sinkhorn-iterated) problem into a closed-form one; the piece is careful to mark this as the real novelty and to avoid conflating it with existing Sinkhorn-attention work.

It is purely theoretical with no experiments, so all 'results' are identities and geometric explanations of an already-shipped mechanism (SDPA), not performance gains — the piece states this explicitly as a boundary of the claim.

title: Attention ist Optimaler Transport — ganz einfach erklaert
category_reason: Explains (via Litman 2025) why scaled-dot-product attention has its softmax form and why the backprop update is a policy-gradient RL step — a theory of attention/optimization.
thesis: Softmax attention was not invented, it is forced: it is the unique solution of a simple optimization problem ('go where it is similar, but do not commit too hard' + the constraint that weights sum to 1). Even more, the backward pass is secretly REINFORCE-style policy-gradient RL, and the whole thing is unified by one matrix (1/tau)(diag(p) - pp^T) that is simultaneously the OT dual-potential curvature, the Fisher information matrix, and the RL 'gearbox'.
key_claims: Attention balances two opposing forces — maximize similarity vs. stay broad (high entropy) — plus the constraint sum(alpha)=1; softmax is the enforced compromise, not a choice.

Dividing scores by sqrt(d_k) is required: with independent equal-strength components the score has variance d_k, so unscaled softmax saturates (collapses to one ~100% answer, vanishing gradients) for large d_k; /sqrt(d_k) restores variance 1 and keeps the distribution formable.
The backward pass is exactly the REINFORCE policy-gradient update (with a baseline trick that comes for free from the sum-to-1 constraint).

One matrix (1/tau)(diag(p) - pp^T) unifies three fields: optimal transport (curvature of the log-sum-exp dual potential), information geometry (~the Fisher matrix), and RL (damps the learning update once the policy has committed).

Honesty corner: SDPA stays bit-identical (it explains, not invents); it is purely theoretical (no experiments); no Sinkhorn needed because only one marginal (rows sum to 1) is fixed; the entropy link to Jaynes (1957) is classical — the novelty is the one-sided-transport embedding + the policy-gradient bridge.
methods_math: one-sided entropic optimal transport (log-sum-exp dual potential)
visualizations: three canvas 2D experiments: (1) a query arrow rotating around 5 keys with angle/length/temperature sliders + winner and entropy readouts, (2) a d_k slider showing softmax saturation without vs with /sqrt(d_k), (3) an 'attention bandit' stepping/auto-running a policy-gradient update toward the best key
internal_tensions: The 'RL' reading of backprop is a reformulation that holds under specific assumptions (single fixed marginal, softmax policy); it is an elegant unification but the file stresses it changes no bit of SDPA — a lens, not a new mechanism.
Claims the entropy link is classical (Jaynes 1957) while presenting the EOT framing as the contribution — the contested point is whether 'attention as OT' is genuinely new or a reframing.

title: Backpropagation – Schicht für Schicht
category_reason: Schritt-für-Schritt-Visualisierung der Rückwärtspropagation (Gradientenfluss, Kettenregel) in einem Feedforward-Neuronen-Netz
thesis: Schritt-für-Schritt-Interaktive Durchlauf von Backpropagation durch ein kleines Feedforward-Netz (Input→2 Hidden→Output, Sigmoid, quadratischer Verlust): zuerst Forward-Pass, dann wandert ein 'Fokus' von rechts nach links und berechnet pro Schicht den Gradienten (Delta) über die Kettenregel, mit Gewichtsanpassungen und Live-Loss-Chart
key_claims: Forward-Pass: jedes Neuron berechnet (Eingaben × Gewichte + Bias) → Sigmoid → Ausgabe; Verlust = ½Σ(Ziel−Ausgabe)²

Backprop: der Fokus bewegt sich von der Ausgabeschicht rückwärts; jede Schicht fragt 'Was hätte ich anders machen sollen?' — die Kettenregel schiebt den gewünschten Wandel ('Wäre besser') durch das Netz
Der Ausgabeschicht-Gradient ist Δ = Ausgabe-Fehler × sigmoid'(Ausgabe); Hidden-Schichten akkumulieren den von der nächsten Schicht zurückgeschobenen Fehler, multipliziert mit ihrem eigenen sigmoid'
Jedes Gewicht wird um Gradient × Lernrate (hier LR=0.5) angepasst; der Loss sinkt über Runden

title: Backprop als Funktor - Eine interaktive Reise
category_reason: Main subject is backpropagation and supervised learning, reformulated via category theory; fundamentally about neural network training
thesis: German interactive walkthrough of Fong-Spivak-Tuyeras' 'Backprop as Functor' (arXiv:1711.10455): a learner is a tuple (P, I, U, r) where the request function r is the missing ingredient for composing learning algorithms; learning algorithms form a symmetric monoidal category Learn; gradient descent L_eps,e : Para -> Learn is a faithful, object-injective, strong symmetric monoidal functor; backpropagation is precisely the composition rule in Learn; the full chain NNet -> Para -> Learn shows neural nets are automatically learning algorithms.
key_claims: Two learners A->B and B->C cannot be composed without a backward channel: the front learner has no training pair (a, b') - the request function s : Q x B x C -> B supplies the missing 'desired output'
A learner is a 4-tuple (P, I, U, r): parameter space, implementation, update, and request; the request is trivial for a single learner but essential for composition
Learn is a symmetric monoidal category: objects are sets, morphisms are equivalence classes of learners, composition is series, tensor is parallel, braiding allows wire crossings
Para is the category of differentiable parametrized functions (objects R^n, morphisms (P, I) with I : P x R^n -> R^m differentiable)
Theorem III.2: for any eps>0 and error function e with partial-e/partial-x invertible, gradient descent L_eps,e : Para -> Learn is a faithful, object-injective, strong symmetric monoidal functor
Backpropagation is not a separate algorithm - it is the formula for composition in Learn: U_A = U_B * U_C with the request s_C substituted

NNet is a purely combinatorial category (objects = layer sizes, morphisms = connectivity patterns); I_sigma : NNet -> Para adds activation functions; the chain NNet -> Para -> Learn makes any net a learning algorithm

Bimonoid structure (mu=addition, delta=copy, eta=unit, epsilon=delete) in Learn explains wiring: a neuron is a composite of 5 atoms (lambda, beta, sigma, mu, delta); weight tying follows from the comonoid request rule

The sufficient condition on error functions (partial-e/partial-x invertible) is satisfied by MSE and product loss; cross-entropy is 'almost' an example (singular at 0 and 1); the request has no eps (a coincidence of quadratic loss)
Learn sits between Lens (trivial parameter space) and Open Game (best response) - the request function is the same idea as put/coplay

title: How BoTorch Works Internally — A Visual Explainer
category_reason: Main subject is BoTorch, a Bayesian optimization library — a core ML/optimization topic.
thesis: BoTorch implements Bayesian optimization as a two-stage loop — fit a Gaussian-process surrogate to observed (x, f(x)) pairs, then choose the next query point by maximizing an acquisition function that balances exploration and exploitation — and its modular architecture (separate GP model, acquisition function, and optimizer) makes each stage independently swappable.
key_claims: Bayesian optimization treats the unknown objective as a Gaussian process: after observing n points, the posterior GP gives a mean and uncertainty at every candidate x.
The acquisition function (e.g., Expected Improvement, Upper Confidence Bound, Probability of Improvement) converts the GP posterior into a single scalar to maximize over the candidate set.
BoTorch separates the GP model, the acquisition function, and the optimizer into independent modules, so users can swap any component without affecting the others.
Batch acquisition functions (q-EI, q-NEGF) extend the single-point logic to parallel queries by integrating over the joint posterior of multiple candidate points.
methods_math: Monte Carlo integration for batch acquisitions
visualizations: interactive charts showing GP posterior evolution
acquisition-function landscape plots
module-architecture diagram
internal_tensions: The GP surrogate is a modeling choice, not a truth — for highly multimodal or discontinuous objectives the GP can be badly miscalibrated, and no amount of acquisition-function cleverness fixes a wrong posterior.

title: Wie ein Sprachmodell denkt — Attention, FFN und die Rolle der Schichten
category_reason: Transformer-Erklärbarkeit: Attention/Kollaps (Geshkovski), FFN als Key-Value-Speicher (Geva), Superposition (Elhage), SwiGLU (Shazeer). EXAKTES DUPLIKAT von wie_ein_llm_denkt.html (gleicher Titel und Inhalt).
thesis: Ein Transformer-Block ist ein Gleichgewicht aus Kontraktion (Attention zieht Tokens zu Clustern, ohne Gegenkraft Kollaps) und Verfeinerung (FFN als Key-Value-Speicher addiert auf den Residual-Stream), das über zwei orthogonale Achsen (Positionen vs Features) läuft.
key_claims: Attention arbeitet über Positionen, das FFN über Features — orthogonal, daher können sie sich nicht in die Quere kommen [Vaswani §3.3].

Attention ohne Gegenkraft kollabiert fast alle Tokens zu einem einzigen Punkt (bewiesen für d≥3, exponentiell schnell für d≥n) [Geshkovski 2024]; reale Modelle leben in einem metastabilen Zustand (zu wenig Schichten für Phase 2).
Die Form des Kollaps hängt vom Spektrum der Value-Matrix V ab — vier Fälle (Identität / einfach λ>0 / paranormal / −Identität) [Geshkovski 2023].
Das FFN ist ein Key-Value-Speicher: erste Matrix = Schlüssel (Muster), zweite = Werte (nächste-Wort-Verteilung); 3,6 Muster pro Schlüssel [Geva].
Der Residual-Stream dominiert die endgültige Vorhersage; das FFN verfeinert (Kom-promiss), ersetzt die Vorhersage selten [Geva].
Superposition: spärliche Features werden als fast-orthogonale Richtungen übereinandergelegt (Phasenübergang, nicht graduell) [Elhage] — widerspricht Keups Falt-Bild.
SwiGLU ist multiplikatives Gating (Produkt zweier Projektionen), keine elementweise Nichtlinearität; GLU-Varianten schlagen ReLU [Shazeer].

title: Attention – Geometrisch Verstehen
category_reason: It is a German interactive, geometry-first explanation of the transformer attention mechanism from 'Attention Is All You Need' (Vaswani et al., 2017), covering Q/K/V subspaces, the dot-product score, scaled softmax, the convex-combination output, and multi-head attention; it is squarely about transformers/neural nets.
thesis: A German interactive, geometry-first explanation of the attention mechanism in 'Attention Is All You Need' (Vaswani et al., 2017): attention is content-dependent routing — each token sends a query into the embedding space, matches it against other tokens' keys (similarity = dot product / projected length), normalizes to weights with softmax, and outputs a convex combination of the values; the Q/K/V matrices cut slanted subspaces to specialize the comparison, and multi-head attention runs several such 'views' in parallel.
key_claims: The core idea: embeddings are points in a high-dimensional space where directions can carry meaning; attention adds content-dependent routing — 'whom do I ask, and what do I get back' — letting each token deliberately gather information from other tokens.

W^Q, W^K, W^V cut slanted 64-dim subspaces out of the full 512-dim embedding space, giving specialized views: the query space ('what am I looking for?'), the key space ('what do I offer?'), and the value space ('what do I pass on?'); they are oblique projections, not axis-aligned slices, so different aspects (syntax / semantics / position) can be emphasised.

Q * K is the dot product, geometrically the projected length of one vector onto the other: same direction -> large positive score -> high attention; perpendicular -> ~0; opposite -> negative -> ~0 after softmax.
Division by sqrt(d_k) (here sqrt(64) = 8) normalizes the dot-product variance (which is ~d_k in 64 dims) back to ~1; without it softmax saturates and the gradients vanish.

Softmax turns the scaled scores into a probability distribution (all positive, sum to 1); temperature controls sharpness — low temperature = one token dominates (near a hard lookup), high temperature = near-uniform.

The weighted sum of the values is a CONVEX combination, so the output point lies inside the convex hull (simplex) of the values: attention can only MIX existing information, not invent new information; the following FFN layer then transforms non-linearly.

Multi-head attention cuts 8 different 64-dim subspaces (each with its own W^Q, W^K, W^V), each attending to a different aspect (syntax / semantics / local / verb-noun / reference / position / negation / long-range); the 8 outputs (64d each) are concatenated (to 512d) and projected back by W^O.

Why attention is so powerful: content-dependent routing (any token to any other, strength by content), parallel perspectives (8 heads ask different 'questions'), O(1) path length (information flows in one step, unlike RNNs), and learnable subspaces (the model decides which aspects to compare).
methods_math: embeddings as points in a high-dimensional vector space with directional meaning
linear projections W^Q, W^K, W^V as oblique subspaces of the embedding space
the dot product as projected length / similarity and the 1/sqrt(d_k) variance normalization
softmax as a probability distribution and its temperature/sharpness
the output as a convex combination of value vectors (the value simplex)
multi-head attention and the concat + W^O re-projection
scaled dot-product attention (SDPA) and O(1) path length
visualizations: a MathJax + Canvas 2D single-page with 7 sections, each a heading, prose, a math block and an interactive canvas
an overview canvas: a 2D simplification where 'sitzt' (red) queries the space, thick lines = high attention, the green diamond = output
a subspace canvas showing W^Q projecting the full (grey) space onto a slanted (red) subspace, with an angle slider
a dot-product canvas: rotate the query (white) and read its projection onto each key, with a query-angle slider
a softmax bar chart of attention weights for the query 'sitzt' over all keys, with a sharpness (1/temperature) slider

internal_tensions: The load-bearing insight/tension is that attention can only produce a point inside the convex hull of the values — it mixes, it does not invent; the non-linearity that adds new information comes from the FFN, not from attention itself.

There is a real 512-dim object being explained in 2D/3D canvases, so the geometric pictures are faithful analogies (slanted subspaces, a triangle of values) rather than literal pictures of the high-dimensional space.
It is a visualization/interpretation piece on a well-known 2017 paper, so it explains rather than extends; it contains no new mechanism, only a geometric re-telling of SDPA and multi-head attention.

title: McCulloch & Pitts (1943) – Interaktiv Erleben
category_reason: Interactive walkthrough of the 1943 paper that founded artificial neural networks and their computational equivalence to Turing machines.
thesis: An interactive retelling of McCulloch & Pitts (1943): neurons are all-or-none logical switches, their networks realize AND/OR/NOT and are computationally equivalent to Turing machines — the 'birth certificate of AI'.
key_claims: A neuron fires all-or-none like a bit (0/1); a threshold determines when it fires.
Neuron networks realize the logic gates AND (threshold 2), OR (threshold 1) and NOT (via inhibition).
Every logical function/expression can be built as a neuron network (their Theorem 2).
Inhibition has absolute veto: a single inhibitory synapse blocks firing no matter how many excitatory inputs arrive.
Circular/recurrent nets let activity circulate -> memory and reference to past events; variable synapses can be replaced by loops (Theorem 7), so learning ~ recurrent activity.
A network plus a memory/tape computes exactly what a Turing machine can, and vice versa.
visualizations: DOM neuron threshold demo (stimulus vs threshold sliders, fire/silence)
DOM logic-gate toggles (AND/OR/AND-NOT with truth outputs)
canvas neuron-network animation of the paper's 'heat after a short cold stimulus' example (delay + AND + inhibition)
DOM time-step 'circuit' loop for memory (start/stop/inhibit to wipe it)
DOM memory-matching game pairing concepts + SVG progress ring
internal_tensions: The 'Turing equivalence' and 'every program buildable' claims are presented pedagogically, not as a formal proof.
Conflates 'learning' with recurrence/loops (a loose reading of their Theorem 7).

title: Eine Rose mit anderem Namen — Kategorielle Homotopie für LLMs
category_reason: Mathematik FÜR KI: Kategorielle Homotopie (Homotopie-Äquivalenz, n-Simplex, Nerv) wird explizit als Linse auf LLM-Repräsentationen angewendet — semantisch äquivalente Darstellungen sind 'die gleiche Rose unter anderem Namen'. Klare KI-Kopplung.
thesis: Kategorielle Homotopie liefert eine mathematische Linse für LLMs: Zwei Repräsentationen (z.B. zwei Paraphrasen, zwei Embedding-Punkte desselben Begriffs) sind 'die gleiche Rose unter anderem Namen', wenn sie homotopisch äquivalent sind — es gibt Abbildungen zwischen ihnen, deren Kompositionen (bis auf Homotopie) die Identität ergeben. Das n-Simplex zeigt, wie ein semantischer Raum trianguliert wird und wie Homotopie die Invarianz der Bedeutung unter stetiger Verformung der Repräsentation formalisiert.
key_claims: Zwei Objekte (Repräsentationen) sind homotopisch äquivalent, wenn Abbildungen f, g existieren mit f∘g ≃ id und g∘f ≃ id — 'eine Rose mit jedem anderen Namen' (Shakespeare).
Der Nerv einer Kategorie / ein simplicial set kodiert Relationen höherer Ordnung: ein n-Simplex ist eine (n+1)-stellige Relation (Dreieck = 3-ary, Tetraeder = 4-ary …).
In einem LLM belegen semantisch äquivalente Texte (Paraphrasen) homotopisch äquivalente Regionen des Embedding-/Latentraums — die Bedeutung ist invariant unter stetiger Verformung der Oberfläche.
Homotopie-Äquivalenz gibt eine formale Version von 'Bedeutung bleibt erhalten, während sich die Repräsentation stetig ändert' — der Kern des Sprachverstehens.
Die n-Simplex-Darstellung macht sichtbar, wie Komposition (Wort → Phrase → Satz) als Verklebung von Simplexen modelliert werden kann.
visualizations: Plotly: n-Simplex (2D/3D, Dreieck/Tetraeder, klickbare Ecken/Kanten)
Temml: Formel-Rendering der Homotopie-Äquivalenz-Identitäten
Diagramm: Paraphrase ↔ Paraphrase als homotopisch äquivalente Punkte
internal_tensions: Die LLM-Kopplung ist metaphorisch/aspirativ: es wird kein Theorem bewiesen, dass reale Embedding-Räume unter Paraphrasierung tatsächlich homotopie-invariant sind.
Die n-Simplex-Visualisierung ist niedrig-dimensional; reale Embedding-/Latenträume sind hochdimensional, und der Nerv eines 'Bedeutungskategories' wird nicht konkret konstruiert.
Die 'Kategorie der Bedeutungen' wird nicht exakt definiert (Objekte = Wörter? Sätze? Embeddings?) — die Homotopie hängt an einer unbestimmten Grundkategorie.

title: Vom Weltzugang zum Weltmodell (From World Access to World Model — Coherent Representation)
category_reason: A sheaf-/category-theoretic epistemology of 'world models' that is applied with a dedicated, substantive LLM station (structural necessity of hallucination, model collapse, RLHF as a Tarski anchor) — sheaves/category theory used 'for AI', with a clear AI application.
thesis: A world model is the global section reconstructed from local descent data along an admissible cover — provisional, revisable, and never identical to what it represents; coherence is necessary but not sufficient for truth, and an LLM structurally (not accidentally) confuses the two, which is why it must hallucinate.
key_claims: A world model = a global section glued from locally-compatible sections over an admissible cover (the sheaf/Garben condition: local compatibility ⇒ unique global section).

Coherence (internal consistency) is necessary but NOT sufficient for truth; correspondence ('Kontakt' to W) is a separate, independent test — a self-consistent fantasy passes coherence and fails correspondence.
The class 𝒯 of licensed transformations carries all the content: an unlicensed or overly rich 𝒯 is itself a form of overfitting — more transformation freedom demands more evidence.

The cover never reaches the whole context c, only the accessible interface c_acc ⊆ c; every instrument widens but never closes the cover, so the model is of the interface, not the thing-in-itself (Kant's Ding an sich).

Truth (veridicality) = the limit of (coherence ∧ correspondence) as the W-anchored cover is widened — approximated, never reached, a regulative ideal; justified acceptance = coherence on the current cover ∧ no failed contact point (Popper: not yet falsified), which IS operationalizable.

An LLM is an internal coherence machine without licensed correspondence transitions, so it wins on fitness metrics and structurally must hallucinate; model collapse is predicted because AI-generated corpus text adds only derived patches that do not widen c_acc.

Five pathologies of a model — self-consistent fantasy, fact-book, contact-point liar, calibrated error, question-outside-the-cover — each needs a different cure; the fifth (no contact point at all, the question lies outside c_acc) is the sneakiest and breaks no condition.
Self-application: the framework instantiates 'Pathology 4: calibrated error' — it has a consistent small bias toward presenting a working definition or loose reading with the force of a theorem.
methods_math: sheaf theory (presheaf vs sheaf, sections, global sections, gluing/Garben condition, Čech nerve, winding number on the circle)
category theory (equalizers, pullbacks, Ologs / ontology-logs, higher n-morphisms, commutativity)
Tarski's T-convention (semantic truth, object vs meta language)
visualizations: 44 interactive demos on custom 2D canvas + Plotly charts
Trace-machine (world→access→trace), perception pipeline, 'difference detective' (3 levels: world/channel/processing)
Ladder of six kinds of equality + silent-upgrade detector + isomorphism≠identity coin swap
Transformation triangle / thermometer Olog, overfitting-by-freedom (𝒯 richness), Sellars' web vs foundation
Cover builder + instruments widening c_acc, panorama sheaf (stitching), presheaf-vs-sheaf counterexample, circle/winding-number
Equalizer & pullback (thermometer agreement, radar/video track matching), higher-coherence filler, n-morphism tower, Čech nerve

Model-vs-factbook connectivity, Popper risky predictions, pathology simulator, fitness-vs-truth survival sim
LLM chain (world→author→document→model), model collapse, hallucination two-types, tools as licensed transitions, RLHF, nine-step audit, self-audit, final full diagram
internal_tensions: Circularity: the right side of Tarski's T (the fact in the meta-language) is itself a trace, so correspondence secretly becomes coherence at a higher level; the escape is the limit over INDEPENDENT W-anchored widenings (derived patches do not advance it).
c_acc never reaches c — the model is of the interface, not the thing (Kant).

The framework self-identifies as Pathology 4 (calibrated error) and lists three found residues: the Bradley reading (reconstruction, not exegesis), 𝒯 = space of reasons (analogy, not identity), and the Caramello transfer (imprecisely formulated).
The coherence-vs-correspondence four-field: only (coherent ∧ contact) is a good indicator for 'right', and even that is not a proof.

title: Was ein Weltmodell ist — ganz einfach erklärt
category_reason: A very simple German-language interactive explanation of world models with explicit LLM connections: 'Genau das verwechselt ein LLM: Es hat eine brillante innere Struktur und hält sie dann für Weltwissen.' The file discusses coherence vs. correspondence, the five pathologies of broken models, and truth as a limit — all framed with direct relevance to LLMs.
thesis: A very simple German-language interactive explanation of what a world model is: you never perceive the world directly (only underdetermined traces), a world model stitches local patches into a coherent whole (sheaf condition on overlaps), coherence ≠ truth (coherence is internal consistency, correspondence is external anchor — two different tests), there are five ways a model can be 'broken,' and truth is a regulative ideal (a limit) rather than an attained state. The file explicitly applies this framework to LLMs, which confuse internal coherence with world knowledge.
key_claims: You never perceive the thing itself: between the world W and the trace r you receive, there is always an access function O; the trace is underdetermined — many different (W, O) combinations produce the same r.

A world model consists of many local patches (measurements, perspectives, sensors); it can only call itself a 'whole' if the patches agree where they overlap — this is the sheaf (gluing) condition, or 'Garbenbedingung'.

Coherence (internal consistency) and correspondence (external anchor to the world) are two different tests: a model can be perfectly coherent and still have nothing to do with the world. A theory that can never fail is not an untested theory — it is a coherent fiction.

The error of many systems (including LLMs): they optimize almost exclusively for coherence (self-consistency) and then hold the result to be true. An LLM has a brilliant internal structure and then mistakes it for world knowledge.
There are exactly five basic ways a model can be 'broken' (pathologies), and each requires its own specific remedy; 'the model is wrong' is too coarse — you need to know WHERE it is wrong.

Truth = lim(coherence ∧ correspondence): as you add more independent, world-anchored access points, you approach truth, but you never fully reach it; truth remains a regulative ideal. What you can actually do every day is 'justified acceptance': the model is coherent on your current coverage and has not yet failed at any hard contact point with an independent source.
methods_math: underdetermination: many (world, access) pairs produce the same trace
sheaf condition (gluing): local patches must agree on overlaps
coherence vs. correspondence (Tarski's correspondence theory, Popper's falsifiability)
five pathologies of broken models (didactically condensed)
truth as a limit: lim(coherence ∧ correspondence)
justified acceptance: coherent + no failed contact points
regulative ideal (Kant): truth as a goal, not a state
visualizations: Experiment 1 — Trace Machine: a thing W in the world and an access function O; choose W and O, see the underdetermined trace r; 'Erkennbar?' (Recognizable?) readout
Experiment 2 — Patchwork (Flickenteppich): four patches with overlapping seams; adjust how many patches agree on their shared seams; 'Globales Bild?' (Global picture?) readout; 4/4 agreement = yes
Experiment 3 — Two Tests: sliders for coherence (internal consistency) and correspondence (external anchor); the status readout shows how the model fares on each test independently
Experiment 4 — Pathology Simulator: select one of five error types; read where exactly the model is broken and what heals it
Experiment 5 — Truth Status Calculator: three sliders (coherence, correspondence, hard contact points); compute the model's truth status live
internal_tensions: The file is explicitly 'ganz einfach erklärt' (very simply explained) and 'keine Mathematik-Vorwissen nötig' (no math background needed), which means the sheaf-theoretic and epistemological content is heavily condensed; the 'five pathologies' are 'didactically condensed' (didaktisch verdichtet) and may not correspond cleanly to standard philosophical or mathematical categories.

The LLM application is the most practically relevant but also the least developed: the file states that LLMs confuse coherence with correspondence but does not offer a concrete mechanism for testing an LLM's correspondence (beyond 'hard contact points'), which is the hard problem in AI evaluation.

The 'truth as a limit' framing is philosophically rich (Kant's regulative ideal, Popper's conjectural knowledge) but potentially deflationary: if truth is never attained, what does 'justified acceptance' buy you in practice? The file does not address this operational question.

The file is a 'stark vereinfachte Darstellung' (strongly simplified representation) of a larger work ('From World to Model: Coherent Difference — Teil 4, Kapitel 3'); the simplifications are acknowledged but may lose important qualifications present in the full treatment.

title: Coherent World Models — Interaktive Visualisierung
category_reason: Mathematik FÜR KI: Kohärente Weltmodelle (Traces, Descent/Garben, Tarski-Wahrheit, Korrespondenz vs. Kohärenz) werden explizit auf LLMs angewendet — Halluzination = Kohärenz ohne Korrespondenz, Korrektur über 'Korrespondenz-Brücken' (In-Context, RAG, Tools, formale Verifikation). Klare KI-Kopplung.
thesis: Ein 'kohärentes Weltmodell' ist eine Struktur (𝒞 Kontext-Stellen, 𝒱 Ziel der Repräsentationen, 𝒯 zulässige Übergänge), in der lokale Daten (Traces) per Descent/Garben-Verklebung kohärent sind und ein Tarski-artiger Wahrheitsbegriff Behauptungen in der Welt (W) verankert; angewandt auf LLMs zeigt sich: ein Baseline-LLM hat interne Kohärenz (𝒯) aber keine Korrespondenz (keine Observation-Pfeile O_i: W→R_i), daher halluziniert es außerhalb der Trainingsverteilung — und der Fix ist nicht Skalierung, sondern das Stück-für-Stück Anhängen von 'Korrespondenz-Brücken' (In-Context, RAG, Tools, formale Verifikation).
key_claims: Ein Weltmodell hat drei Zutaten: 𝒞 (Stellen der Kontexte), 𝒱 (Ziel der Repräsentationen), 𝒯 (zulässige Übergänge).

'Kohärenz' = lokale Traces (Daten) verkleben/deszendieren konsistent (garben-ähnlich); 'Korrespondenz' = Behauptungen sind per Observation-Pfeile O_i: W→R_i in der Welt W verankert (Tarski-Wahrheit, Convention T).
Ein Baseline-LLM hat internen 𝒯 (Tokenisierung, Attention, MLP, Logits), aber KEINE Observation-Pfeile — sein Trainingskorpus ist selbst ein transformierter Trace, nicht direkte W-Daten.
Halluzination = Kohärenz ohne Korrespondenz: das LLM ist intern kohärent, aber ohne Korrespondenz-Check erfindet es bei Out-of-Distribution-Anfragen Inhalt.
In-Context Learning fügt einen 'Cover-Patch' (den Prompt) hinzu — einen flachen Observation-Pfeil zum eingefügten Dokument, nicht zu W.
RAG fügt zur Inferenz neue Observation-Pfeile hinzu (erholte Passagen sind näher an W als die Parameter, aber der Retriever braucht Kalibrierung).
Tools/Code-Execution fügen echte W→R_i-Pfeile hinzu (das Programmverhalten ist ein Fakt über die Hardware); formale Verifikation (Coq/Lean) ist der stärkste Tarski-Check (ein typgeprüfter Proof).
'Der einzige Weg': Kohärenz nicht durch Skalierung reparieren — Korrespondenz Stück für Stück anhängen (Context, RAG, Tools, formale Verifikation), jeder Pfeil einzeln lizenziert/auditierbar.
visualizations: SVG: Augmentations-Diagramm (Baseline→Context→RAG→Tools→formal→Full, klickbar)
Canvas: finale Zusammenfassung (die drei Zutaten 𝒞/𝒱/𝒯)
Plotly + MathJax: Formel-Rendering der Weltmodell-Komponenten
SVG-Welt-/LLM-Diagramm (W, R_i, G, Out, Pfeile)
internal_tensions: Das Rahmenwerk (Traces, Descent, Tarski) ist philosophisch/aspirativ; 'Kohärenz' und 'Korrespondenz' werden definiert, aber es gibt kein formales Modell oder eine Messgröße für das 𝒯 oder die O_i eines LLMs.
'Halluzination = Kohärenz ohne Korrespondenz' ist eine nützliche Diagnose, aber die Zuordnung zu echten LLM-Fehlmodi bleibt qualitativ.
Die Augmentations-Leiter (Context→RAG→Tools→formal) ist eine Design-Vorschrift, kein empirisches Ergebnis — der 'einzige Weg' wird behauptet, nicht nachgewiesen.

title: Concept Attractors in LLMs — Interactive Explainer
category_reason: Erklärt, wie LLM-Schichten als kontraktive Abbildungen (IFS) 'Konzept-Attraktoren' bilden und wie man daraus trainingsfrei Konzepte steuern kann (Chytas & Singh 2025, arXiv:2601.11575v1).
thesis: Die Schichten eines LLMs verhalten sich wie kontraktive Abbildungen eines iterierten Funktionensystems (IFS): wiederholte Anwendung zieht Repräsentationen gegen stabile 'Konzept-Attraktoren' im residual stream; weil Attraktoren stabil und lokalisiert sind, lassen sich Konzepte trainingsfrei identifizieren und steuern, indem man gezielt in/aus dem Attraktor-Bassin schiebt.
key_claims: Ein LLM-Layer-Stack ist ein iteriertes Funktionensystem; die Kontraktivität der Abbildungen sorgt (Banach-Fixpunktsatz-Analogie) für die Existenz stabiler Fixpunkte/Attraktoren.
Konzepte (z.B. ein Name, ein Ort, ein Fakt) entsprechen lokalen Attraktoren im hochdimensionalen residual stream — Repräsentationen, die das Konzept kodieren, konvergieren dorthin.
Weil die Attraktoren stabil (kontraktiv) sind, sind sie robust gegen kleine Störungen und damit detektier- und steuerbar.
Trainingsfreie Manipulation: addiert man einen kleinen Vektor in Richtung des Attraktors (oder aus ihm heraus), verschiebt man die Modellantwort — ein mechanistischer 'Steuerhebel'.
Die Idee verknüpft mechanistische Interpretability (Geva, Meng et al.) mit der dynamisch-systemischen Attraktor-Sicht (Chen et al. 2018).
visualizations: Canvas/Plotly (Basins, Trajektorien, Attraktor-Landschaft)
Interaktive Slider (Steuervektor, Layer)
Temml/KaTeX Mathematik
internal_tensions: Die Kontraktivität der LLM-Layer ist empirisch beobachtet, aber nicht formal bewiesen; ein globaler Kontraktionsnachweis über alle Schichten fehlt.
Attraktoren sind heuristisch lokalisiert; Superposition (fast-orthogonale Konzepte) macht die 'Einzigartigkeit' eines Attraktors fragil.
Die trainingsfreie Steuerung funktioniert für klar lokalisierte Konzepte; für verteilte/abstrakte Konzepte bricht die Attraktor-Interpretation zusammen.

title: Concept Attractors in LLMs – Interaktive Erklärung
category_reason: Main subject is how concepts form attractor states in the representation space of large language models — a core topic in LLM interpretability.
thesis: Concepts in LLMs are not stored as fixed locations but emerge as attractor basins in the model's activation space: nearby inputs in semantic space are pulled toward a shared stable state, and the geometry of these basins (depth, width, noise sensitivity) explains both the robustness and the fragility of LLM concept representations.
key_claims: Concepts correspond to attractor regions in LLM hidden-state space where many nearby inputs converge to a common representation.
The depth and shape of an attractor basin determine how robust a concept is to paraphrase, noise, and distributional shift.
Data-generation quality (diversity, coverage) shapes the landscape: sparse training data produces shallow, easily-escaped attractors.
The attractor picture unifies otherwise separate observations — synonym robustness, concept confusion, and hallucination — under one geometric account.
visualizations: canvas attractor-basin animations with particle trajectories
interactive sliders controlling basin shape and noise
internal_tensions: The attractor metaphor is geometrically evocative but the LLM forward pass is a fixed (non-iterative) map, so 'dynamics' here are really iterated applications of the layer map, not a true continuous-time dynamical system.

title: Cover 1965 — Interaktiv: Trennende Flaechen, Kapazitaet 2d, Generalisierung
category_reason: Mathematische Grundlagen des maschinellen Lernens: Kapazitaet linearer Trenner, VC-artige Zaedhung und Generalisierung (Cover 1965).
thesis: Die Anzahl der von N Punkten in d Dimensionen linear trennbaren Aufteilungen ist C(N,d) = 2 * sum_{k=0}^{d-1} binom(N-1, k); die Kapazitaet waechst linear mit 2d (Cover 1965).
key_claims: C(N,d) = 2 * sum_{k=0}^{d-1} binom(N-1, k) zaehlt trennbare Aufteilungen.
Im Grenzfall ist die Kapazitaet 2d — zwei Muster pro Gewicht.
Phi-Trick: gekruemmte Trennflaechen sind Hyperebenen im Merkmalsraum (Vorlaeufer des Kernel-Tricks).
Dualitaet Punkte <-> Hyperebenen (Trotter-Sheridan / polar duality).
Generalisierung beginnt erst ueber der Kapazitaet 2d.
Extrem-/Stuetzvektoren sind die einzigen, die eine Trennung tragen.
XOR ist in 2D nicht linear trennbar.
visualizations: Plotly-Kurve C(N,d) ueber d
N Punkte im Raum + trennende Flaechen
Stuetzvektor-/Extrempunktdemo
XOR-nicht-trennbar-Demo
internal_tensions: Die Formel ist exakt, aber die Uebertragung auf neuronale Netze (hoehere Kapazitaet) bleibt offen.
Der Phi-Trick ist ein Vorlaeufer, kein vollständiger Nachweis fuer moderne Netze.

title: Die Darstellungstheorie Neuronaler Netze — interaktiv
category_reason: Darstellungstheorie (Quiver-Darstellungen, Modulisräume) als exakte algebraische Struktur für neuronale Netze; basiert auf Armenta & Jodoin (arXiv:2007.12213v2).
thesis: Ein neuronales Netz ist eine dünne Quiver-Darstellung mit Aktivierungsfunktionen als modifizierte Morphismen; isomorphe Netze haben dieselbe Funktion (Thm 4.13), ReLU-Netze besitzen positive Skalierungsinvarianz (Cor 4.15), und alle Entscheidungen faktorialisieren durch den Modulisraum (Cor 7.18) — was die algebraische Struktur zum zentralen Werkzeug für Architektur- und Generalisierungsverständnis macht.
key_claims: Ein neuronales Netz ist eine dünne Quiver-Darstellung; isomorphe Netze haben dieselbe Funktion (Armenta & Jodoin, Thm 4.13).
ReLU-Netze besitzen positive Skalierungsinvarianz: Multiplikation aller Gewichte einer Schicht mit c > 0 und Bias mit 0 lässt die Funktion invariant (Cor 4.15).
Teleportation: Flippen von ReLU zu min(0,x) durch negative Skalierung τ < 0 erzeugt ein 'duales' Netz, das die komplementäre Entscheidung trifft.
Max-Pooling bricht die algebraische Struktur: es ist keine lineare Abbildung und damit keine Quiver-Darstellung mehr.
Daten können selbst als Quiver-Darstellungen modelliert werden (Thm 6.4), was eine 'doppelte' Darstellungstheorie ergibt.
Der Modulisraum eines Netzes hat Dimension #Kanten − #versteckte Neuronen (bei generischen Gewichten).
Alle Entscheidungen eines Netzes faktorialisieren durch seinen Modulisraum (Cor 7.18): die Klassifikationsfunktion ist eine Abbildung Moduli → Labels.
Residuelle Blöcke sind algebraisch nicht trivial — sie ändern die Quiver-Struktur und damit den Modulisraum (Refutation von Meng et al.).
visualizations: Canvas 2D (Quiver-Diagramme, Modulisräume)
Plotly (Dimension, Invarianz)
Temml (Formeln)
Interaktive Demos (Skalierung, Teleportation)
internal_tensions: Die Theorie gilt für 'dünne' Quiver-Darstellungen; tiefe, breite Netze mit Skip-Connections sind algebraisch komplexer und die Modulisraum-Formel wird ungenau.
Max-Pooling, Softmax und Sigmoid brechen die Quiver-Struktur — die Theorie deckt nur ReLU-Netze vollständig ab.
Die Refutation von Meng et al. ist algebraisch exakt, aber die praktische Relevanz für die Trainingsdynamik bleibt offen.

title: Holografische Entzerrung bei d=3 Grokking
category_reason: Investigates grokking (delayed generalization) in neural networks using Fourier analysis and Gram-matrix algebra at dimension d=3.
thesis: Squeezes a Fourier-based algorithmic understanding of grokking to the minimal dimension d=3, showing how the Gram matrix of training-set Fourier components controls the phase transition from memorization to generalization, and maps the result back to a 3D visualization.
key_claims: Grokking is a phase transition in the loss landscape triggered by weight decay and continued training past memorization
In d=3 the Gram matrix of the training set's Fourier feature components has eigenvalues that control the critical training step at which generalization begins
The 'holographic' de-squeeze maps the high-dimensional grokking picture to 3D without losing the phase-transition structure
Generalization onset time scales with the condition number of the feature Gram matrix
methods_math: Fourier feature analysis, Gram matrix eigenvalue decomposition, phase transitions in loss landscapes, weight decay regularization
visualizations: 3D phase-transition surface; Gram-matrix eigenvalue evolution plot; loss landscape cross-sections before and after grokking
internal_tensions: Reducing to d=3 necessarily loses the spectral richness of realistic feature spaces; the 'holographic' mapping is an analogy for visualization, not a proven equivalence to the full-dimensional picture.

title: Deep Neural Networks Entmystifiziert
category_reason: Main subject is deep neural networks and deep learning fundamentals

Depth gives an exponential advantage: O(N^L) piecewise-linear regions for L layers vs O(N*L) for a wide shallow net
Deep nets progressively untangle entangled input manifolds - each layer applies a piecewise-linear (ReLU) transformation that simplifies the geometry
Superposition / polysemanticity: many features share neurons; linear probing can extract them; this is why interpretability is hard
Backprop is the chain rule applied to a computation graph; ResNets solve the vanishing-gradient problem via skip connections
Weight matrices of trained nets are smooth in frequency space (low-frequency dominated), which is a signature of generalization
Grokking: a net can memorize a task for many epochs, then abruptly generalize - a phase transition in the loss landscape
Scaling laws: test loss L(N,D) follows a power law L proportional to N^-0.076 in parameters; compute-optimal allocation predicts emergent capabilities
Mechanistic interpretability (circuits): individual features/computations can be isolated; a 'circuit' is a subgraph responsible for a behavior

title: Deep ResNet Visualization — Spiral Entangling
category_reason: German interactive visualization of how deep ResNet architectures progressively untangle a two-spiral classification problem layer by layer, showing the geometric effect of residual blocks on the data manifold. Core deep learning / neural network architecture content.
thesis: A German-language interactive visualization showing a two-arm spiral dataset being progressively separated by a deep ResNet: each residual block applies a small local deformation to the data manifold, and the accumulation of many such deformations over 50+ layers straightens the spirals into linearly separable clusters — with the user able to step through layers and watch the geometry change.
key_claims: A two-arm spiral is one of the hardest 2D classification problems for shallow networks but is easily separable by a sufficiently deep network: each residual block contributes a small 'untangling' step.

Skip connections (h_{l+1} = h_l + F_l(h_l)) ensure that the identity function is always an option for each block, preventing degradation in very deep networks and allowing the gradient to flow unchanged through the skip path.

The data manifold in feature space undergoes a sequence of local diffeomorphisms (one per block); the composition of many small diffeomorphisms can produce a large global deformation (straightening the spiral) that no single small map could achieve.

The 'effective depth' of untangling is greater than the number of layers with nonzero F_l: even blocks that learn F_l ≈ 0 contribute by providing a stable identity path that other blocks can build on.

Visualization of the intermediate feature spaces shows that the spiral does not get 'cut' or 'folded' — it is smoothly reparametrized, consistent with the idea that deep networks learn coordinate changes rather than decision boundaries.
methods_math: ResNet residual block: h_{l+1} = h_l + F_l(h_l)
composition of local diffeomorphisms as global untangling
two-spiral dataset generation and its topological properties
t-SNE / PCA projection of high-dimensional feature spaces to 2D for visualization
gradient flow through skip connections (identity shortcut)
effective rank of the Jacobian of the composed map
visualizations: layer-by-layer animation: 2D projection of the data manifold at each residual block, showing the spiral progressively straightening; user can scrub through all 50+ layers
side-by-side comparison: shallow network (5 layers) vs. deep ResNet (55 layers) on the same spiral, showing the shallow network's failure
feature importance heatmap: which blocks contribute the most 'untangling' (measured by change in manifold curvature)
gradient flow visualization: backpropagation through the skip connections shown as arrows, demonstrating the gradient highway
internal_tensions: The visualization projects high-dimensional feature spaces to 2D, which can make the 'straightening' look more dramatic or more gradual than it actually is in the true dimensionality; the projection method (t-SNE vs. PCA) significantly affects the perceived geometry.

The claim that deep networks 'learn coordinate changes' is an interpretive overlay on the visualization; the actual learned maps are not necessarily diffeomorphisms (ReLU introduces non-invertible kinks).

title: Dense -> ReLU -> Dense Explorer
category_reason: Interactive lab visualizing what a two-layer (affine + ReLU + affine) neural-network block does to input space geometrically.
thesis: A 'Dense -> ReLU -> Dense' layer is a piecewise-linear map of input space: two affine transforms with a ReLU fold in between, so you can watch the same point/grid get stretched, folded (negative -> 0), and re-stretched across 1D-5D.
key_claims: The network function is out = A2 * max(0, A1*x + b1) + b2: two affine maps with one ReLU nonlinearity between them.
ReLU 'folds' the space (negative values -> 0); it is the only nonlinearity in the block.
Each stage (x -> A1x+b1 -> ReLU -> A2z+b2) is rendered as a separate view of the same point/cloud, so the composition is decomposable step by step.
Above 3D the view switches to parallel coordinates, one colored polyline per dimension across the four stages.

internal_tensions: It shows only a single forward pass for one point/one grid; it says nothing about training or expressiveness (no depth-vs-width claim here, unlike the tropical page).

title: Transformer Residual Stream Dynamics
category_reason: Analyzes the residual stream of transformers as a discrete dynamical system using Jacobian eigenvalue spectra and non-normal matrix theory.
thesis: Treats the transformer's residual stream as a discrete-time dynamical system where depth is the time index; the Jacobian eigenvalue spectrum (98% complex-conjugate pairs) and the strong non-normality of the iteration matrix control how information is rotated, amplified transiently, and eventually dissipated through layers.
key_claims: The residual stream evolves as a discrete dynamical system x_{l+1} = x_l + F_l(x_l) with depth as the time index
The Jacobian matrix of the full iteration has 98% complex-conjugate eigenvalue pairs, indicating dominant rotational dynamics
The iteration matrix is strongly non-normal: the spectral radius underestimates transient amplification
Transient growth visible in the pseudospectrum explains how small early-layer perturbations can be amplified before eventual decay
The balance between rotational and dissipative components controls how much signal survives to the output layer
methods_math: Discrete dynamical systems, Jacobian eigenvalue analysis, non-normal matrix theory, pseudospectrum, transient growth
visualizations: Eigenvalue spectrum plot in the complex plane; pseudospectrum heatmap; residual stream trajectory through layers; transient amplification curve
internal_tensions: Linearizing around a single trajectory ignores the high-dimensional nonlinearity of attention; the 'time' interpretation of depth is a metaphor that breaks down when skip connections create non-Markovian dependencies.

title: Dynamischer Residual Stream (Paper 2) — Fernando & Guitchounts 2026
category_reason: German interactive explanation of a 2026 paper (Fernando & Guitchounts) on the dynamics of the residual stream in transformer architectures: how information is written, read, and overwritten across layers, with logit-lens and attention-head visualizations. Core transformer interpretability.
thesis: A German-language interactive explanation of Fernando & Guitchounts (2026): the residual stream in a transformer is a shared 'blackboard' on which attention heads and MLPs sequentially write and overwrite features; the paper's contribution is a formal account of the dynamics (write/read/overwrite operations) and how the logit lens can be understood as projecting the blackboard's content onto the output vocabulary at each intermediate layer.
key_claims: The residual stream is a high-dimensional vector that is never overwritten in place — each sublayer (attention, MLP) adds its output to it, creating an additive 'blackboard' that accumulates information layer by layer.

Attention heads implement a 'read-modify-write' operation: they read a key pattern from the blackboard, attend to the corresponding value positions, and write the result back — this is the fundamental unit of information flow in the transformer.

The logit lens (interpreting the residual stream at layer ℓ as if it were the final output) works because the residual stream at each layer already contains a partial 'draft answer'; the dynamics paper formalizes when this draft is reliable vs. when later layers substantially revise it.

Overwrite dynamics: later attention heads can cancel or suppress features written by earlier heads, creating a 'competing writers' picture; the paper characterizes the conditions under which a feature survives to the final layer.

The MLP sublayers act as 'nonlinear feature extractors' that read the current blackboard state and write back a transformed version, enabling composition of features that attention alone cannot express.
methods_math: residual stream as additive accumulator: h^ℓ = h^ℓ⁻¹ + f_ℓ(h^ℓ⁻¹)
attention as a keyed read operation: Attention(Q,K,V) = softmax(QKᵀ/√d)V
logit lens: W_U h^ℓ as an intermediate prediction
MLP as nonlinear feature map: MLP(h) = W₂ ReLU(W₁ h + b₁) + b₂
visualizations: animated residual stream as a horizontal 'blackboard' with layers as columns; attention heads and MLPs shown as arrows writing/erasing features
logit lens heatmap: rows are layers, columns are vocabulary tokens, color = logit value; user can scrub through layers to watch the 'draft answer' evolve
individual attention head animation: query/key/value vectors shown as arrows in 2D projection, with the attention pattern as a matrix
overwrite dynamics: two competing heads writing to the same feature slot, with a slider controlling the relative 'write strength' to show cancellation
internal_tensions: The 'blackboard' metaphor suggests a single shared space, but in practice the residual stream is high-dimensional and different heads attend to different subspaces; the 2D/3D projections in the visualizations can mislead about the true geometry.
The paper's formal account of write/read/overwrite is presented as settled, but the boundary between 'writing' and 'overwriting' a feature is somewhat arbitrary — depends on the chosen feature basis.

title: Origami in N Dimensions – Dense–ReLU–Dense Network
category_reason: Geometrie/Expressivität neuronaler Netze: ein 2→3→1 Dense-ReLU-Dense-Netz faltet den Eingaberaum wie Origami (Keup & Helias 2022, Lewandowski 2025); Montúfar-Expressivitätsgrenzen. Klarer KI-Bezug.
thesis: Ein schmales Dense-ReLU-Dense-Netz (2→3→1) 'faltet' den Eingaberaum stückweise-linear wie Origami: die versteckte Schicht erzeugt durch die ReLU-Grenzebenen eine Regionenaufteilung, deren Faltungszahl die Expressivität steuert (Montúfar), und so einfache Muster (z.B. Ei vs. Ring) in lineartrennbare Stücke zerlegt.
key_claims: Ein 2→3→1-Netz (Eingang 2D, 3 ReLU-Neuronen, 1D-Ausgang) faltet die Ebene stückweise-linear; die Faltlinien sind die ReLU-Nullstellen der versteckten Schicht.
Jede ReLU-Neuron teilt den Raum in eine 'an' und eine 'aus'-Hälfte; die Überlappung der 3 Neuronen erzeugt bis zu 2³ Kombinationen (Regionen).
Die Hamming-Kubus-Analogie: jede Region entspricht einem Bitmuster der aktivierten Neuronen; ein 'Bit-Flip-Walk' zeigt, wie man von Region zu Region wandert.
Montúfars Expressivitätsgrenzen: die Anzahl der linearen Regionen wächst mit der Anzahl der Neuronen – mehr Neuronen = komplexere Faltschläge.
Die Klassifikation 'Ei' vs. 'Ring' gelingt, weil die Faltung die nicht-konvexen Muster in lineartrennbare Stücke zerlegt.
Keup & Helias (2022) bzw. Lewandowski (2025) formalisieren diese 'Space-Folding'-Sicht auf ReLU-Netze.
visualizations: Three.js: 3D versteckte Schicht (Faltung im Raum)
2D: Faltlinien / Regionenaufteilung der Ebene
Hamming-Kubus (8 Bitmuster)
Bit-Flip-Walk (Region-zu-Region-Navigation)
Temml-Formel-Rendering
internal_tensions: 2→3→1 ist didaktisch, aber die Regionenzahl (≤8) ist winzig gegenüber realen Netzen (10⁴+) – der Sprung zur Skalierung wird nur angedeutet.
Die Montúfar-Schranke (2^n) ist eine Obergrenze; die tatsächlich erreichte Regionenzahl hängt von der generischen Lage der Gewichte ab und wird nicht berechnet.
Die 'Origami'-Metapher ist anschaulich, aber sie kaschiert, dass nicht jede Faltung jede Zielfunktion erreicht – Expressivität ≠ Lernbarkeit.

title: Energy-Based Learning — Interaktive Reise durch LeCun et al. 2006
category_reason: Maschinelles Lernen: Energie-basierte Modelle (LeCun et al. 2006, 'A Tutorial on Energy-Based Learning') — Energie-Landschaften, Minimization, Contrastive Divergence, MRF/Boltzmann. Klare KI-Kopplung.
thesis: Energie-basierte Modelle (EBM) definieren eine skalare Energie E(x[, y]) über Eingaben (und optionalen Labels): gültige/daten-nahe Konfigurationen haben niedrige Energie, ungültige hohe. Lernen formt die Energie-Landschaft so, dass echte Daten in Täler fallen und korrupte Daten auf Berge; Inferenz ist Energiminimierung. LeCun et al. (2006) stellen EBMs als allgemeines, diskriminative und generative Sichtweisen vereinigendes Rahmenwerk dar (Klassifikation, Rekonstruktion, strukturierte Vorhersage).
key_claims: Ein EBM ordnet jeder Konfiguration eine skalare Energie E(x, y) zu; das Modell 'erklärt' Daten, indem es echte Daten niedrig-energetisch macht.
Training drückt die Energie echter Daten herunter und die Energie korrupter/abwesender Daten hoch (Contrastive Divergence / Noise Contrastive Estimation).
Inferenz ist Energiminimierung: Um das beste Label y für Eingabe x zu finden, minimiert man E(x, y) über y.
EBMs verallgemeinern sowohl den generativen (modellierte gemeinsame Verteilung) als auch den diskriminativen (bedingte Verteilung) Blick.
Strukturierte Vorhersage: E(x, y) über strukturierte y (Sequenzen, Graphen, Segmentierungen) — die Energie kodiert Kompatibilitäts-Constraints.
Verbindung zu Markov-Zufallsfeldern, Boltzmann-Maschinen und Hopfield-Netzen (in Sonderfällen Energie = −log Wahrscheinlichkeit).
visualizations: Plotly: 2D Energie-Landschaft (Täler/Berge), vor/nach Training
Plotly: Energiewerte echter vs. korrupter Daten (Gap)
Schematische Inferenz (Minimierung über y)
Verbindungsdigramm EBM ↔ MRF ↔ Boltzmann ↔ Hopfield
internal_tensions: Das Training von EBMs ist rechnerisch schwer (Partitionssummen unzugänglich); Contrastive Divergence ist eine Approximation, keine exakte Schätzung.
Die 2D 'Energie-Landschaft' ist schematisch; reale EBM-Landschaften sind hochdimensional und nicht direkt darstellbar.
Die Einheit mit generativen/diskriminativen Modellen wird behauptet, aber die Bedingungen (z.B. Existenz einer normalisierenden Verteilung) werden nur angerissen.

title: How a Neural Network Learns Addition (mod P) - The 'Fourier Multiplication' Algorithm
category_reason: It is a step-by-step interactive explainer of how a neural network computes modular addition via Fourier features / circle embeddings (the 'Fourier Multiplication Algorithm').
thesis: A 7-step interactive explanation of how a neural network learns modular addition (a+b mod P): it embeds each number as a point on circles at several frequencies, adds by rotating (multiplying) those circle positions, and reads the answer by constructive wave interference (a score that peaks exactly at a+b mod P).
key_claims: Modular addition is cast as 'clock math' on a P-hour clock: numbers live on a circle and adding means moving around the circle, wrapping to 0 once the sum reaches P.
The network encodes a number a at frequency k as a point on the unit circle at angle 2*pi*k*a/P (x = cos, y = sin) — a Fourier feature / wave encoding of a discrete value.

Addition is done by combining rotations via the angle-addition formula cos(a+b) = cos(a)cos(b) - sin(a)sin(b): multiplying the wave values of a and b rotates the combined position to angle(a+b mod P) — 'it rotates, without adding'.

The answer is read by scoring each candidate c with score(c) = sum_k cos(2*pi*k*(a+b-c)/P), which is maximal exactly at c = a+b mod P because the waves line up (constructive interference) and cancel for wrong c (destructive interference); more frequencies sharpen the peak.
The network uses several frequencies at once (e.g. k = 14, 35, 41, 42, 52 for P = 113), each giving a different 'view' of the numbers, and the summed score selects the answer.
methods_math: modular arithmetic (Z/PZ) as the cyclic/clock group
Fourier feature map / trigonometric embedding x -> (cos(2 pi k x / P), sin(2 pi k x / P)) at multiple frequencies
the angle-addition formula cos(a+b) = cos a cos b - sin a sin b (rotation/complex-multiplication in the circle group)
constructive/destructive wave interference as the scoring function sum_k cos(2 pi k (a+b-c)/P)
visualizations: a 7-step tabbed walkthrough (0 Problem, 1 Clock, 2 Waves, 3 Numbers->Circles, 4 Combining Waves, 5 Reading the Answer, 6 Full Algorithm) with a step navigation bar
Step 0: an interactive clock/number-line wrap demo (sliders P, a, b) showing where the sum lands and a 'WRAPS!' jump arrow
Step 1: numbers placed on a circle with a dashed arc showing 'move +b steps' from a to a+b mod P
Step 2: a cosine wave plot with frequency and position sliders reading off the wave height
Step 3: a unit-circle scatter of all numbers at a chosen frequency, with one highlighted number and its (cos, sin) coordinates and angle
Step 4: an angle-addition diagram (red angle a + green angle b = gold angle a+b) with the cos(a+b) identity displayed
Step 5: a bar chart of the interference score for every candidate answer, the correct bar highlighted
Step 6: a full animated pipeline (place on circles -> combine rotations -> score -> pick) driven by a 6-phase Animate / Reset sequence
internal_tensions: Titled a 'neural network' but no trained network, gradients, or layers are ever shown — it reconstructs the algorithm by hand, so it explains the *function* the net implements rather than how it *learns* it (no actual grokking or learning dynamics).

It presents the 'Fourier Multiplication' as the discovered mechanism, but real addition networks do not necessarily implement a clean per-frequency rotation; this is a pedagogical idealization that may overstate the fidelity of actual trained weights.

The scoring/interference picture is essentially a Fourier-basis / matched-filter view; it does not explain why a network would pick these particular frequencies, nor what changes for composite vs prime P.

title: Fourier Projection: Extracting Circles from Skewed Embedding Spaces
category_reason: Directly about transformer embedding spaces and the grokking paper: Fourier projection as the mechanism by which the model reads out addition
thesis: In the grokking circuit, the embedding space contains circles that are 'skewed' — rotated across multiple dimensions so no single 2D coordinate slice reveals them. The Discrete Fourier Transform provides the orthogonal basis (sin/cos at each frequency) that 'un-skews' these circles: projecting onto the Fourier basis at frequency k extracts the clean 2D circular structure, and the readout uses constructive interference of multiple cosine waves to peak at c = a+b mod P.
key_claims: Circles in embedding space are 'skewed': they exist in a rotated orientation across multiple dimensions, not aligned with any coordinate plane
Axis-aligned projections (XY, XZ, YZ) distort the circle into ellipses — the periodic structure is lost
The DFT provides an orthogonal basis of sinusoidal functions; projecting data onto this basis extracts the circular component at each frequency
The Fourier coefficients at frequency k (cosine and sine) define a 2D plane in which the circle at that frequency lives
The grokking algorithm: embed a as rotation by a, attend to b to compose rotations (trig identity), read out via cos(w_k(a+b-c)) which peaks at c = a+b mod P
Multiple key frequencies superimpose: their cosine waves constructively interfere at the correct answer and destructively interfere elsewhere

axis_aligned_slices
fourier_spectrum_bars
before_after_projection

interference_wave_overlay
internal_tensions: The 3D visualization is a pedagogical simplification: real transformer embeddings are 64+ dimensional, not 3D
The 'skewed circle' analogy is illustrative but the actual embedding is a superposition of multiple frequency circles, not a single circle
The Fourier projection works cleanly for pure sinusoids; real embeddings have noise and cross-frequency contamination

title: Garben im Transformer — Interaktiver Begleiter
category_reason: Anwendung der Garben-/Kohomologietheorie auf Transformer-Representationen (NeurIPS 2026, Bryce Grant & Peng Wang, Case Western Reserve University): Zerlegung des Aktivierungsraums in Inhalt (H^0) vs Formulierung (H^1) ueber einen Garben-Laplace-Operator.
thesis: Der Repräsentationsraum eines Transformer-Abstraktionskopfs laesst sich ueber einen Garben-Laplace-Operator auf einem Paraphrased-Graphen in 'Bedeutung' (H^0-Content) und 'Formulierung' (H^1-Einfluss) zerlegen; der Content liegt im Kern der Paardifferenz-Kovarianz, ist robust gegen die Wahl des Projektionsoperators P (PCA-P 81,6 %, Random-P 74,2 %, Identity-P 77,5 %), schlaegt alle label-freien Baselines um +9 bis +36 Prozentpunkte und uebertraegt sich cross-lingual (EN-FR).
key_claims: Ein Garben-Laplace-Operator auf einem Paraphrased-Graphen zerlegt den Aktivierungsraum in H^0 (Content) und H^1 (Formulierungs-Einfluss).
Der Content liegt im Kern der Paardifferenz-Kovarianz — die Kernwahl ist der aktive Wirkmechanismus.
Content ist P-robust: PCA-P 81,6 %, Identity-P 77,5 %, Random-P 74,2 % — die Zerlegung haengt nicht an einem speziellen P.
H^0 schlaegt alle label-freien Baselines um +9 bis +36 pp und liegt nur ~2 pp unter der label-benoetigenden Obergrenze (LDA, NCA).
Die Methode uebertraegt sich cross-lingual (EN-FR) ohne Neu-Training.
