title: Eine Theorie der Generalisierung im Deep Learning — Interaktiv
category_reason: Mathematische Generalisierungstheorie fuer ueberparametrisierte neuronale Netze: erklaert, warum ueberparametrisierte Netze trotzdem generalisieren, ueber Output-Raum-Dynamik, Tangentenkern und Signal/Reservoir-Zerlegung (Litman & Guo, arXiv 2605.01172).
thesis: Generalisierung in ueberparametrisierten Netzen ist kein Zufall, sondern folgt aus der Output-Raum-Dynamik: ein einheitlicher spectraler Filter M (getrieben vom Tangentenkern K = J J^T und der kumulativen Dissipation W) erklmaert Grokking, Double Descent, implizite Bias und benigne Ueberanpassung gleichzeitig; ein Signal-Kanal trennt sich vom prinzipiell unsichtbaren Reservoir, und ein SNR-Tor mu^2 > sigma^2/(b-1) liefert den einzeiligen Adam-Fix.
key_claims: Die Tangentengradienten bilden den Tangentenkern K = J J^T, der die Output-Dynamik des Trainings steuert.
Die kumulative Dissipation W zerlegt die Update-Richtung in einen Signal-Kanal und einen Rest.
Reservoir-Unsichtbarkeit: G * P_res = 0 — das Reservoir beeinflusst den Test-Fehler nicht.
Drift skaliert mit T, Diffusion mit sqrt(T); diese Trennung erklmaert die zeitliche Lage des Grokking-Fensters.
Eine Four-Zellen-Fehlerzerlegung (train/test x signal/reservoir) macht den Uebertrag von train nach test sichtbar.
Ein einziger spectraler Filter M erklmaert Grokking, Double Descent, implizite Bias und benigne Ueberanpassung in einem Zug.
Das SNR-Tor mu^2 > sigma^2/(b-1) ist die einzeilige Adam-Korrektur, um das Rauschen unter dem Signal zu halten.
visualizations: Plotly + Canvas-Animationen des Trainingslaufs
Temml-Formeln fuer K, W und den Filter M
Interaktive Drift/Diffusion-Regler
Four-Zellen-Heatmap (train/test x signal/reservoir)
Spectraler-Filter-Kurve M ueber den Eigenwerten
SNR-Tor-Demo (mu^2 gegen sigma^2/(b-1))
internal_tensions: Die Theorie ist elegant und einheitlich, aber die Drift/Diffusion-Skalierung (T vs sqrt(T)) gilt fuer ideale Trajektorien und braucht Empirie an realen Netzen.
Das Reservoir ist zwar test-unsichtbar, veraendert aber den Trainingsverlauf — seine praktische Rolle bleibt interpretativ.
Der einzeilige Adam-Fix ist ein klarer Handlungsansatz, setzt aber genaue Schmaetzung von Signal- und Rauschen-Lautstaerke voraus.

title: Warum Auswendiglernen nicht schadet — ganz einfach erklärt
category_reason: Theorie der Generalisierung überparametrisierter neuronaler Netze (benignes Overfitting, Grokking, double descent) inkl. praktischem SNR-Update-Gate
thesis: Eine Theorie der Generalisierung im Deep Learning: Der Ausgaberaum spaltet sich in einen Signalkanal (Bildraum kumulativer Erreichbarkeit W) und ein Reservoir (Kern von W), in dem auswendig gelerntes Rauschen für jede Testfrage unsichtbar 'geparkt' wird; im Signalkanal trennt SGD kohärente Drift (∝T) von Rausch-Diffusion (∝√T), was benignes Overfitting, Double Descent, Implicit Bias und Grokking vereinigt und zu einem einzeiligen SNR-Gate (Update nur wenn Signal² > Rausch²/(b−1)) führt
key_claims: Schau auf die Ausgaben des Netzes (eine pro Trainingsbeispiel), nicht auf die Milliarden Gewichte; der Ausgaberaum spaltet in zwei senkrechte 'Zimmer': Signalkanal (wo Training Fehler abbaute → im Test sichtbar) und Reservoir (wo Training nicht hinkam → für jede Testfrage unsichtbar)

Das Reservoir wird über W, die über die gesamte Trainingslaufzeit summierte 'kumulative Erreichbarkeit', definiert; große W = Signalkanal, W=0 = Reservoir; bei echten Netzen fällt W's Spektrum über viele Größenordnungen ab, also ist das Reservoir riesig und der Signalkanal winzig
Im Signalkanal wächst kohärentes Signal wie T (geradeaus), während Rauschen wie √T random-walkt (Zickzack); langes Training lässt das Signal das Rauschen überholen

Die vier bekannten Mysterien sind derselbe Mechanismus: benignes Overfitting (Rauschen liegt physisch im Reservoir), Double Descent (neue Kapazität hilft nur, wenn die neue Richtung mehr Signal als Rauschen bringt), Implicit Bias (SGD passt 'leichte' Richtungen zuerst an), Grokking (Signal wandert aus dem Reservoir in den Signalkanal; Testgenauigkeit springt beim Überholen)

Praktischer Bonus: pro-Parameter-Gate — Parameter k aktualisieren nur wenn Signal²(k) > Rausch²(k)/(b−1); eine Zeile in AdamW (ein zusätzlicher Vektor), kein Validierungsdatensatz nötig; in 5 Domänen getestet (PINNs, Grokking, DPO-Finetuning, INR-Bildkodierung, Lorenz)

Die Theorie verlangt ein zweimal differenzierbares Netz und einen konvexen Ausgangsverlust; die exakte Kopplung gilt nur für quadratischen Verlust (kleiner Rest, der mit Glattheit/Datendichte schrumpft); sie vermeidet 'Breite→∞', eingefrorene Kerne, Asymptotik und 'mit hoher Wahrscheinlichkeit'
visualizations: 3 interaktive Canvas-Demos: (1) Reservoir-Unsichtbarkeit (Restfehler- + Testpunkt-Vektoren drehen, zeigt Testbewegung=0 wenn Fehler im Reservoir liegt), (2) T-vs-√T Signal-vs-Rauschen-Rennen mit Random Walks, (3) SNR-Gate-Streu Diagramm (Parameter nach Pass/Block gefärbt vs. Schwelle 1/(b−1))
Live-Anzeigen (Trainingsfehler, Testbewegung, Signal:Rauschen, Pass/Block-Anteil)
internal_tensions: 'Sehr einfache' Popularisierung eines arXiv-Preprints (2605.01172 — eine future-dated ID, möglicherweise fehlerhaft/unkontrollierbar); die Kernaussage 'eine Zeile Code verbessert Training in 5 Experimenten' ist stark und nicht unabhängig verifizierbar
Die 'Honesty Corner' gibt zu, dass exakte Ergebnisse quadratischen Verlust voraussetzen; das eine-Parameter-Gate setzt unabhängige Batches voraus (bei Multi-Epochen bleibt ein Restterm)

title: Die Geometrie der Wahrheit - Interaktiv
category_reason: Main subject is LLM interpretability: finding a linear 'truth direction' in LLM activations and testing it causally
thesis: German interactive walkthrough of Marks & Tegmark's 'The Geometry of Truth' (COLM 2024, arXiv:2310.06824): LLMs represent truth/falsehood of simple factual statements as a linear direction in activation space; the direction is found unsupervised (PCA), generalizes across structurally and topically diverse datasets (transfer), and is causally effective (adding theta to a false statement's activation makes the model output TRUE); the direction emerges with scale (7B->13B->70B).
key_claims: LLMs can output falsehoods while 'knowing' better (hallucination, sycophancy, deliberate deception); the inner state may disagree with the output
A concept (e.g., 'truth') is represented as a direction theta in high-dimensional activation space, not a single neuron; a linear probe is just a dot product theta*x with sign read-off
The key activation is over the sentence-ending punctuation mark (the period), in middle layers (Layer 15 for 13B) - this is where the whole sentence is summarized
PCA (unsupervised, label-free) finds the truth direction as PC1: the direction of maximum variance separates true from false statements

The truth direction generalizes: a probe trained on cities transfers to Spanish vocabulary, number comparisons, etc. (out-of-distribution); training on cities+neg_cities improves transfer (opposites cancel the spurious 'association' feature)

Causal intervention (the strongest evidence): adding theta to a false statement's activation makes the model output TRUE on a dataset the probe never saw; Mass-Mean outperforms LR and CCS in 7/8 conditions
The likely dataset (no truth content, only plausibility) shows truth != plausibility: a plausibility probe is perfect on sp_en_trans (r=0.95) but below chance on negated datasets (r=-0.63, -0.89)

Negation causes axis rotation across layers: cities and neg_cities axes are antipodal in early layers, orthogonal in middle layers, aligned in later layers - explained by two competing features (truth f+ and association f-)
Larger models have more abstract, unified representations: 7B groups by surface features, 13B separates cleanly but sometimes in opposite directions, 70B merges into one common direction

Mass-Mean probing (difference of class means, no optimization) is competitive with logistic regression and CCS for classification, and superior for causal intervention; the inverse-Sigma correction (Fisher LDA) handles correlated features

internal_tensions: The point clouds are explicitly synthetic illustrations (stated in the footer), not real LLaMA activations - the qualitative structures match the paper but the exact numbers are approximate
The paper only tests simple, unambiguous factual statements; it cannot distinguish 'true' from 'generally believed', 'undisputed', or 'verifiable' - the scoping is acknowledged but limits the claim
Only the LLaMA-2 family was studied; whether the truth direction is architecture-specific or universal is open
Mass-Mean's superiority in causal intervention (7/8 conditions) is unexplained - the authors say 'we don't know'; the inverse-Sigma correction helps but does not fully account for the gap
The likely dataset result (plausibility != truth) is strong but relies on the assumption that the likely dataset captures plausibility cleanly; the 100.-most-likely token choice is a heuristic

title: Die Geometrie neuronaler Populationen — interaktiv erklärt
category_reason: Geometrie neuronaler Populationen und optimales Kodieren in neuronalen Netzen und im Gehirn (Wakhloo, Slatton & Chung 2024, arXiv:2402.16770): drei geometrische Größen (Korrelation c, Ausrichtung a, Partizipationsverhältnis PR) bestimmen den Generalisierungsfehler eines linearen Lesers.
thesis: Eine gute neuronale Repräsentation passt zur verborgenen Struktur der Welt — empfindlich genug, sauber getrennt und so weit gestreut, wie es die Erfahrung rechtfertigt; drei geometrische Kennzahlen der Population (Korrelation c, Ausrichtung a, Partizipationsverhältnis PR) bestimmen den Generalisierungsfehler eines linearen Lesers, mit einem irreduziblen Fehler-Boden und einem optimalen entflochtenen Code.
key_claims: Der Generalisierungsfehler eines linearen Lesers hängt nur von drei geometrischen Größen der Populations-Verteilung ab: mittlerer Korrelation c zwischen Neuronen, Ausrichtung a (Kodierungsrichtung vs. Aufgabenrichtung) und Partizipationsverhältnis PR (wirksame Dimension).
Es gibt einen irreduziblen Fehler: selbst die beste Population kann nur so gut sein, wie die verborgene (latente) Struktur der Aufgabe es erlaubt.
Der optimale Code ist entflochten: Neuronen sollten die latente Struktur entflechten (eine Richtung pro latenter Faktor) und dabei redundanten Korrelationen vermeiden.
ReLU wirkt als Rauschfilter: durch die Nichtlinearität wird Rauschen unterdrückt und die effektive Kodierungsrichtung verbessert.
Bestätigung am Affenhirn: Populationen in V4/IT zeigen genau diese geometrische Signatur (niedrige Korrelation, gute Ausrichtung, angemessenes PR).
Partizipationsverhältnis PR als Maß für die effektive Dimension: kleines PR = nur wenige Neuronen tragen die Information (sparsam), großes PR = breit verteilt.
visualizations: Plotly: Generalisierungsfehler vs. (c, a, PR)
three.js: 3D-Punktewolke der Population
2D-Canvas: Neuronen-Vektoren und Kodierungsrichtung
Interaktive Labore (Regler für c, a, PR, ReLU-Schalter)
internal_tensions: Das Modell ist lineares Lesen auf top-Gaußschen Populationen; reale Netze sind nichtlinear und trainiert — die Übertragbarkeit ist eine Analogie, kein bewiesener Mechanismus.
Die optimale Geometrie ist aufgabenabhängig (hängt von der latenten Struktur ab); ohne diese Struktur ist optimal undefiniert.
Die Affendaten sind korrilierend (Beobachtung); die Kausalrichtung Geometrie → Generalisierung bleibt hypothetisch.

title: Gradient Flow — Interaktive Visualisierung
category_reason: An interactive visualization of forward pass, loss computation, and backpropagation in a neural network. The entire subject is the training dynamics of a neural network, which is core ML.
thesis: An interactive German-language visualization of gradient flow through a neural network: the user watches forward-pass activations (green) and backward-pass gradients (red) propagate through the network in real time, with controls for learning rate, animation speed, target output, and residual connections; edge thickness encodes |weight| and edge glow encodes |update|.
key_claims: The forward pass propagates activations from input to output; each edge's thickness is proportional to the absolute value of its weight.
The backward pass (backpropagation) propagates gradients from the loss back to the input; each edge's glow intensity is proportional to the magnitude of the weight update.
Residual (skip) connections are shown as zigzag edges: they carry the identity signal, allowing gradients to flow directly through the network without degradation.
The learning rate controls the step size of each weight update; too large causes oscillation, too small causes slow convergence.
The loss is computed at the output layer and drives the entire backward pass; the gradient magnitude |∇| is displayed alongside the epoch and loss value.
The user can step through the animation frame-by-frame ('Step') or run it continuously ('Play'), and can reset or generate a new random input to observe different training trajectories.
methods_math: backpropagation (chain rule applied layer by layer)
gradient descent (weight update: w ← w - lr · ∂L/∂w)
residual connections (identity skip paths for gradient flow)
loss function (e.g., MSE) at the output
visualizations: Canvas-based neural network diagram: nodes (neurons) connected by edges; forward signal (green) flows left-to-right, backward signal (red) flows right-to-left
Edge encoding: thickness = |weight|, glow = |update|, zigzag style = residual (identity) connection
Controls: learning rate slider, speed slider, target-y input, residual toggle
Transportation controls: Play / Step / Reset / New Input buttons
Live readout: epoch counter, loss value, gradient magnitude |∇|
Legend panel explaining the color and edge encodings
internal_tensions: The visualization is 2D and shows a small network; the true power of backpropagation (and its challenges: vanishing/exploding gradients, saddle points) does not appear at this scale.
The learning rate is a single global parameter; in practice, modern optimizers (Adam, LAMB) use per-parameter adaptive learning rates, which this visualization does not capture.

The residual connection is shown as a binary toggle; in real networks (ResNet, transformer), residual connections are integral to every block, and their effect on the gradient flow is more subtle than 'identity path'.

The file is a visualization, not an explanation: it shows the flow but does not derive the chain rule or explain why the gradient points in the direction of steepest descent; the 'Aha' is visual, not conceptual.

title: Grid Walker: Wie ein neuronales Netz eine Welt 'sieht'
category_reason: It is a German interactive walkthrough of Brenner, Knoesche & Scherf (2026) on how decoder-only transformers and RNNs, trained only to predict the next step of a grid walker, spontaneously form a linear world-state representation extracted by self-attention.
thesis: A German 10-chapter interactive walkthrough of Brenner, Knoesche & Scherf (2026): using a fully solvable 'grid walker' prediction task (a random walker that must reach a target in exactly T steps) as a miniature world whose predictive distribution is exactly computable, the paper shows that transformer first-attention layers universally encode the world-state [x_t/t, y_t/t, log t] (readable by linear probes and CKA) while the MLPs then specialize to the variant's 'effective field' q_t — and that this clean world/task separation is an architectural bias of self-attention, not a necessity of the prediction task (RNNs solve it too but without the clean separation).
key_claims: The setup is a random walker on a 2D grid making moves L/R/U/D that must reach a target in exactly T steps; three variants — Walker L (return to start), Walker D (two possible targets, must infer which), Walker O (obstacles break symmetry) — give a world whose full predictive structure is exactly computable.

Fair sampling uses Doob's h-transform / Bayes: Pr(delta | x, tau) = H(tau-1, x+delta) / H(tau, x), where H(tau, z) is the number of valid length-tau paths from z to the target (dead-ends get probability 0).

The next-step distribution decomposes in diagonal coordinates u = x+y, v = x-y into an 'effective field' q = (q_u, q_v, q_uv): q_uv = 0 for Walker L (2D field), q_uv != 0 for Walker D (Bayesian uncertainty over which target), and all three components live for Walker O.

The core mechanistic finding: the first attention head does three things — (A) uniform attention over all past positions, (B) additive value-writes (each token contributes a token-code plus a position-code), (C) token-codes arranged so their average equals the average displacement, i.e. <token-code> = A * (x_t/t) — so one round of uniform averaging computes the world's coordinate system x_t/t plus a log t time code.

Two-stage layer pipeline: after attention the activation is ~ [x_t/t, y_t/t, log t] (a world coordinate system, invariant across variants, cross-variant CKA 0.95-0.97); after MLP -> LN-final it becomes q_t (the effective field, specialized to the variant, cross-variant CKA drops sharply).

The net represents *more* than the loss requires (the full world-state, not just the next step): this is not poor compression but an architectural bias — self-attention makes this rich representation cheap.

RNN comparison: LSTMs and GRUs reach the same Bayes-optimal prediction quality (they must track the world-state too), but the world-state is *mixed* with other variance — no separate 'world layer' — so the world/task separation is architecture-dependent, a 'Rashomon effect'.
methods_math: Doob h-transform / conditional bridge random walk (Pr(delta|x,tau) = H(tau-1,x+delta)/H(tau,x))
path counting H(tau, z -> p) via dynamic programming / reverse BFS, with parity and reachability constraints
diagonal coordinates u = x+y, v = x-y and the log-probability decomposition -q_u du - q_v dv - q_uv du dv (effective field q in R^3)
linear probes in two directions (decode a -> y vs encode y -> a), read off as R^2
Centered Kernel Alignment (CKA), invariant to rotation and scaling
attention mechanics: uniform attention, additive value-writes, and token-codes whose mean equals x_t/t
visualizations: a 10-chapter sectioned page with a sticky TOC and sliders/click controls throughout
Chapter 2: an interactive grid-walker canvas — pick variant (L/D/O) and horizon T, sample random valid paths, and play them back step by step
Chapter 3: a Bayes / h-transform panel — a heatmap of cells reachable in tau steps (intensity = path count) plus arrow/probability bars for the four next-step probabilities, all slider-driven
Chapter 4: a vector-field canvas of the effective field q over the grid (drift q_u, q_v arrows, or a q_uv coupling heatmap), switching between Walker L and Walker D

Chapters 5/6: a clickable attention-matrix canvas (uniform / recent / decay modes) with a per-query contribution bar, plus a 'compass' canvas where clicking L/R/U/D builds a sequence and shows the mean token-code equals x_t/t
Chapter 7: a simulated linear-probe lab (noise and extra-dimension sliders -> R^2) and a CKA lab (rotation leaves CKA unchanged; only noise lowers it)

Chapter 8: a grouped Plotly bar chart of decode/encode R^2 for z_t vs q_t across layer hooks (pre / post-attn / post-MLP / LN-final) and a Plotly heatmap of the cross-variant CKA matrix (post-attn vs post-MLP)
Chapter 9: a Plotly grouped bar chart comparing Transformer vs RNN encoding-R^2 for the world-state across the three walkers
internal_tensions: The 'world-state is represented more than the loss requires' claim is a strong interpretability claim; the piece presents the linear-probe/CKA evidence as decisive, but high probe R^2 can coexist with the information being non-causal, and the 'cheapness' argument for attention is asserted rather than proven.

The two-stage story (attention = universal world-state, MLP = variant-specialized) is clean, but the cross-variant CKA numbers are quoted from the paper and the RNN 'no clean separation' is shown via a small chart; the mechanistic decomposition (uniform attention + additive value-writes) is stated, not derived.

title: Grokking Experiments — What They Actually Did
category_reason: It is an English interactive breakdown of the deep-learning 'grokking' experiments (Power et al., 2021) in which a tiny transformer learns binary operation tables and later generalizes; it is squarely about neural-network training and generalization.
thesis: An interactive English reconstruction of exactly what Power et al. (2021), 'Grokking: Generalization Beyond Overfitting on Small Algorithmic Datasets', experimented with: a tiny overparameterized transformer (~400K params) learns binary operation tables over abstract symbols, and the piece walks through seven experiments to show which operations generalize, what makes generalization happen (weight decay + noise), the dramatic memorization-then-grokking gap (double descent), robustness to wrong labels, the geometric structure learned inside (t-SNE of embeddings), and a hidden isomorphism between different operations.
key_claims: The setup: a decoder-only transformer (2 layers, width 128, 4 heads, ~400K non-embedding params) trained on 5 tokens <a> <op> <b> = <c> with loss only on the answer token c, where each element is an ABSTRACT SYMBOL (no numeric structure given), AdamW lr=1e-3 weight-decay=1, batch 512, 10^5-step budget — massively overparameterized, so classical theory predicts mere memorization.

Experiment 1 (which operations generalize): symmetric operations (x+y, x^2+y^2) need less data than asymmetric ones (x-y, x/y); x+y mod (p-1) and x*y mod p are mathematically equivalent via primitive roots and indeed show identical curves; some operations (e.g. x^3 + x y^2 + y) never generalize even at 95% data; and mixed operations (divide if odd, subtract if even) CAN generalize — the network learns to dispatch.

Experiment 2 (ablations on the S_5 group product, 120 elements / 14400 equations): weight decay is 'king' and roughly halves the data needed; weight decay toward the origin beats decay toward the initialization; any source of noise (mini-batch SGD, gradient noise, weight noise) helps, consistent with 'noise finds flatter minima'; the learning rate must be within ~1 order of magnitude; and ALL configurations reach 100% training accuracy in 10^3-10^4 steps, so generalization — not optimization — is the bottleneck.

Experiment 3 (time to generalize): near 25-30% of the data, removing just 1% of data requires 40-50% MORE optimization steps (an exponential blowup); meanwhile the time to reach 99% training accuracy actually DECREASES with less data (fewer examples are easier to memorize); this is a genuine compute-for-data tradeoff.

Experiment 4 (the dramatic grokking demo, division mod 97, 50% data, Adam with NO weight decay, 10^6 steps): training accuracy hits 100% by ~10^3 steps, validation accuracy stays at chance (1/97 ~ 1%) until ~10^5 steps, then suddenly shoots to 100% by ~10^6 steps; the validation LOSS actually INCREASES during memorization (double descent), peaking around 10^5 before the second descent — showing grokking can happen without explicit regularization, just from SGD noise over long training.

Experiment 5 (outlier robustness / wrong labels): the network always reaches 100% training accuracy (it memorizes the wrong labels too); generalization is barely affected up to k=1000 corrupted labels but degrades at k=2000-3000 — evidence that the network has capacity far beyond what memorization needs and that generalization requires a 'non-trivial explanation', not just capacity constraints.

Experiment 6 (what the network learns inside): t-SNE of the output-layer weights shows modular addition forms a CIRCLE (the network discovered Z/pZ is cyclic), with adding 8 tracing a path around it and residue classes mod 8 clustering; S_5 forms coset clusters; weight decay makes the structure more apparent; and at 0% training progress (before grokking) the embedding is just noise.

Experiment 7 (the hidden equivalence): x+y mod (p-1) is isomorphic to x*y mod p (via the discrete logarithm / primitive roots), and x-y mod (p-1) is isomorphic to x/y mod p; the data-efficiency curves of these isomorphic pairs match.
methods_math: tiny decoder-only transformer architecture (2 layers, 128 width, 4 heads) and the abstract-symbol operation-table task
a sweep over training-data fraction (10%-95%) and best validation accuracy as the generalization metric
ablation over optimizer/regularization: AdamW weight decay, decay-to-origin vs decay-to-init, mini-batch/gradient/weight noise, learning-rate sensitivity
the compute-for-data tradeoff and the critical data threshold (exponential blowup near 25-30% data)
double descent: training accuracy saturating while validation loss first rises then falls (the dramatic grokking curve)
robustness to corrupted labels (memorizing wrong answers) as evidence about capacity vs explanation
t-SNE visualization of output-layer embeddings revealing group/coset structure (cyclic Z/pZ, S_5 cosets)
isomorphisms between operations via primitive roots / discrete logarithm (x+y mod p-1 ~ x*y mod p)
visualizations: a 'what they built' architecture box (a code-styled block) spelling out the transformer, input format, abstract-symbol caveat, and optimizer
Experiment 1: a 12-operation grid plus a Plotly of best validation accuracy vs data-fraction with a fraction slider

Experiment 2: a Plotly of the 9 ablation curves (AdamW-the-winner, Adam, full-batch, full-batch+noise, dropout, decay-to-init, low/high LR, weight-noise) with a method-highlight dropdown and an optional training-accuracy toggle
Experiment 3: a Plotly of optimization-steps-to-99%-validation vs data-fraction with a critical-threshold and steepness slider and an optional train-time overlay
Experiment 4: the hero grokking plot (division mod 97) — training accuracy, validation accuracy and optionally loss vs steps — with data-fraction and weight-decay sliders and a Run button
Experiment 5: a Plotly of generalization vs number of corrupted labels (k) with a k slider and an Update button
Experiment 6: a t-SNE Canvas (650x650) of the output embeddings with task (mod-add / S_5), modulus, training-progress (noise -> structure) and colour-by-residue-mod sliders
Experiment 7: two side-by-side Plotly panels (isomorphic data-efficiency curves) with a prime-p slider, plus a small Canvas for the isomorphism map
internal_tensions: The headline tension is memorization-vs-generalization: an overparameterized model that should just memorize instead, after a long delay, 'groks' and generalizes — the double-descent loss curve (val loss rising then falling) is the visual signature of this paradox.

Regularization is both the driver and the complicating factor: Experiment 4 shows grokking happens even with NO explicit weight decay (just SGD noise), while Experiment 2 shows weight decay dramatically accelerates it — the piece holds both true at once.

It is a careful 'what they actually did' reconstruction of another group's experiments, so the claims are about faithfully reproducing the power et al. findings (and their interpretations, e.g. 'noise finds flatter minima') rather than presenting new results.

title: Holographic Storage & LLM Embedding Parallel
category_reason: English explanation of holographic data storage (volume holography, Fourier transform reconstruction, angular multiplexing) with an explicit and sustained parallel to LLM embedding spaces: how a hologram's non-local storage of information (any fragment contains the whole) mirrors the distributed, superposed nature of LLM embeddings. thesis: An English-language explanation of how volume holograms store and reconstruct data using wave interference and diffraction, drawing a sustained structural parallel to LLM embedding spaces: in both cases, information is stored non-locally (every part of the hologram contains information about the whole object; every dimension of an embedding vector contributes to the meaning), and retrieval is a projection operation (diffraction reconstructs the image; the unembedding matrix W_U projects the embedding onto the vocabulary).
key_claims: A volume hologram stores data as an interference pattern in a thick photorefractive or polymer medium; reconstruction is achieved by illuminating the hologram with the reference beam, which diffracts to reconstruct the object wave — this is a physical implementation of a correlation (matched filter) operation.

Angular multiplexing: many holograms can be stored in the same volume by using slightly different reference beam angles; during reconstruction, selecting the correct angle retrieves the correct data page, with crosstalk between pages acting as 'noise' — analogous to how LLMs store many concepts in the same embedding dimensions with superposition.

Non-local storage: if a hologram is broken into pieces, each piece still reconstructs the full image (at lower resolution); this is structurally analogous to LLM embeddings, where meaning is distributed across all dimensions and no single dimension 'contains' the meaning.

The reconstruction process (diffraction) is a linear projection: the stored interference pattern is multiplied by the reconstruction beam and integrated over the volume, which is mathematically a correlation operation — the same type of operation as the dot product between an embedding vector and a target concept vector in an LLM.

The 'grain' of the hologram medium (spatial resolution of the interference fringes) sets the storage density limit; analogously, the dimensionality of the embedding space sets the information capacity limit of an LLM, and the 'grain' is the quantization of floating-point precision.

internal_tensions: The LLM parallel is suggestive but not rigorous: holographic storage is a physical wave-optics phenomenon while LLM embeddings are learned mathematical representations; the 'non-locality' of a hologram is a property of wave physics, not of the information encoding per se.

title: Wie NNs beliebige Muster bauen – Mechanismen-Visualisierung
category_reason: A German-language interactive visualization explaining how neural networks build arbitrary patterns: the universal approximation theorem, local-expert hidden units, gradient descent training, and hierarchical feature learning in deep networks. Core neural-network theory and mechanism explanation.
thesis: A German-language interactive visualization explaining how neural networks build arbitrary patterns: from the universal approximation theorem (one hidden layer suffices in principle) through the mechanism of how individual hidden units learn to be local experts, to the full training process (gradient descent on a loss landscape) and hierarchical feature learning in deep networks.
key_claims: The universal approximation theorem: a single hidden layer with sufficiently many units and a non-polynomial activation function can approximate any continuous function on a compact set to arbitrary precision.
In practice, hidden units learn to be 'local experts': each unit fires strongly in a region of input space and weakly elsewhere, and the network output is a weighted sum of these local contributions.

Training via gradient descent adjusts weights so that each unit's contribution becomes increasingly aligned with the target function; the loss landscape is non-convex but gradient methods work in practice.
Deeper networks learn hierarchical features: lower layers detect local patterns (edges, parts), and higher layers compose them into global structures (wholes, categories).
The 'mechanism' of approximation is not a single clever trick but the collective contribution of many simple local experts whose weighted sum produces the global function.
visualizations: function approximation with adjustable number of hidden units
local expert activation heatmaps (which unit fires where)
gradient descent ball-on-loss-landscape animation
layer-by-layer feature hierarchy (edges → parts → wholes)
side-by-side comparison panels
target function vs. network output overlay
internal_tensions: The universal approximation theorem is existence-only: the required width can be enormous and the weights are not constructively found; the file's visual demos show smooth convergence that masks the non-convexity, plateaus, and mode-collapse phenomena of real training.

title: LLM Transformer – Attraktoren & Bedeutungsraum (Embedding Space)
category_reason: Visualizes an LLM/transformer's embedding space, per-layer attractors, context accumulation and unembedding — an interpretability picture of LLMs.
thesis: Meaning is a point in a high-dimensional space; transformer layers act as attractors that pull token embeddings (early layers = fixed/syntactic like POS, middle = semantic like 'capital of X', late = dynamic/context-dependent), the last vector of the last layer carries the mixed total context meaning (like a clock that extends with each token), and the next token is the nearest point in the vocabulary (unembedding via cosine similarity).
key_claims: Each token is a point in high-dim space; similar meanings lie close (2D projection shown); a 'CAPITAL_OF' convergence attractor is drawn.
Layer attractors are layer-typed: early (0–3) = fixed/syntactic (POS, article, preposition), middle (3–8) = semantic (e.g. CAPITAL_OF, COUNTRY), late (9–11) = dynamic, context-dependent (NEXT_TOKEN).
The last vector of the last layer contains the 'gemischte Gesamtbedeutung' (mixed total meaning) — metaphorically a clock that extends with each added token/frame.
Partial inhibition: attention selectively masks past tokens (illustrated with per-token attention-weight bars).
Unembedding / next-token prediction = nearest point in the vocabulary space (cosine similarity, e.g. 'Die Hauptstadt von Frankreich ist' → 'Paris', d≈0.06, cosine 0.94).
Cross-lingual: German and English tokens for the same meanings are placed near each other and connected (both → 'paris' attractor).
visualizations: Plotly: 2D embedding space (DE / EN / both, with the CAPITAL_OF star attractor and cross-lingual connector lines); a layer-attractor plot with a layer slider (0–11) where active attractor basins (circles) and token positions shift toward them (early=solid syntax, late=dashed dynamic). Canvas: 'context accumulation' — a growing context frame of token boxes with attention-weight bars, a gradient 'mixed vector', and a clock whose hand sweeps with context steps; an unembedding canvas placing the accumulated context vector with candidate tokens at distance-proportional radii plus a softmax probability bar.
internal_tensions: The 'layer attractor' picture (early=syntax, mid=semantics, late=next-token) is a specific, partly contested interpretability narrative; it is not universally supported across architectures/depths.
All token coordinates and attractor positions are hand-authored 2D values, and the context/'clock' and unembedding panels use randomized/fake vectors — illustrative, not read from a real model.

The claim that the final-layer last-position vector 'contains the whole meaning' (the 'clock extends') echoes the pooled/last-token representation debate; here it is asserted as a metaphor without qualification.

title: LLM als Attraktor in einem Bedeutungsraum — Eine interaktive Ideenexploration
category_reason: The entire file is a thought-exploration of how LLMs can be understood as dynamical systems moving through a semantic/meaning space, with attention as the mechanism creating basins of attraction. This is a core AI/LLM interpretability and mechanism question.
thesis: An interactive German-language idea exploration proposing that an LLM's 'thinking' is best understood as a dynamical trajectory through a high-dimensional meaning space, where attention heads create local basins of attraction, and the model's output is the state the trajectory settles into — with interactive 2D/3D visualizations of the basin structure.
key_claims: An LLM's residual stream can be viewed as a point in a high-dimensional semantic space; each transformer layer applies a nonlinear map that moves this point, and the final output is a function of the terminal state.

Attention heads act as 'local attractor generators': each head pulls the residual stream toward a semantic subspace associated with its learned key pattern, creating a superposition of competing basins.
The 'grokking' phenomenon (sudden generalization after a long plateau) can be reinterpreted as the trajectory crossing a basin boundary into a more stable attractor that generalizes.
Meaning is not stored at a single point but is a region of the space: paraphrases occupy nearby basins, and the model's 'understanding' is the basin's geometry (shape, volume, depth).
Temperature sampling corresponds to adding noise to the trajectory: low temperature = gradient descent within one basin; high temperature = random jumps between basins.
The 'Idea 2' framing (this is a second version) suggests an earlier idea explored a different metaphor; the attractor framing is presented as more mathematically precise.
methods_math: dynamical systems: fixed points, attractors, basins of attraction, Lyapunov stability
nonlinear maps in high-dimensional spaces, superposition of basins
attention as a learned projection onto a semantic subspace (spectral decomposition)
basin boundary crossing as a bifurcation / phase transition
Langevin dynamics as a model of temperature-sampled generation
gradient flow in continuous limit of discrete layer updates
visualizations: interactive 2D 'meaning landscape' with adjustable attention-head weights: drag sliders to see how basins merge, split, or deepen
animated trajectory of the residual stream through the 2D landscape as layers are applied (one step at a time)
basin boundary heatmap showing sensitivity to input perturbation (a proxy for 'interpretability fragility')
grokking simulation: a trajectory that plateaus in a shallow basin, then suddenly jumps to a deeper one when a hidden symmetry is discovered
temperature dial: watch the same trajectory become a random walk between basins as temperature increases
internal_tensions: The 2D visualizations are necessarily reductive: real LLM spaces are 10^4-10^7 dimensional, and the 'basin' structure in high dimensions is poorly understood (curse of dimensionality, mode collapse).
The file presents the attractor metaphor as established, but it is an analogy, not a proven model; no empirical validation (e.g., CKA similarity across layers) is offered.

The 'grokking as basin crossing' claim is suggestive but conflates two different phenomena: the Nanda et al. grokking (regularity discovery via weight decay) and the basin-crossing narrative are not clearly linked.
The file is explicitly labeled 'idea2' — a draft/thought-exploration, not a finished argument; several claims are presented as open questions rather than theses.

title: Kohärente Welten – 20 Konzepte zum Anfassen
category_reason: An interactive German-language collection of ~17 canvas mini-visualizations on coherent world models, with explicit LLM connections: the 'Hallucination (Selbst-Kohärenz ≠ Wahrheit)' concept, 'Kohärenz vs. Korrespondenz' framed in terms of LLMs, and 'Embedding-Raum' as a core concept. The file directly discusses how LLMs confuse internal coherence with world knowledge.
thesis: An interactive German-language collection of ~17 canvas-based mini-visualizations exploring how multiple local viewpoints cohere into a single 'world': from Spencer-Brown's primitive act of drawing a distinction, through topology without metric, sheaf gluing, homotopy as coherence-without-equality, embedding spaces where meaning = position, to the critical distinction between coherence (internal consistency) and correspondence (external anchor) — with an explicit application to LLM hallucination.
key_claims: Distinktion (Spencer-Brown): before anything exists, a boundary must be drawn; every distinction creates an inside and an outside — all mathematics begins here.

Lokalität ohne Metrik: a topological space is a set of points plus a specification of which subsets are 'open' (neighborhoods); proximity arises from membership in common neighborhoods, not from distances or coordinates.
Sheaf & Gluing: two observers see parts of the world; their views must agree on the overlap for a coherent global picture to exist — this is the sheaf axiom made tactile.
Kohärenz statt Gleichheit: two things need not be identical to belong together; it suffices that there is a continuous deformation (homotopy) between them — the core of ∞-categories and HoTT.
Embedding-Raum: words have no intrinsic meaning; their meaning is their position in the network of differences to all other words — the space is the pattern of their relations, not a container.
Hallucination (Selbst-Kohärenz ≠ Wahrheit): an LLM can generate internally coherent text that has no correspondence to the world; coherence is necessary but not sufficient for truth.

Kohärenz vs. Korrespondenz: coherence checks whether a model is internally consistent; correspondence checks whether it is anchored to the world; these are two different tests, and one alone is never enough.
methods_math: Spencer-Brown's Laws of Form (distinction as primitive)
topological spaces, open sets, neighborhoods (without metric)
sheaf theory: gluing axiom, local-to-global principle
embedding spaces, word vectors, relational meaning

internal_tensions: The file covers 17 concepts in a single page, which means each mini-visualization is necessarily shallow; the 'tactile' (zum Anfassen) promise is kept at the interaction level but not at the conceptual depth.

The jump from Spencer-Brown's distinction (a philosophical/logical primitive) to sheaf theory (a sophisticated algebraic-geometric tool) to LLM hallucination (a practical AI concern) is large; the connecting thread (coherence) is stated but not argued.

The 'Hallucination' concept is the most practically relevant but also the least developed: the file states that self-coherence ≠ truth but does not offer a concrete mechanism for detecting or mitigating hallucination.

The file is labeled 'ideen2' (ideas 2), suggesting it is a draft or second iteration of an earlier exploration; the concepts are presented as a gallery rather than a unified argument, and the relationship between the 17 concepts is implicit.

title: Transformers Learn In Context by Gradient Descent · Interaktiver Erklärer
category_reason: Erklärt den Mechanismus von In-Context-Learning in Transformer-LLMs als impliziter Gradientenabstieg; zentrales Ergebnis verbindet Forward-Pass mit GD-Schritt (von Oswald et al., ICML 2023).
thesis: Der Forward-Pass eines Transformers berechnet einen Schritt impliziten Gradientenabstiegs auf den Demonstrations-Beispielen: Die Gewichtsmatrizen W_K, W_Q, W_V und die Projektion P sind so konstruiert, dass ein einzelner Forward-Pass exakt einen GD-Schritt auf quadratischer Verlustfunktion reproduziert.
key_claims: Proposition 1: Es existiert eine explizite Konstruktion von W_K, W_Q, W_V, P, so dass der Forward-Pass eines 2-Schicht-Transformers exakt einen GD-Schritt mit Lernrate η = λ reproduziert.
W_K^T W_Q = η·I: die Schlüssel-Query-Interaktion kodiert die Lernrate.
Die Projektionsmatrix P ist meta-ge Lernt: sie optimiert die Lernrate über die Demonstrationen.
Tiefe Transformer = mehrere aufeinanderfolgende GD-Schritte (ein Layer pro Schritt).
GD++ (Kraftkorrektur) entspricht einer zusätzlichen Schicht mit Hessian-Korrigatur.
In-Context-Learning ist ein Fall von Mesa-Optimierung: das Modell optimiert eine interne Metaspiele, um die GD-Dynamik zu lernen.
Verbindung zu Fast Weights (Schmidhuber 1992): Attention ist eine moderne Realisierung des Fast-Weight-Prinzips.

Interaktive Lernraten-Regler
Schichtweite GD-Schritte animiert
KaTeX-Formeln für die Matrixkonstruktion
internal_tensions: Das Ergebnis gilt für lineare/quadratische Tasks; für echte NLP-Daten ist die Näherung nicht bewiesen.
Die Konstruktion ist existenzbasiert (es gibt eine Lösung), aber nicht die einzige; reale Trainingsverfahren erreichen diese Konfiguration nicht garantiert.
Mesa-Optimierung ist ein interpretativer Rahmen, kein formal bewiesener Mechanismus — der Begriff trägt kontroverse Konnotationen.

title: Informationsgravitation · Interaktive Reise durch das Paper
category_reason: Feldtheoretisches Modell für Token-Auswahl in LLMs: modelliert Sprachmodell-Generierung als Bewegung in einem durch Informationsmasse gekrümmten semantischen Raum (Vyshnyvetska, arXiv:2504.20951, 2025).
thesis: Eine Nutzerfrage Q übt eine Informationsmasse M(Q) = αH(Q) + βD(Q) + γN(Q) aus, die den semantischen Potentialraum Φ(t,Q) = −log P(t|Q) krümmt; Token-Generierung ist die Bewegung in diesem Potential, und die drei Hauptphänomene (Zufallszahlen-Bias, Prompt-Sensitivität, Halluzinationen) sind derselbe Effekt in verschiedenen Parameterbereichen.
key_claims: Informationsmasse M(Q) = α·H(Q) + β·D(Q) + γ·N(Q): Entropie, Kontexttiefe und Novelty kombinieren zu einer einzigen Größe.
Semantisches Potential Φ(t,Q) = −log P(t|Q); Gradient g = −∇Φ zeigt zum wahrscheinlichsten Token.
Hessematrix-Hoch-Eigenwerte auf kleinen Gebieten + niedrige globale Token-Probabilität → Halluzination (Einfang in falsches lokales Minimum).
Prompt-Sensitivität (56 Prozentpunkte, Sclar et al.) = Bifurkationspunkt zwischen zwei Attraktor-Tälern; kleine ΔΦ kann den Attraktor wechseln.
Zufallszahlen-Bias (Zhang et al., 2024: Llama-2 bevorzugt die 5) = Training-Data-Attraktor im Potential.
Boltzmann-Verteilung / Softmax mit Temperatur T: T→0 deterministisch (Capture), T→∞ uniform (chaotisch).
Vorgeschlagene adaptive Temperatur T(Q) = f(M(Q)): hohe Masse → höhere T, um aus Fallen herauszukommen.
Informations-Schwarzloch (Alignment): künstlich erzeugte Region extrem hoher Dichte → deterministische Standardantworten.

title: Intrinsische Dimension in tiefen neuronalen Netzen — Interaktive Reise
category_reason: Intrinsische Dimension von Repräsentationen in tiefen Netzen als zentrales diagnostisches Werkzeug; basiert auf Ansuini et al. (NeurIPS 2019, arXiv:1905.12784) und TwoNN (Facco et al. 2017).
thesis: Tiefe Netze verformen den Eingaberaum nicht 'flacher', sondern 'dünner': die intrinsische Dimension der Repräsentationen steigt zunächst an (Hunchback) und fällt dann wieder; die Daten sind dünn (niedrige ID) aber gekrümmt (nicht flach), und die ID der letzten versteckten Schicht ist ein starker Prädiktor für die Testgenauigkeit (r=0.94) — was den Flachheits-Mythos und die Übertrainings-Interpretation von Ma et al. 2018 widerlegt.
key_claims: Die intrinsische Dimension (ID) in tiefen Netzen zeigt ein Hunchback-Phänomen: sie steigt in frühen Schichten, erreicht ein Maximum und fällt in späten Schichten (Ansuini et al. 2019).
Die ID der letzten versteckten Schicht korreliert stark (r=0.94) mit der Testgenauigkeit — sie ist ein Prädiktor für Generalisierung.
Tiefe Netze machen Daten nicht flacher, sondern dünner: die ID sinkt, aber die Krümmung steigt — die Repräsentation ist eine gekrümmte niedrigdimensionale Mannigfaltigkeit.
Der TwoNN-Äschätzer (Facco et al. 2017) ist der Standard für die ID-Schätzung in hochdimensionalen Räuen; er nutzt die Verteilung der Abstände zum 1. und 2. nächsten Nachbarn.
Random-Label-Experimente: bei zufälligen Labels steigt die ID in der zweiten Hälfte des Trainings (Memorisation); bei echten Labels bleibt sie stabil — ID als 'Übertrainings-Alarm' ist irreführend.
Die Trainings-Dynamik der ID ist nicht monoton und hängt von Architektur, Learning-Rate-Schedule und Datenkomplexität ab.
Widerlegung von Ma et al. 2018: eine steigende ID ist kein Übertrainings-Signal, sondern kann mit besserer Generalisierung einhergehen.
Widerlegung des Flachheits-Mythos: tiefe Netze minimieren nicht den Flachheitsgrad, sondern die ID in Kombination mit der Krümmung.
visualizations: Three.js (3D-Punktewolken, Krümmung)
Canvas 2D (ID-Verläufe, TwoNN-Histogramme)
Plotly (Training-Kurven, Korrelationen)
Temml (Formeln)
14 interaktive Labs
internal_tensions: Der TwoNN-Äschätzer hat bekannte Bias bei nicht-euklidischen Metriken und inhomogener Dichte — die ID-Schätzung in tiefen Netzen (mit LayerNorm, Softmax) ist nicht genau euklidisch.
Die Korrelation r=0.94 ist auf MNIST/CIFAR-10-Architekturen beobachtet; die Übertragbarkeit auf große Sprachmodelle ist unklar.
Das Hunchback-Phänomen ist ein Durchschnitt über viele Experimente; individuelle Trainingsläufe können andere Verläufe zeigen.

title: Intrinsische Dimension tiefer Netze — Einfach erklärt
category_reason: ML-Theorie: intrinsische Dimension neuronaler Repräsentationen (Ansuini et al. 2019, TwoNN-Schätzer); 'Dimension sinkt mit der Tiefe'. Klare KI-Kopplung.
thesis: Tiefe neuronale Netze lernen Repräsentationen, deren intrinsische Dimension (die effektive Anzahl der Dimensionen, die die Daten tatsächlich nutzen) mit der Tiefe sinkt — ein 'Ahnungs'-Ergebnis, dass tiefe Netze die Daten-Mannigfaltigkeit schrittweise komprimieren. Ansuini et al. (2019) schätzen diese intrinsische Dimension mit der TwoNN-Methode und zeigen, dass sie über die Schichten hinweg abnimmt: tiefere Schichten fassen zunehmend niedriger-dimensionale Struktur.
key_claims: Die intrinsische Dimension einer Datenmenge/einer Repräsentation ist die effektive Anzahl der Dimensionen, die die Daten besetzen — kleiner als die Umgebungsdimension.
TwoNN (Ansuini et al. 2019): schätzt die intrinsische Dimension aus der Verteilung des Verhältnisses der Distanzen zum 2. vs. 1. nächsten Nachbarn (Peak = Dimension).
In tiefen Netzen sinkt die intrinsische Dimension der versteckten Repräsentationen tendenziell mit der Tiefe — das Netz 'komprimiert' die Daten.
Diese 'Dimensionsreduktion mit der Tiefe' ist eine Signatur dafür, dass das Netz bedeutungsvolle, kompakte Repräsentationen lernt.
PCA-basierte Schätzungen können irreführend sein; TwoNN ist für mannigfaltigkeits-artige Daten robuster.
Niedrigere intrinsische Dimension in tieferen Schichten korreliert mit besserer Generalisierung/Robustheit (vereinfachte Repräsentation).
visualizations: Canvas/Plotly: TwoNN-Histogramm (Peak = intrinsische Dimension)
Plotly: intrinsische Dimension vs. Schichttiefe (abfallend)
Vergleich PCA vs. TwoNN
Mannigfaltigkeits-Skizze (Daten in hoch-/niedrig-dimensionalem Raum)
internal_tensions: Die intrinsische Dimension ist eine heuristische Schätzung, keine wohldefinierte Invariante — der Wert hängt vom Schätzer und den Parametern ab.
'Dimension sinkt mit der Tiefe' wird beobachtet, aber die kausale Mechanik (warum tiefer = niedriger-dimensionaler) ist nicht vollständig verstanden.
Die TwoNN-Schätzung setzt eine (nahezu) uniforme Verteilung auf der Mannigfaltigkeit voraus — für real ungleichmäßig verteilte Daten ist sie verzerrt.

title: Wie viele Regler stecken in einem Gedanken? (Intrinsic Dimension of Deep NNs, very simple)
category_reason: A plain-language explainer of Ansuini et al. 2019: the low intrinsic dimension of deep CNN representations and its correlation with generalization.
thesis: Even though a CNN layer stores 100,000+ numbers, the information the network 'really knows' lives in only a few dozen 'knobs' (a low-dimensional, curved manifold) — and the intrinsic dimension of the final layer strongly predicts how well the network generalizes (r ~ 0.94).
key_claims: A digital face image has 150,528 numbers, but ~4 'knobs' (position x/y, size, smile) nearly capture it — the essential degrees of freedom are far fewer than the storage.
In a VGG-16 CNN the intrinsic dimension is a 'Buckel' (bump): high in early layers, lowest in the last (pool4 ~19 knobs vs 100,352 stored numbers, ratio ~2e-4).

The data in deep layers is curved, not flat: PCA (a linear method) estimates ~200 components while the nonlinear TwoNN method estimates ~19 — a factor >10 — so a nonlinear view is needed to see the true dimension.
The intrinsic dimension of the final layer predicts generalization: across 14 architectures the correlation with test accuracy is r = 0.94 (a thinner folded manifold -> better generalization).

Honesty corner: TwoNN is accurate only up to ~dimension 20 (above that the values are lower bounds); the paper is CNN-only (Transformers/LLMs open); simplifying MNIST digits drops ID from 13 to 3, showing ID tracks data complexity, not just architecture.
methods_math: manifold hypothesis (data on a low-dim curved manifold in high-dim space)
visualizations: two canvas 2D demos: (1) a face you shape with 4 sliders showing the 'knobs vs stored numbers' ratio, (2) the 'Buckel' (bump) curve of intrinsic dimension across VGG-16 pooling layers with a layer selector and ID/embedded-dim/ratio readouts
internal_tensions: It presents the low-ID -> better-generalization correlation as suggestive, but correlation is not causation; the file frames it as 'the geometry of the learned representation co-determines generalization', a hypothesis rather than a proven mechanism.
TwoNN's reliability ceiling (dim ~20) and the CNN-only scope are real limits the file itself flags.

title: Attention Heads als 'Augen'
category_reason: Explains transformer attention heads and the causal attention matrix with an interactive demo.
thesis: Each attention head is an 'eye' attending to a different aspect of token relations; the attention matrix (rows = query tokens 'I look from here', columns = key tokens 'I look there') can be read directly, with the causal mask zeroing the upper-right triangle.
key_claims: Rows of the matrix are Query tokens ('I look from here'), columns are Key tokens ('I look there'); each cell is that head's attention score for the pair.
The upper-right triangle is set to 0 by the causal mask — a token can only attend to itself and earlier tokens.

Eight hand-defined head 'scorers' model different behaviors: previous token, sentence start (BOS-like), self-reference, word-length match, repetition detector, far-back exponential decay, vowel-pattern similarity, and token-2-back.
Softmax is applied per row after masking, producing weights that sum to 1.
After attention each token gets a new vector that is the (causally limited) weighted sum of the context.
visualizations: An interactive HTML attention matrix with color-coded cells (click any cell for details), a legend of head-buttons (each with an emoji and behavior), a selectable head count, and an output-vector panel showing each token's weighted context aggregation; live sentence input.
internal_tensions: The heads are hand-coded toy scorers standing in for learned projections, so the 'specialization' is illustrative rather than empirical.
The 'eyes' metaphor risks over-reading intentionality into a linear-algebraic operation.

title: Global Workspace in Language Models - Interaktive Erklärung
category_reason: Interaktive Erklärung des Papers 'Verbalizable Representations Form a Global Workspace in Language Models' (Gurnee et al., 2026): LLM-Repräsentationen bilden einen kleinen 'verbalisierbaren' Globalen Arbeitsraum (J-Space), lesbar über eine Jacobian-Lens. Klare KI-Kopplung (LLM-Interpretierbarkeit + Safety).
thesis: Sprachmodelle besitzen einen kleinen, 'verbalisierbaren' Teil ihrer internen Repräsentationen (den J-Space/Jacobian-Space), der wie ein Globaler Arbeitsraum (analog zur Global-Workspace-Theorie aus der Neurowissenschaft) funktioniert; eine Jacobian-Lens macht diese Gedanken lesbar, und die Struktur hat praktische Sicherheitsrelevanz.
key_claims: Der J-Space macht nur ~5–10 % der Gesamtaktivierung (bzw. ~6–7 % der Varianz) aus, trägt aber ~59 % der berichteten Änderungsleistung; der Rest (~93 % Varianz) leistet nur ~5 %.
Eine 'Jacobian Lens' (J-Lens) — im Unterschied zur Logit Lens — zeigt, welche Wörter ein Modell gerade intern 'denkt', auch wenn es sie nicht ausspricht.
Der J-Space erfüllt fünf Eigenschaften eines Globalen Arbeitsraums: verbaler Bericht, gerichtete Modulation, internes Reasoning (Zwischenschritte), flexible Generalisierung und Selektivität.
Die Workspace-Zone liegt in den oberen Schichten des Modells (Layer-Diagramm).
Der J-Space ist für Safety-Anwendungen nutzbar: Erpressungs-/Blackmail-Szenario, Erkennung trainierter Fehlausrichtungen und 'Counterfactual Reflection Training' werden demonstriert.
Kausale Interventions-Experimente (z. B. Ersetzen des J-Space-Vektors 'spider' durch 'ant' ändert die Antwort von 8 auf 6) belegen die kausale Rolle des J-Space.

title: J-Space & Jacobian Lens — Transformer Interpretability
category_reason: German interactive explanation of J-Space (a geometric structure for transformer representation space) and the Jacobian Lens (a tool for reading out intermediate computations), using Temml for embedding visualizations and Plotly for projections. Core transformer interpretability / representation geometry.
thesis: A German-language interactive explanation of two complementary tools for understanding transformer internals: J-Space, which posits that the representation space of a transformer has a geometric structure (a 'J-space') where semantically related concepts occupy nearby regions, and the Jacobian Lens, which uses the Jacobian of the output with respect to an intermediate layer to read out what the layer is 'thinking' — visualized with Temml embedding projections and Plotly scatter plots.
key_claims: J-Space is the hypothesis that the high-dimensional representation space of a transformer is not a flat vector space but has intrinsic geometric structure: semantically related tokens are close, and the 'distance' between concepts in J-space corresponds to their functional relationship in the model's computation.

The Jacobian Lens works as follows: for a given intermediate layer ℓ and output token v, the Jacobian entry ∂logit(v)/∂h_ℓ[i] measures how much the i-th dimension of the layer-ℓ residual stream influences the probability of token v; this gives a 'lens' that maps the layer-ℓ state to a vocabulary distribution.

Unlike the standard logit lens (which uses the unembedding matrix W_U directly), the Jacobian Lens accounts for the nonlinear transformations in later layers, giving a more accurate 'readout' of intermediate computations at deeper layers.

In J-Space, linear directions correspond to semantic features (e.g., 'positive sentiment', 'past tense'); the geometry of J-space is anisotropic — some directions are 'longer' (more important) than others, and the metric is learned, not Euclidean.

The combination of J-space geometry and the Jacobian Lens allows the user to 'navigate' the model's internal computation: pick a layer, pick a direction in J-space, and see which tokens are affected — a kind of 'X-ray' of the transformer's reasoning.
methods_math: Jacobian matrix ∂f/∂h and its entries as influence measures
logit lens: W_U h^ℓ as a baseline readout
Jacobian Lens: J_ℓ[v,i] = ∂logit(v)/∂h_ℓ[i] as a per-token influence map
embedding space geometry: cosine similarity, anisotropy, metric learning
PCA / t-SNE projection of high-dimensional embeddings to 2D/3D
Temml (Temml) for rendering embedding vectors as interactive 3D point clouds
visualizations: Temml 3D embedding cloud: token embeddings projected to 3D, color-coded by semantic category; user can click a point to see its Jacobian Lens readout
Jacobian Lens heatmap: rows are vocabulary tokens, columns are dimensions of the residual stream at layer ℓ; color = J_ℓ value; user can scrub through layers to watch the 'focus' of the lens shift
J-space navigation: a 2D slice of J-space with a draggable 'probe' vector; the affected tokens are highlighted in a side panel
comparison: logit lens vs. Jacobian Lens at the same layer, showing where they agree and where the Jacobian Lens captures nonlinear effects the logit lens misses
internal_tensions: The J-space hypothesis is presented as established, but the geometric structure of transformer representation space is still an active area of research; the 'J-space' is a useful metaphor but its precise mathematical definition is not settled.

The Jacobian Lens is computationally expensive (requires backpropagating through all later layers for each token), which limits its practical use to small models or a subset of tokens; the page does not emphasize this computational cost.

title: Hohe Dimensionen komprimieren — Ganz einfach erklärt
category_reason: Johnson–Lindenstrauss-Lemma / Random Projection für Geometrie von Embeddings hoherdimensionaler Daten (Fotos als Punkte); zentrale Geometrie hinter ML-Embeddings und Dimensionsreduktion
thesis: Sehr einfache, interaktive Erklärung des Johnson–Lindenstrauss-Lemmas: n hochdimensionale Punkte lassen sich zufällig auf ein Handvoll Dimensionen projizieren (≈O(log n), abhängig nur von der Anzahl der Punkte, nicht von der Ausgangsdimension d), während fast alle paarweisen Abstände erhalten bleiben — weil in hohen Dimensionen zufällige Richtungen nahezu orthogonal sind und Abstände selten kollidieren
key_claims: Ein Punkt in d Dimensionen ist nur eine Liste von d Zahlen; ein Foto mit 1 Million Pixeln ist ein Punkt mit einer Million Koordinaten; 'Ähnlichkeit' = kleiner Abstand zwischen Punkten, also ist das Erhalten der Abstände das Ziel
Der Trick: Punkte zufällig auf wenige Dimensionen werfen (wie ein Foto der Punktwolke aus einem zufälligen Winkel) — fast alle paarweisen Abstände überleben
Die Anzahl benötigter Ziel-Dimensionen hängt nur von n (Anzahl der Punkte) ab, nicht von der Ausgangsdimension d: ~O(log n) (illustriert als ≈4·log₂ n)
Mit einer einzigen zufälligen Richtung (1 Dim) brechen viele Abstände; mit einem Handvoll (2–3) überleben fast alle — die zentrale Beobachtung hinter dem Lemma

Warum es funktioniert: In hohen Dimensionen sind die individuellen Abstandsstörungen nahezu unabhängig (kaum Kollisionen), sodass der allergrößte Teil aller Abstände 'auf einmal, gleichzeitig' überlebt
visualizations: 3 interaktive Canvas-Demos: (1) 'was eine Dimension ist' (2D/3D-Ebenen), (2) 'der Wurf' (Random-Projection einer 3D-Wolke auf 1/2/3 Dimensionen mit Nachbar-Kanten + Abstands-Ratio-Histogramm, zeigt %-Anteil innerhalb ±25%), (3) 'wie viele Dimensionen reichen' (Balken davor vs. benötigtes k=4·log₂ n, demonstriert k unabhängig von d)
internal_tensions: Popularisierung, die nur 3D-Punktwolken verwendet (das '1M-Pixel-Foto' ist Rhetorik; das eigentliche Demo projiziert 3D→weniger Dimensionen)

'≈4·log₂ n' ist eine Heuristik-Konstante, nicht die exakte JL-Schranke (die spezifische ε,δ-abhängige Konstanten hat); die Unabhängigkeits-Intuition der Störungen blendet die concentration-of-measure-Maschinerie hinter dem echten Beweis aus

Grenze der Klassifikation: Die Mathematik (JL/Embeddings-Geometrie) ist grundlegend für ML-Embeddings, aber die Seite rahmt es als reine Daten-Kompressions-Geometrie, ohne ML/Neuronale Netze explizit zu benennen

title: Garben, ∞-Garben & Erkenntnistheorie — Interaktiv
category_reason: Builds from sheaf theory and HoTT to an explicit AI application: section 7 models language-model training as loss-landscape optimization where the model finds the best 'gluing' of training traces, and defines hallucination as 'a gluing where no gluing should exist' — i.e., the model interpolates in regions with no coherent training data. The HoTT embedding-space example (König − Mann + Frau ≈ Königin) is presented as working because semantic proximity is a path in a meaning space.
thesis: A seven-section German interactive essay that builds from sheaf theory (presheaves on sin(x), gluing conditions) through ∞-sheaves (gluing up to homotopy) and HoTT (types as spaces, embedding spaces in AI) to an epistemological claim — the world is a sheaf of traces observed through multiple channels — and finally to AI: the loss function is an energy landscape, the model finds the best gluing of training data, and hallucination occurs when it glues where no coherent training sections exist.
key_claims: A presheaf F: Open(X)^op → Set assigns local data with restriction maps; the gluing condition (compatible local sections → unique global section) makes it a sheaf.

∞-sheaves replace strict equality on overlaps with isomorphisms: sᵢ|ᵢⱼ ≅ sⱼ|ᵢⱼ, with the isomorphisms themselves satisfying higher coherence conditions — 'equality becomes a structure, not a property.'
In HoTT, every type is a space and identity a = b is a path; embedding spaces in AI work because semantic proximity (König − Mann + Frau ≈ Königin) is a path in the meaning space.

Epistemology: a world event w produces traces e = f(w) through multiple channels fᵢ (eyes, ears, instruments, testimony); a world model is 'true' when its local sections glue coherently, at least up to homotopy.
Science is the art of isolating contact points between model and world — experiments with few free variables where gluing can be tested.
A language model's loss is an energy landscape: θ* = argmin E[L(f_θ(x), y)]; the model lands in a valley representing the best gluing of all training traces.

Hallucination is a gluing where no gluing should exist: when the model encounters a context where local training sections do not coherently overlap, it interpolates — producing plausible-sounding but false output.
Local minima in the loss landscape correspond to consistent but incomplete world models.

The HoTT embedding-space example (König − Mann + Frau ≈ Königin) conflates linear algebra in a vector space with path structure in a type — the analogy is intuitive but the mathematical content is different.

title: Self-Organizing Map (SOM) · Kohonen
category_reason: Implements and animates a Kohonen Self-Organizing Map, an unsupervised neural-network / dimensionality-reduction algorithm.
thesis: A real-time canvas animation of Kohonen SOM learning, showing how a 14×14 grid of neurons self-organizes to map a data set onto a fixed topological grid while preserving the data's shape.
key_claims: The SOM repeatedly picks a data point, finds its best-matching unit (BMU), and moves the BMU and its grid neighbors toward it.
Learning rate decays from 0.46 and the neighborhood radius decays over the horizon T=9000: lr = .46·(.008/.46)^f, rad = (G·.62)·(.9/(G·.62))^f.
Neighbor influence is a Gaussian over grid distance: h = exp(−g²/s)·lr.
The grid topology (Panel B) is fixed, while the neuron positions in data space (Panel A) deform to match the data shape.
Five data shapes (ring, blobs, square, spiral, cross) are offered to show the SOM recovering the input's topology.

title: Latent Semantic Manifolds in Large Language Models (Mabrok, 2026)
category_reason: A formal information-geometric paper (arXiv:2603.22301) about the geometry of LLM hidden-state representations — Fisher metric, Riemannian semantic manifolds, Voronoi token generation, and rate-distortion bounds, empirically tested on 6 real LLMs.
thesis: Language is a lossy compression of a continuous concept space; contextual hidden states of a transformer lie on a thin Riemannian 'latent semantic manifold' (k≈20 ≪ d) tiled by token Voronoi cells, and there is a provable, unbridgeable loss floor for any finite vocabulary — the first empirical confirmation of a proven geometric theorem about LLM representations.
key_claims: Hypothesis 4.1: for each layer ℓ, contextual hidden states (layer ≥ 1) lie on a smooth compact connected k-dimensional Riemannian submanifold of ℝ^d with k ≈ 15–22 and d = 768–2048, so only 1–3% of the vector space is actually used.
The manifold is GENERATED by the transformer, not inherited from the embedding table — raw token embeddings (layer 0) violate the hypothesis (Robinson et al. 2025; MLE gives a k≈68 artifact there).

Token generation = Voronoi projection: when embeddings have equal norm, argmax ⟨e_t, h⟩ is identical to argmin ‖h − e_t‖ (greedy decoding = nearest-neighbor search); each token's cell volume μ(R_t) measures its conceptual breadth (polysemous vs precise words).

The Fisher metric G = Wᵀ(diag(p) − ppᵀ)W is the canonical metric on hidden states — by Chentsov's theorem it is the only Riemannian metric (up to scale) invariant under sufficient statistics; it is the second derivative of the KL divergence (Prop 12.3).

Satz 10.5 (linear volume law): the normalized expressibility gap η(ε) = [H^{k−1}(∂V)/(λ·vol(M))]·ε + O(ε²) for ε < 1/(2κ_∂); a single scalar α characterizes vocabulary quality; empirically log-log slopes 0.873–1.117 with R² > 0.985 on all 6 models.

Satz 10.8 (fundamental distortion bound): D ≥ c_k·ν_min·(vol(M)/N)^(2/k) — no finite vocabulary reaches zero distortion; halving the loss at k=20 needs ~1024× more tokens, at k=50 ~33 million× (the curse of dimensionality).

There is an 'irreducible ambiguity floor': m_0.05 ≈ 0.04–0.06 across all 6 models despite a 12× parameter range — ~5% of natural-language positions are genuinely ambiguous and no model size removes it (analogous to irreducible loss in scaling laws).

The geometry (k, the hourglass pattern, the linear gap law) is an invariant of the TASK 'next-token prediction on natural language', not of the architecture — identical across GPT-2/OPT/Pythia, 124M–1.5B, different data and tokenizers.

internal_tensions: All evidence is correlation and consistency-checking, not causality — no intervention experiments.
Not tested above 1.5B parameters; if k grows with scale, the rate-distortion / vocabulary-design predictions change fundamentally.
vol(M) is never measured absolutely (only ratios), so Satz 10.8 is qualitative, not numerically verified.
The Fisher metric degenerates when the output distribution becomes sharp (large β, Σ_p → 0) — a stated boundary of the framework.
Layer 0 (raw embeddings) violates the manifold hypothesis, so the hypothesis applies only to contextual states (layer ≥ 1).
Entropy and margin are related but NOT the same (|Spearman ρ| ≈ 0.16–0.23, not ~1); the paper argues margin — not entropy — is the right quantity for 'can language express this thought'.
Vision-language / other modalities are untested.

title: Latente Semantische Mannigfaltigkeiten in LLMs — Einfach erklärt
category_reason: Geometrie der Embeddings / LLM-Internes: Wort-/Begriffs-Embeddings liegen auf (nahe) einer niedrig-dimensionalen semantischen Mannigfaltigkeit; deren Geometrie kodiert Bedeutungsrelationen. Klare KI-Kopplung.
thesis: Die Wort-/Begriffs-Embeddings eines LLM liegen auf (oder nahe) einer niedrig-dimensionalen semantischen Mannigfaltigkeit im hochdimensionalen Embedding-Raum; die Geometrie dieser Mannigfaltigkeit (Distanzen, Krümmung, Vektorrelationen) spiegelt Bedeutungszusammenhänge — ähnliche Bedeutungen sind geometrisch nah, Analogien sind (nahezu) parallele Vektoren, und die Form der Mannigfaltigkeit erfasst den gelernten 'Bedeutungsraum'.
key_claims: LLM-Embeddings besetzen einen strukturierten niedrig-dimensionalen Unterraum ('semantische Mannigfaltigkeit') im hochdimensionalen Raum — die Mannigfaltigkeits-Hypothese für Sprache.
Ähnliche Bedeutungen sind geometrisch nah (Cosinus-Distanz); Wort-Analogien (König − Mann + Frau ≈ Königin) sind Vektorarithmetik auf der Mannigfaltigkeit.
Die Krümmung/Geometrie der Mannigfaltigkeit kodiert semantische Struktur — sie ist nicht zufällig, sondern vom Training geformt.
Dimensionsreduktion (PCA/UMAP/t-SNE) projiziert die Mannigfaltigkeit in 2D/3D und macht die Begriffskluster sichtbar.
Je kontextreicher das Embedding (LLM vs. statisches Word2Vec), desto 'beugbarer' ist der Punkt — dieselbe Wortform landet je nach Kontext an verschiedenen Stellen der Mannigfaltigkeit.

title: Wenn aus Gedanken Woerter werden (ganz einfach erklaert)
category_reason: Plain-language explainer of an LLM paper on latent semantic manifolds and the expressibility gap.
thesis: Language models 'think' in continuous latent number spaces but always output discrete words from a finite vocabulary; some thoughts never fit exactly into a word, leaving an unavoidable 'unsure zone' the paper calls the Expressibility Gap.
key_claims: The model organizes its data on thin 'sheets' (manifolds) — idea from Ansuini et al. 2019, confirmed for large transformers by Valeriani et al. 2023.
About 40-51% of word predictions fall in the 'unsure zone' (nearly equidistant between two words) across six real models from 124M to 1.5B parameters.
Larger models are on average slightly more confident, but the hardest ~5% of predictions stay equally hard for all models — because the language itself is ambiguous there, not the training.
To halve the error you need roughly 1000x more words, since the thought-space has ~20 effective degrees of freedom (error ~ (1/N)^(2/20)).
Language is a lossy compression of meaning (a map that always leaves something out); the named loss is the 'Expressibility Gap'.
Suggested uses: models could self-report 'I hesitate here', insert new subwords where the unsure zone is widest, and reframe some 'hallucinations' as thoughts sitting on a word boundary.
visualizations: Canvas 2D 'meadow of words': nearest-word Voronoi region with a gold boundary (unsure) zone; hover to read winner word, win-probability, and gap fraction; sliders for vocabulary size and temperature; all local in-browser.
internal_tensions: Admitted simplifications: the field is 2D vs ~20D real, words are randomly placed vs semantically placed, and the 'unsure zone' is measured by geometric distance vs the paper's margin.
The 'floor' that no technique can reach rests on the intrinsic-dimension / covering-rate argument applied to real language.

title: Neural Network Internal Topology: How Deep Layers Decode Superposition
category_reason: Mechanistische Interpretierbarkeit: Superposition, Fourier-Zerlegung, modular addition (mod 113), konstruktive Interferenz, Grokking — explizit über den internen Ablauf eines Transformer.
thesis: Tiefe Schichten dekodieren Superposition topologisch: Embeddings als Rotationen auf Kreisen (Homomorphismus Z/PZ → S¹, Produkt der Kreise = Torus), Fourier-Sparc bei wenigen Key-Frequenzen, Schichten berechnen a+b mod P über trigonometrische Identitäten, und die Antwort entsteht durch konstruktive Interferenz; Grokking ist drei kontinuierliche Phasen, angetrieben von Weight Decay.
key_claims: Das Embedding mappt a, b auf sin(w_k·a), cos(w_k·a), sin(w_k·b), cos(w_k·b) bei Key-Frequenzen w_k; der Kreis S¹ ist der fundamentale topologische Raum, das Produkt mehrerer Kreise ein Torus.

In einem trainierten Transformer (modular addition, mod 113) ist die Embedding-Matrix W_E Fourier-sparse: nur 5 Key-Frequenzen (k = 14, 35, 41, 42, 52) haben signifikante Norm; jedes Neuron operiert primär auf einer Frequenz.
Algorithmus: Embed → Attention+MLP (cos(w_k(a+b)), sin(w_k(a+b)) via trigonometrische Identitäten) → Unembed (cos(w_k(a+b−c))) → Interferenz; die Antwort ist c* = a+b mod P.
84,6 % der MLP-Neuronen lassen sich gut durch Grad-2-Polynome einer einzelnen Frequenz approximieren; jedes Neuron 'spezialisiert' sich auf eine Frequenz.
Konstruktive Interferenz: mehrere Cosinuswellen auf verschiedenen Key-Frequenzen peaken nur bei c* mod P; alle anderen Peaks heben sich durch destruktive Interferenz auf.
Ablation: Entfernen der Key-Frequenzen zerstört die Performance; das Entfernen aller ANDEREN Frequenzen verbessert sie sogar (Fourier-Multiplikations-Zirkuit).
Grokking läuft in drei Phasen: Memorization (0–1,4k Epochs) → Circuit Formation (1,4k–9,4k, Weight Decay treibt den Fourier-Zirkuit) → Cleanup (9,4k–14k, Test-Accuracy springt).

internal_tensions: Spezifisch auf modular addition (mod 113) — die Verallgemeinerung auf freie Sprache/natürliche Token ist offen.
Zwei Ebenen vermischt: 'From the Research' (echtes Paper mit echten Gewichten) vs didaktischer Nachbau mit simulierten Werten.
Das Ablation-Ergebnis (Nicht-Key-Frequenzen entfernen verbessert die Performance) ist kontraintuitiv und braucht den Fourier-Multiplikations-Zirkuit, um zu tragen.

title: Lineare Separierbarkeit in tiefen neuronalen Netzen — Interaktive Erkundung
category_reason: It is a German interactive explainer of a deep-learning paper (Zhang et al., arXiv:2307.13962, 2023) that measures per-layer linear separability of hidden-layer activations in deep neural networks and uses it to explain why larger nets generalize; the whole content is about neural nets, training, and generalization.
thesis: An interactive German walkthrough of Zhang et al. (arXiv:2307.13962, 2023): the paper asks whether the internal work of a deep network can be measured layer by layer, and answers yes by defining a geometric 'linear separability' (LS) of each hidden layer's activations, showing that training and separability rise in lockstep ('synchronicity'), and using random-matrix bounds to explain why deeper and wider nets generalize better even though classical VC/Rademacher theory predicts overfitting.
key_claims: The motivating gap: classical complexity theory (VC dimension, Rademacher) says large nets overfit, but practice shows large nets generalize better; the paper proposes a simple per-layer geometric measure — how well a hyperplane separates the two class clouds of a layer's activations.

Theorem 3: two sets A, B are linearly separable iff every point of the Minkowski difference MD(A,B) = {a_i - b_j} lies on one side of a hyperplane through the origin; the Minkowski-difference trick reduces 'two clouds, one separating line' to 'one cloud, one hyperplane through the origin'.

The MD-LSM gives four numeric LS measures: LS* (fraction of MD-points on the better side; NP-hard to optimize), LS_1 (ratio of absolute distances, in (0,1], 1 = perfectly separable), and LS_2 (squared; rewrites as a generalized eigenvalue problem with a closed, efficiently solvable form — the reason it is usable in practice); a cheap approximation sets MM^T = I so omega_hat = m_tilde/||m_tilde|| is just a sum, no eigendecomposition.

Theorem 1 (synchronicity): whenever training raises the training accuracy in an epoch, the linear separability of the hidden layer rises in the same epoch, and conversely; the per-layer LS curves track the accuracy curve, with deeper layers (closer to the output) showing higher LS.
Theorem 9: a purely linear transformation cannot change separability (only rotation/stretch); it is the non-linear activation that lets a net reorder the points and 'untangle' the classes.
Theorem 11: if F_sigma(x,y) > 2 then the activation moves MD-points from the minor side to the major side, i.e. it increases separability; sigmoid, tanh, arctan, and softsign all satisfy this.

Theorem 12 / Corollary 13 (random-matrix bounds): the probability that separability increases rises with width H (term H * exp(-LS_2^2 / 8 sigma^2) is linear in H but then dominated by the exponential once LS_2 is already high), so a wider or deeper net has a higher chance of increasing LS — the structural explanation for why bigger nets need not overfit.
Best linear classification accuracy is always >= LS* (Theorem 7), and all four measures are monotone in separability; the four measures are validated empirically on MLPs, CNNs, ResNets and ViTs.
