It is a visualization/interpretation piece, not a proof: the deep theorems are asserted and illustrated, and the claims are validated empirically rather than derived end-to-end here.

title: Topology for LLM Interpretability — Interactive Explorer
category_reason: Topologische Datenanalyse angewendet auf LLM-/Transformer-Interpretierbarkeit: persistente Homologie, Mapper, Mannigfaltigkeiten, Faserbündel, Morse-Theorie, Garben und Kohomologie als Werkzeuge, um die Geometrie der Hidden States zu verstehen.
thesis: Topologische Werkzeuge (persistente Homologie, Mapper, intrinsische Dimension, Faserbündel, Morse-Theorie, Garben, persistente Kohomologie) können die Geometrie der Hidden States von LLMs sichtbar machen und damit Interpretierbarkeit liefern — von zirkulären Merkmalen über Superposition bis zu globalen Inkonsistenzen (Halluzinationen).
key_claims: Persistente Homologie auf Aktivierungswolken: lange β₁-Balken → zirkulare Merkmale (Wochentage, Modulo-Arithmetik, Sentiment-Polarität); lange β₀ bei großem ε → gut getrennte semantische Cluster; Persistenz (Tod − Geburt) trennt Signal von Rauschen (entspricht den TDA-Papern von Anthropic und EleutherAI).

Mapper/Reeb-Graphen auf dem Residual-Stream zeigen Verzweigungen (Branching) in der syntaktischen Verarbeitung; informativer als UMAP, weil topologische Konnektivität (nicht nur lokale Distanzen) erhalten bleibt.

Intrinsische Dimension der Hidden States variiert pro Schicht: früh hoch (Roh-Tokens), mittig niedrig (Kompression/Abstraktion), spät wieder hoch (Dekompression für die Vorhersage) — ein Dimensionsprofil charakterisiert jede Schicht.

Residual-Stream als Faserbündel über Positionen; Attention = Verbindung (parallel Transport); Holonomie misst Pfadabhängigkeit — nicht-null Holonomie ↔ nicht-kommutierende Attention-Heads (bezieht sich auf Geometry of Truth, Marks et al.).

Morse-Theorie: Genauigkeit eines linearen Probes als Morse-Funktion; Sattelpunkte im Genauigkeits-Landscape = zwischen interpretierbaren Zuständen = wo Superposition lebt; gilt auch für das Loss-Landscape.

Garben auf dem Attention-Graph: dim(H⁰) = Information, auf der alle Tokens einig sind (globaler Kontext); dim(H¹) = Inkonsistenzen-Modi — lokal anwesend, global nicht vereinbar = genau das, was bei Halluzination passiert.

Superposition: N Merkmale in d<N Dimensionen; die Feature-Vektoren bilden Polytop-Geometrien je nach Sparsity (Anthropic); bei hoher Sparsity exponentiell viele Merkmale; Phasenübergänge zwischen Packungsgeometrien.

title: Nebeneffekte des Lernens aus niedrig-dimensionalen Daten
category_reason: ML-Theorie: interaktive Erklärung des Papers von He, Tsai & Ward (2023) 'Side Effects of Learning from Low-dimensional Data' (arXiv:2203.00614) – Mannigfaltigkeits-Hypothese, Off-Mannigfaltigkeits-Verhalten, Rauschen als Regularisierer, Tiefe, ReLU-Frostgewichte, Adversarial-Beispiele. Klarer KI-Bezug.
thesis: Wenn Daten auf einer niedrig-dimensionalen Mannigfaltigkeit M in einem hochdimensionalen Raum liegen, ist die Normalenableitung ∂f/∂n_M des gelernten Netzes prinzipiell unkontrolliert – Rauschen in Normalenrichtung und (in bestimmten Initialisierungsbereichen) Tiefe wirken als implizite Regularisierer, aber mit hohem Preis (superlineare Datenmenge, exponentielles Wachstum der Instabilität mit der Tiefe bei ReLU), was auch den geometrischen Grund für Adversarial-Beispiele liefert.
key_claims: Mannigfaltigkeits-Hypothese: reale Daten (z.B. 28×28-Bilder in ℝ^784) liegen auf einer niedrig-dimensionalen Mannigfaltigkeit M; die Labels hängen nur vom Punkt auf M ab, nicht von der Normalen-Komponente.
Die Normalenableitung ∂f/∂n_M ist von den Trainingsdaten überhaupt nicht bestimmt – bei σ=0 bleibt das Gewicht in Normalenrichtung genau an der Initialisierung (unkontrolliert).
Lineare Regression (Theorem 2.1): mit Rauschen σ gilt ‖w_y*‖~O(1/(σ√N)) – um Stabilität zu behalten, muss N~O(σ⁻²) superlinear wachsen.

Deep Linear Networks (Arora et al. 2018): der Flow ist in w nichtlinear (Faktor ‖w‖^{2−2/L} + Projektor), auch wenn das Netz linear ist; es gibt eine Slow-Manifold, und nahe w=0 kann die Entkommen-Zeit ~ε^{−2/(L−1)} dauern (Theorem 2.3).
Zwei Zeitskalen: w_x konvergiert schnell, w_y braucht ~1/σ² Iterationen – Training wird praktisch abgebrochen, bevor die Normalen-Stabilität erreicht ist.
Tiefe als impliziter Regularisierer (Theorem 2.4): in der Region U⁺ (außerhalb des Ellipsoids E) regularisiert größere Tiefe (‖w_y(T)‖ sinkt), in E⁻ (innerhalb) verstärkt sie die Instabilität.
ReLU (Lemma 3.1): bei σ=0 bleibt W_y¹ während des gesamten Trainings komplett unverändert ('eingefroren') – nur durch die Initialisierung bestimmt.

Adversarial-Verbindung: die 'unbenutzten' Normalen-Gewichte W_y¹ machen ReLU-Netze anfällig – winzige Perturbationen normal zur Mannigfaltigkeit können die Klassifikation umwerfen (MNIST-Demo, Fig. 3.1).
Theorem 3.2: die Instabilität wächst bei ReLU exponentiell mit der Tiefe (Produkt der Operator-Normen).
Trade-off (Gl. 4.4 & 4.5): Genauigkeit ~O(σ²)+O(N⁻¹) vs. Stabilität ~O(1/(σ²N^β)) mit β<1/2 für ReLU – der Trade-off ist härter als bei linearen Netzen.

Plotly: Verlustkurven (zwei Phasen/Zeitskalen)

Canvas: MNIST-Experiment (perturbiertes Bild, Heatmap I(s,t))

internal_tensions: Die Theorie ist für lineare Netze exakt, für ReLU-Nets aber nur durch Schranken (Theorem 3.2) – die Schranken sind konservativ und werden in der Praxis selten erreicht.
Der Trade-off 'Rauschen hilft Stabilität, aber schadet Genauigkeit' wird gezeigt, aber die optimale σ-Wahl für reale Daten (nicht synthetisch) bleibt offen.
Die 'frozen Weights'-These (Lemma 3.1) gilt bei σ=0 exakt; mit Rauschen wird W_y¹ trainierbar – der Übergang wird angedeutet, aber nicht quantitativ erfasst.

title: Minima Explorer — BasinHopper in 3D Loss Landscapes
category_reason: An English-language interactive 3D visualization of loss landscapes for neural network training, using the BasinHopper algorithm to explore the landscape and find local minima. The subject is ML optimization (loss landscape geometry, local minima, saddle points), which is squarely AI/ML.
thesis: An interactive English-language explorer for 3D loss landscapes: the user can define a loss function (e.g., a 2-parameter neural net loss, a Rosenbrock function, a random smooth function) and watch the BasinHopper algorithm (a stochastic global optimizer that combines Monte Carlo kicks with local minimization) explore the landscape, finding local minima and saddle points. The goal is to make the 'geometry' of the loss landscape visible: where the minima are, how deep they are, and how the optimizer navigates between them.
key_claims: A loss landscape L(w) for a neural network with parameters w is a function from R^d to R; for a 2-parameter net, L: R^2 -> R can be visualized as a 3D surface. The 'shape' of L(w) (number of minima, depth, curvature) determines the difficulty of training.

BasinHopper is a global optimization algorithm: it maintains a current point w, performs a local minimization (e.g., BFGS) from w to find the nearest local minimum w*, then takes a random 'kick' (a perturbation of size sigma) to a new point w' = w* + delta, and repeats. The kick size is adapted based on the acceptance rate (Metropolis-like).

The 'basin' of a local minimum w* is the set of all points that flow to w* under gradient descent; the basin boundary is the set of points that flow to different minima. The size and shape of the basins determine the 'robustness' of the training: a large, deep basin is 'easier' to find than a small, shallow one.

Saddle points (where the Hessian has both positive and negative eigenvalues) are critical points that are not minima; in high-dimensional loss landscapes, saddle points are more common than local minima (the 'saddle point problem'), and the optimizer must 'escape' them (e.g., by using momentum or a higher-order method).

The 'flat minimum' hypothesis: minima with a large 'flat region' (small Hessian eigenvalues) generalize better than 'sharp' minima (large Hessian eigenvalues); the visualizer can compute the Hessian at each found minimum and plot the eigenvalue spectrum.

The loss landscape is not a static object: it depends on the initialization, the batch size, the learning rate, and the architecture; the visualizer shows the landscape for a fixed architecture and initialization, but notes that the 'true' landscape is a family of landscapes parameterized by the training dynamics.
methods_math: multivariate calculus: gradient, Hessian, critical points, local minima/maxima/saddles
BasinHopper algorithm: Monte Carlo kicks + local minimization, adaptive kick size
BFGS quasi-Newton method for local minimization
basin of attraction, basin boundary, gradient flow
Hessian eigenvalue spectrum, flatness of minima, generalization
saddle points, escape dynamics, momentum/Adam as escape mechanisms
loss landscape as a function of architecture, initialization, batch size
global vs. local optimization, convergence guarantees, non-convexity
visualizations: 3D loss landscape surface: a 3D plot of L(w1, w2) for a 2-parameter net or a test function (Rosenbrock, Himmelblau, random smooth); the surface is colored by height (loss value), with local minima highlighted
BasinHopper trajectory: an animated path of the algorithm on the 2D contour plot of L(w1, w2); each 'kick' is shown as a dashed line, each local minimization as a solid line to the nearest minimum
basin boundary map: a 2D color map showing which minimum each point in the parameter space flows to under gradient descent; the basin boundaries are shown as lines
Hessian eigenvalue spectrum: for each found minimum, a bar chart of the Hessian eigenvalues; 'flat' minima (small eigenvalues) and 'sharp' minima (large eigenvalues) are clearly distinguishable

saddle point detector: a 2D contour plot with saddle points (where the Hessian is indefinite) highlighted in red; the user can click a saddle point to see the 'escape' trajectory under gradient descent with momentum
architecture comparison: two 3D landscapes side by side, one for a narrow net (2 hidden units) and one for a wide net (20 hidden units); the wide net landscape is 'smoother' with fewer sharp minima
internal_tensions: The 2D visualizations are necessarily reductive: real neural network loss landscapes have d = 10^4..10^7 parameters, and the geometry is very different (e.g., the 'mode connectivity' phenomenon: minima are connected by low-loss paths, which is not visible in 2D).

The BasinHopper algorithm is a global optimizer, but in practice neural networks are trained with stochastic gradient descent (SGD), which is a local optimizer with a very different noise structure; the file does not discuss the relationship between the two.
The 'flat minimum' hypothesis is stated but not proved; the connection between Hessian eigenvalues and generalization is an active research area, and the file presents it as established.

The file is a visualizer, not a theoretical treatment; the mathematical claims (basin boundaries, saddle point escape) are stated without proof, and the connection to the 'loss landscape conjectures' (e.g., the 'no spurious local minima' result for convex losses) is not discussed.

title: How a Neural Network Learns Addition on a Circle
category_reason: Neuronale Netze lernen Addition auf einem Kreis (modulare Arithmetik Z_P); die zugrunde liegende Gruppen-/Periodenstruktur wird per Fourierrechnung auf endlichen Gruppen analysiert. Klare KI-Kopplung (Grokking/Generalisierung).
thesis: Wenn ein neuronales Netz Addition modulo P (auf einem Kreis) lernt, überträgt es implizit die zugrunde liegende Gruppenstruktur Z_P; die Fourierrechnung auf der endlichen Gruppe zerlegt die Zielfunktion in Fourier-Moden, deren schrittweises Erscheinen das 'Eingrokked-Sein' (Übergang von Auswendiglernen zu verallgemeinernder Regel) erklärt.
key_claims: Addition auf Z_P ist eine periodische (kreisförmige) Funktion: das Netz muss die Wrapping-Struktur des Kreises lernen, nicht nur Punktpaare auswendig.
Die Fourierrechnung auf der endlichen Gruppe Z_P zerlegt jede Funktion in diskrete Fourier-Moden (Kardinalitäts-Charaktere der Gruppe).
Die Logit-Balkendarstellung über alle Kandidaten zeigt die Vorhersageverteilung des Netzes – bei Erfolg konzentriert sie sich auf den einzigen korrekten Summanden.
Generalisierung/Grokking: das Netz wechselt von reinem Memorisieren (interpoliert Trainingspaare) zur Anwendung der additiven Regel, wenn es die tiefen Fourier-Moden erfasst hat.
Die niedrigen Fourier-Moden (große Wellenlänge) werden zuerst gelernt; feinere Moden erscheinen später – eine Spektral-Bias-Dynamik.
Die Kreis-/Gruppenstruktur ist der Grund, warum das Problem für Netze 'grokkbar' ist: es ist eine endliche abelsche Gruppe mit klarer harmonischer Analyse.
visualizations: Kreis-/Kreislinie der Addition mod P
Logit-Balkendiagramm über alle Summanden-Kandidaten
Fourier-Moden-Darstellung (Welche Moden sind aktiv)

internal_tensions: Der 'Grokking'-Begriff wird verwendet, aber der Übergang wird nicht quantitativ (z.B. mit Generalisierungsfehler vs. Trainingszeit) belegt.
Die Fourierrechnung auf Z_P ist exakt für die lineare Zielfunktion; für reale Netze mit ReLU-Nichtlinearität ist die Spektral-Bias-Annahme eine Vereinfachung.
Ein einzelnes 1D-Beispiel (Addition mod P) wird als generelles Muster für 'Grokking' herangezogen – die Übertragbarkeit auf andere Aufgaben bleibt behauptet.

title: Vektor-Alchemie: Semantische Navigation im Latent Space
category_reason: A toy 'latent-space' model where German words are 3D vectors and 'mood/formality/era/intensity' joystick sliders steer a target vector that re-weights the next-token distribution.
thesis: Meaning is a coordinate: words are points in a (hand-built) 3D latent space with axes like mood/formality/era/intensity, and moving a 'latent joystick' changes a target vector whose direction re-scores (via a softmax over relevance) which word is most likely next — a concrete, steerable picture of how vector arithmetic in an embedding space selects the next token.
key_claims: Each word is a 3D vector with scalar features (mood, formality, era, intensity) added to a base position; the embedding space is hand-authored, not learned.
A 'target vector' is set by four sliders (mood, formality, era, intensity); each word's relevance is the dot product of its feature vector with the target direction.
The next-token distribution is a temperature-scaled (x3) softmax over those relevances; the top-10 words are shown as a ranked probability bar list.
The overarching claim is that 'meaning is a coordinate' — a sentence's character can be navigated by moving a vector through this semantic space.
visualizations: Plotly 3D scatter of ~40 words colored/sized by relevance + a target-vector arrow from the origin; 4 sliders + a sentence input; and a live top-10 next-token probability bar panel
internal_tensions: The 'latent space' is entirely hand-built with a few human-chosen axes (mood/formality/era/intensity), so the 'semantic navigation' demonstrates the concept of vector arithmetic but is not a real language model's latent space.
The input sentence only affects the target vector via a proxy formula (sentenceX/Y/Z) rather than the words of the sentence — so 'project the sentence' is largely cosmetic.

title: Coherent Difference — Interaktiv
category_reason: An interactive German-language exploration of how a coherent space (and meaning within it) emerges from local differences, with an explicit 'Embedding-Raum' section on word meaning as position in a relational space. The overall framework — local differences gluing into a global coherent space — is the mathematical foundation of representation learning and embedding-based models.
thesis: An interactive German-language exploration of 'Coherent Difference' in eight steps: how a space (and meaning within it) emerges from local differences rather than from a pre-existing container. The steps range from Spencer-Brown's primitive act of drawing a distinction, through topology without metric, sheaf gluing, homotopy as coherence-without-equality, to an embedding space where word meaning is its position in the network of differences, and finally the train-at-the-platform as a phenomenological synthesis.
key_claims: Distinktion (Spencer-Brown): before anything is, a boundary must be drawn; every distinction creates an inside and an outside — all mathematics begins with this act of differentiation.

Lokalität ohne Metrik: a topological space does not require distances or coordinates; it is a set of points plus the specification of which subsets are 'open' (neighborhoods). Two points are 'near' if every neighborhood of one also contains the other.

Gluing (Sheaf): two observers see parts of the world; their views must agree on the overlap for a coherent global picture to exist. The sheaf axiom in one sentence: if local data agree on overlaps, there exists exactly one global extension.

Kohärenz statt Gleichheit: lightning and thunder are not equal — they are coherently connected (by a time delay). Two things need not be identical to belong together; it suffices that there is a continuous deformation (homotopy) between them.

Embedding-Raum: words have no meaning in themselves; their meaning is their position in the network of differences to all other words. The space is not a container that words occupy — the space IS the pattern of their relations.

Der Zug am Bahnsteig: a train is not 'behind' its appearances (sight, sound, touch, spatial presence) — it IS the coherent network of its appearances. Each sensory modality is a 'face' of the same underlying event, related by coherence, not identity.

The whole document is a chain of eight steps, each clicking on the previous: distinction → locality → gluing → coherence → embedding → phenomenology, building from the simplest possible act (drawing a line) to a full account of how a 'world' emerges from local differences.

internal_tensions: The eight steps cover an enormous range (philosophy, topology, algebraic geometry, machine learning, phenomenology) in a single file; each step is interactive but shallow, and the connecting logic between steps is asserted rather than argued.

The 'Embedding-Raum' section is the most directly AI-relevant (word embeddings, relational meaning), but it is presented as a philosophical claim ('the space IS the pattern of their relations') rather than a technical one; the connection to actual embedding-based models (word2vec, BERT) is not made.

The Spencer-Brown starting point is provocative but potentially misleading: 'all mathematics begins with a distinction' is a philosophical claim, not a mathematical one; the file does not address the objection that mathematics also requires composition, iteration, and quantification, not just distinction.

The train metaphor in the final step is poetic but underdeveloped: the file does not explain how the 'coherent network of appearances' is formally specified, or how this differs from the sheaf-theoretic gluing in step 3.

title: Neuronale Netze — Aha-Explorator aus kategorialer und physikalischer Perspektive
category_reason: An interactive German-language 'aha-explorer' that explains neural networks from a categorical (functors, natural transformations) and physical (energy landscapes, gradient flow) perspective. The main subject is the mathematical structure of neural networks, which is squarely AI/ML.
thesis: An interactive German-language 'aha-explorer' that reframes neural networks in two complementary languages: (1) categorical — a neural net is a functor from a category of input spaces to a category of output spaces, with layers as functors and activations as natural transformations; (2) physical — the training dynamics is a gradient flow on an energy landscape, and the network's function is a path through configuration space. The goal is to give the reader 'aha' moments by showing the same network in both lights simultaneously.
key_claims: A feedforward neural net can be viewed as a functor F: C -> D where C is a category of input distributions/spaces and D is a category of output distributions; each layer is a functor, and the composition is the whole network.
Activations (ReLU, sigmoid, etc.) are natural transformations between the 'linear map' functor and the 'nonlinear map' functor: they commute with reparametrizations of the input space.
The loss landscape L(w) is a potential energy function on the parameter space; gradient descent is the overdamped Newton equation dw/dt = -grad(L), and the network 'settles' into a local minimum.
The width of a network (number of neurons per layer) corresponds to the dimension of the configuration space; wider networks have more 'degrees of freedom' and can represent more complex functions.

The 'aha' insight: the same network can be read as (a) a categorical composition of functors (structural view) or (b) a physical system relaxing to an energy minimum (dynamic view); the two perspectives are dual in the sense that the categorical structure determines the landscape's topology.

Overfitting corresponds to the network finding a very narrow, deep minimum (high curvature) rather than a broad, shallow one; regularization (weight decay, dropout) modifies the landscape to favor broader minima.
methods_math: category theory: categories, functors, natural transformations, composition
universal algebra: monoids of compositions, free monoids on layer maps
gradient flow as an ODE, Lyapunov stability of minima
energy landscapes, Hessian matrix, curvature at critical points
Hessian eigenvalue distribution as a proxy for generalization
parameter-space dimensionality and its relation to function class capacity
regularization as a landscape modification (ridge, L1, dropout as stochastic noise)
visualizations: dual-view panel: left side shows a 2-layer net as a commutative diagram (categorical view), right side shows the same net as a 2D energy landscape with a ball rolling to the minimum (physical view); the two panels are synchronized
activation-function slider: watch the commutative diagram deform as the activation changes from linear to ReLU to sigmoid, with the natural-transparency condition highlighted

Hessian eigenvalue spectrum plot: for a trained 2-layer net, show the eigenvalues of the Hessian at the found minimum; a 'broad vs. narrow' toggle changes the regularization strength and updates the spectrum
width-vs-capacity plot: a 2D function (e.g., XOR, sine, Gaussian mixture) with a slider for network width; the approximation quality and the landscape's 'roughness' update in real time
gradient-flow animation: a particle following the gradient on a 2D slice of the loss landscape, with the velocity field shown as arrows; the user can pause at any point to inspect the local Hessian
internal_tensions: The categorical framing is mathematically elegant but arguably over-abstract for a practical ML audience; the 'aha' moments depend on the reader already knowing category theory, which limits the intended audience.

The physical framing (energy landscape) is standard in NN theory, but the claim that 'categorical structure determines landscape topology' is strong and not well-supported in the literature; the file presents it as an open conjecture.

The 2D landscape visualizations are necessarily reductive: real loss landscapes in high-dimensional parameter space have a very different geometry (mode connectivity, loss surfaces that are not bowl-shaped).
The file is an 'explorator' (draft), not a finished exposition; several sections are sketched rather than fully worked out, and the categorical/physical duality is asserted more than proved.

title: Neural Networks as Sheaves: Gluing Local Approximations
category_reason: Math FOR AI: interprets a ReLU neural network (function approximation + SGD training) through sheaf gluing — local affine sections glued by the optimizer.
thesis: A ReLU network is a machine for constructing piecewise-linear sheaves: each neuron is an affine local section, each ReLU is a restriction map (folding ℝ into U⁺/U⁻), the output layer is the gluing axiom (weighted sum = global section), and the optimizer is the gluing morphism that nudges the local pieces until they are globally compatible with the data.
key_claims: Each hidden neuron computes an affine map z_j = w_j·x + b_j — a 'local section' of a sheaf on ℝ.
ReLU partitions ℝ into open sets U_j⁺={w_j x+b_j>0} and U_j⁻={w_j x+b_j<0}; on U⁺ the section is the affine function, on U⁻ it is 0; the bend is the 'gluing locus'.
The output ŷ(x)=Σ_j α_j·ReLU(w_j x+b_j)+β is the sheaf gluing axiom in action: compatible local sections assemble into a unique global section.

The loss + gradient-descent optimizer enforces compatibility (adjusts slopes, offsets, combination weights) — the 'gluing morphism' that reduces the discrepancy between the assembled global section and the target.
More neurons = finer open cover = better approximation (function approximation).

Concept map: open cover = regions where each ReLU is active/inactive; local section = affine piece; restriction map = ReLU; gluing axiom = output-layer weighted sum; gluing morphism/cocycle = optimizer.
methods_math: sheaves (open covers, local sections, restriction maps, gluing axiom)
visualizations: Canvas 2D: (3) a single ReLU neuron hinge with w,b,α sliders marking the bend point; (4) N bent pieces (faint) summed to a global curve against targets sin/|x|/step/bump, with neuron-count and target selectors; (5) live training — a ReLU net fit to sin(1.5x) with a function-approximation canvas and a loss curve, live epoch/loss readout, neuron-count and learning-rate sliders. Temml-rendered equations.
internal_tensions: The sheaf correspondence is structural analogy rather than theorem: ReLU 'restriction' and the output 'gluing' do not satisfy the literal sheaf axioms (no restriction maps between overlapping covers are defined, no Cech cocycles are formed).
The optimizer as 'gluing morphism' is a metaphor for weight updates; it does not compute an actual gluing datum or cocycle.

Directly comparable/contrasting with simplicial_complex_attention4 (which applies sheaves to attention) and with universal-approximation literature — the 'finer cover = better approximation' line echoes universal approximation but without its rate guarantees.

thesis: Feed-forward ReLU networks achieve linear separability by progressively folding the data manifold into unused higher dimensions — each layer folds what the previous layer has folded, exponentially increasing the number of linear regions; the final layer is the 'single straight cut' (Fold-and-Cut Theorem connection). Bimodal tuning curves are the fingerprint of active folds.

ReLU is the 'hammer blow' — it can only affect the convex hull, not selectively reach interior points
Folding (Origami in N dimensions) is the primary efficient method when layers are wider than the data dimension
Shear (peeling) is the inefficient alternative for narrow layers, requiring very deep networks
Each layer multiplies the number of linear regions (exponential in depth): N^L regions for L layers of width N
Bimodal tuning curves (dip at zero in preactivation histogram) are the fingerprint of a fold separating a class
Causality test: silencing 10 bimodal neurons collapses accuracy; silencing 10 unimodal neurons has minimal effect

title: Kohärente Weltmodelle — Eine interaktive Reise
category_reason: Sheaf-Theorie, Descent und ∞-Stacks als mathematisches Framework für Kohärenz in LLM-Weltmodellen; Origami/ReLU-Falten (Keup & Helias 2022) als konkretes Descent-Beispiel; Modellkollaps als Überdeckungs-Theorie-Phänomen.
thesis: Kohärenz — philosophisch (Bradley, Blanshard, BonJour) und mathematisch (Descent, Sheaves, ∞-Stacks) — ist die fundamentale Struktur, die ein LLM-Weltmodell zusammenhält; das Falten von ReLU-Netzen (Origami, Keup & Helias 2022) ist ein konkretes Descent-Phänomen, und der Zusammenbruch der Kohärenz (Modellkollaps) lässt sich als Versagen der Überdeckungstheorie formalisieren.
key_claims: Ein Sheaf über einer Kategorie kodiert 'lokale Daten, die sich global verkleben lassen' — genau die Struktur, die ein kohärentes Weltmodell braucht.
Descent (Warendt): wenn lokale Informationen global verträglich sind, existiert ein globales Objekt — die formale Aussage dahinter, dass ein LLM 'zusammenhält'.
ReLU-Netzwerke falten den Raum (Origami-Interpretation, Keup & Helias 2022): jede ReLU-Schicht ist eine piecewise-lineare 'Falte', und die Komposition aller Falten ist ein Descent-Problem.
Modellkollaps entsteht, wenn die trainierende Überdeckung zu dünn wird: lokal kohärente Fragmente lassen sich nicht mehr global verkleben.
Sellars' 'Raum der Gründe' (space of reasons) ist informell eine Kategorie; ein LLM-Weltmodell ist ein Sheaf auf dieser Kategorie.
Fünf Pathologien (Halluzination, Inkohärenz, Konfabulation, Kontextverlust, Zielverschiebung) entsprechen dem Versagen verschiedener Axiome der Sheaf-Struktur.
Wahrheit = Kohärenz + Korrespondenz: ein Sheaf mit zusätzlichem 'Correspondence'-Träger ist ein 'verankertes' Weltmodell.
∞-Stacks generalisieren Sheaves auf Homotopie-Ebene und modellieren die 'Tiefe' von Weltmodellen (mehrschichtige Kohärenz).

title: Transformer Layers as Space-Morphing Maps — Interactive Explorer
category_reason: Transformer-Geometrie: Layer als Faser-Bündel-Morphismen / Space-Morphing, Jacobian-Zerlegung (Divergenz/Curl/Shear), Coq-verifizierte Eigenschaften (Norman Koch, April 2026).
thesis: Transformer-Schichten 'bewegen' Token-Vektoren nicht, sondern verzerren den Repräsentationsraum (Space-Morphing / Faser-Bündel-Morphismus); der lokale Verzug wird vom Jacobian beschrieben, das Coq-verifiziert in einen symmetrischen (Stretch/Shear/Divergenz) und einen antisymmetrischen (Rotation/Curl) Teil zerfällt.
key_claims: Gleiche Endlage, andere Interpretation: 'point moves' (traditionell) vs 'space warps' (neu) — die Schicht formt den gesamten Raum, der Punkt reitet nur mit.
Faser-Bündel: Base = Token-Positionen {1..n}, Faser = Repräsentation je Schicht (wie Etagen), Layer-Map = 'Aufzug' zwischen Etagen.
Das Jacobian J zerfällt in J_sym + J_antisym; 10 Eigenschaften sind in Coq verifiziert (z.B. J_antisym antisymmetrisch und trace-free, ⟨J_sym,J_antisym⟩_F = 0, Divergenz kommt nur vom Strain).
Divergenz = tr(J) (Expansion/Kontraktion), Curl = Rotation (trace-free), Shear = spurlöser symmetrischer Teil (reine Formänderung ohne Volumenänderung), Determinante = Volumenänderung.
Residual-Stream: h[l+1] = h[l] + Δ[l]; J = I + J_Δ; verifiziert tr(I + J_Δ) = n + tr(J_Δ).
Inner Layers machen die schwerste Arbeit — Layer-Activity-Profil low→high→low, letzte Schicht zeigt oft eine 'Reversal' (un-warps den Raum zurück).
Holographische Distribution/Polysemantik: Konzepte sind über viele Neuronen/Schichten verteilt; Entfernen von Dimensionen degradiert graceful (wie ein geschnittenes Hologramm), nicht katastrophal.

title: AttentionViz — Interaktive Erklärun (Yeh et al. 2023)
category_reason: Explains a transformer-attention interpretability tool (joint Q/K embedding, global head view).
thesis: AttentionViz projects Queries and Keys into a shared 2D space so that nearby points mean high attention, giving a global (matrix) view of what each head generally does across thousands of examples, instead of one sentence at a time.
key_claims: Attention depends on the Q-K dot product, which is closely related to distance, so nearby points in the plot correspond to high attention — the head's shape becomes a visual signature.
Trick 1 (Key-Translation): softmax is translation-invariant, so all keys can be shifted by a constant vector without changing attention, letting the two clouds be centered together.
Trick 2 (QK-Skalierung): scaling queries by c and keys by 1/c preserves the dot product but changes visual distance; c is chosen so distance correlates optimally with attention.
Empirically in BERT the average Spearman correlation between Query-Key distance and dot product is about -0.938 (near-perfect negative).

Findings: BERT heads show 'positional spirals' and semantic clusters; ViT heads sort patches by brightness, hue, and frequency/angle; GPT-2 shows an 'attend-to-first' anomaly with large Query/Key norm differences (~ -4.6 average).
Builds on Activation Atlas (Carter et al.), t-SNE/UMAP/PCA, and BertViz (Vig 2019).
visualizations: Canvas attention demo (drag a query; circle size = attention to each key), a trick canvas with translation/scale sliders to mix the Q/K clouds, a Plotly distance-vs-dot-product scatter, a canvas morph between a positional spiral and semantic clusters, and a Plotly ViT hue/frequency scatter; Temml for the equations.
internal_tensions: Distance is a proxy for attention (a correlation, not an identity); the 'nahe Punkte = hohe Attention' claim is approximate.
Several plots (e.g. the -0.94 correlation) use simulated/illustrative data in this page even though the paper reports real BERT numbers.

title: Interactive Explainer: Geometric Structure of Layer Updates
category_reason: Main subject is the geometric structure of how representations change from layer to layer in deep language models (Pythia, Mamba, DistilGPT2) — a core LLM interpretability topic.
thesis: Each layer update in a deep language model decomposes into a 'tokenwise' component (a local, input-conditioned linear map applied to each token independently) and a 'residual' component; the full update is almost perfectly aligned with the tokenwise part, while the residual — though small in norm — points in a geometrically distinct direction and is where the functionally important computation lives, as evidenced by its strong correlation with output-perturbation (KL divergence).
key_claims: The layer update h_{ℓ+1} − h_ℓ decomposes as T(h_ℓ) + r(h_ℓ), where T is a local, input-conditioned tokenwise map (locally linear, globally nonlinear) and r is the residual.
The full update is nearly parallel to the tokenwise component: angular deviation is typically < 10°, while the residual often exceeds 60° from the tokenwise direction.
When the tokenwise approximation is poor (large residual), the model's output changes significantly: Spearman ρ between approximation error and KL output deviation is 0.80–0.91 for Pythia models.
The full and tokenwise updates live in a low-dimensional subspace (well-captured by 1–8 top singular vectors), while the residual is spread across many more dimensions.

These geometric properties hold across architectures: both Transformers (Pythia, DistilGPT2) and state-space models (Mamba) show the same tokenwise/residual separation, even though Mamba has no attention mechanism.

title: FlatNet: Manifold Flattening & Reconstruction — Visual Guide
category_reason: An interactive visual guide to FlatNet, a white-box autoencoder that flattens curved data manifolds layer-by-layer using local differential geometry. The entire subject is representation learning / autoencoding, a core ML task.
thesis: An interactive English-language visual tour of FlatNet (JMLR 2024, Psenka et al.): a white-box autoencoder that constructs encoder/decoder layers greedily — no backprop — by using a local quadratic model (the second fundamental form) to peel off curvature one wrinkle at a time, with intrinsic dimension and network depth discovered automatically.
key_claims: Real-world data sits on a curved low-dimensional manifold inside a high-dimensional space; FlatNet uncurls this surface into a flat affine plane where PCA becomes trivial.
Theorem 6: if (φ, ψ) flatten the manifold M, then φ(M) is a convex subset of a d-dimensional affine subspace — so PCA on top of φ gives the minimal encoder for free.

Around any point x₀, the manifold is modeled as x₀ + v + ½·II_{x₀}(v,v), where II is the second fundamental form (extrinsic curvature); projecting onto the tangent plane removes the curvature term, which is the local flattening step.
Local flattenings are glued globally via a partition of unity (smooth Gaussian weights), so each layer is well-defined on the whole dataset.
Iterating local flattenings acts as a convexification flow: each layer nudges points toward the local mean (inside the convex hull), and the manifold uncurls into a flat plane.

The algorithm is O(N·D·d²) per layer — linear in samples and ambient dimension, polynomial only in intrinsic dimension — and uses Stiefel-manifold optimization for the tangent basis plus closed-form least squares for the curvature tensor.

FlatNet is genuinely new vs. VAEs (no backprop, provably flat latent space, auto-discovered dimension) and vs. classical manifold learning (t-SNE, ISOMAP): it has explicit encoder/decoder maps (out-of-sample works) and uses second-order geometry, not just first-order distances.

PCA as minimal compression of a flat affine subspace

internal_tensions: The method assumes the manifold is connected and flattenable; it fails on closed-loop manifolds (e.g., rotation groups) and struggles with self-colliding hypersurfaces (Swiss roll) where compression causes overlap.
The single-manifold assumption is a significant limitation: multi-class data (e.g., MNIST digits) requires a mixture-of-manifolds treatment that is left as future work.

The 'white-box, no backprop' framing is compelling but the per-layer greedy construction may miss globally optimal flattenings; the convexification flow convergence is visualized but not proved in the guide.

The guide is a visual tour of a published paper (JMLR 2024), so the mathematical claims (Theorem 6, convexity certificate) are stated but not proved in this file; the reader must trust the paper for the proofs.

The incommensurate frequencies make the helix never self-intersect (like irrational rotations on a torus giving dense non-repeating orbits), so every position is uniquely encoded
tanh/sigmoid positional encodings would fail because they lack the rotation property (there is no matrix M_k with tanh(pos+k)=M_k·tanh(pos)), so the model could not generalize relative distances

title: RoPE 3D Slice Visualizer (1-64D)
category_reason: An interactive 3D visualizer for Rotary Position Embeddings (RoPE), a core positional-encoding mechanism used in modern transformer architectures (LLaMA, etc.). The entire subject is a transformer component, which is directly AI/ML.
thesis: An interactive German-language 3D visualizer for Rotary Position Embeddings (RoPE): the user selects dimension pairs, sets input values (x₁, x₂), the base frequency, and the number of positions, then watches how the RoPE rotation matrix acts on the embedding in 2D, 3D, or multi-slice views, with an animation mode that sweeps positions from 0 to 199. The key insight is that RoPE encodes position as an independent 2D rotation in each dimension pair, with a geometrically spaced frequency spectrum.
key_claims: RoPE encodes position as a rotation in 2D subspaces: for dimension pair i, the rotation angle is position × θᵢ, where θᵢ = base^(-2i/d) (a geometrically decreasing frequency spectrum).
The rotation is applied independently to each dimension pair: the full d-dimensional RoPE is a block-diagonal matrix of d/2 independent 2D rotations, each with its own frequency.

Higher-index dimension pairs have lower frequencies (longer wavelengths) and thus encode slower-varying positional information; lower-index pairs have higher frequencies and encode fine-grained position.

The 3D view shows how multiple dimension pairs' rotations compose: each pair traces a circle (or ellipse, depending on x₁, x₂) in its own 2D subspace, and the full embedding is the composition of all these rotations.
The multi-slice mode shows several dimension pairs simultaneously, making the frequency spectrum visible: low-index pairs rotate fast (tight circles), high-index pairs rotate slow (wide circles).
The animation mode sweeps the position from 0 to 199, showing how the embedding point traces a path in the high-dimensional space as the position changes.
methods_math: Rotary Position Embedding (RoPE): x'ᵢ = xᵢ·cos(pos·θᵢ) - xᵢ₊₁·sin(pos·θᵢ), x'ᵢ₊₁ = xᵢ·sin(pos·θᵢ) + xᵢ₊₁·cos(pos·θᵢ)
position encoding as a function of token index
base frequency parameter (controls the frequency range)
visualizations: 2D mode: a single dimension pair's rotation shown as a point moving on a circle in the (x₁, x₂) plane as position changes
3D mode: multiple dimension pairs' rotations composed in 3D space; the embedding point traces a helical path
Multi-slice mode: several dimension pairs shown simultaneously in parallel 2D slices, making the frequency spectrum visible
Controls: x₁, x₂ input fields, base frequency slider, position count slider, max dimension selector (8D/16D/32D/64D/128D)
Animation: '▶ Animieren' button sweeps position from 0 to 199; 'Aktualisieren' (update) for static view
Dimension pair selector: choose which pairs to display in the current mode
internal_tensions: The visualizer shows the RoPE rotation in isolation; it does not show how RoPE interacts with the attention mechanism (the key insight of RoPE is that it makes the attention score depend only on the relative position, not the absolute position).
The 2D/3D views are necessarily reductive: a 64D RoPE is a composition of 32 independent 2D rotations in a 64D space, and the 3D projection loses most of the structure.
The file does not compare RoPE to other positional encodings (sinusoidal, learned, ALiBi); the reader sees how RoPE works but not why it was chosen over alternatives.

The 'Max Dim' selector goes up to 128D, but the animation only sweeps to position 199; for real transformer context lengths (4K, 8K, 128K), the behavior of RoPE at very long positions (frequency aliasing, extrapolation) is not explored.

title: Interactive Coq Proof Explorer: Transformer Jacobian Geometry — Deep Dive
category_reason: Machine-checked (Coq) geometry of the Jacobian matrix of a single transformer layer — the subject is the mathematics of transformers (Jacobian decomposition, residual connections), i.e. math-for-AI.
thesis: The Jacobian matrix of a transformer layer obeys a small set of exact, machine-checked geometric laws — decomposition into symmetric and antisymmetric parts, trace as divergence, Frobenius orthogonality of the two parts, idempotence of the symmetrization, the shear tensor being trace-free, the residual connection giving J = I + delta, trace cyclicity, and invariance under orthogonal similarity — and all ten bundle into a single conjunction transformer_jacobian_geometry_complete.
key_claims: Every layer Jacobian splits uniquely into a symmetric and an antisymmetric part (J = S + A).
The trace of the Jacobian is its divergence; trace is a first-order local quantity.
The symmetric and antisymmetric parts are Frobenius-orthogonal (their inner product is zero).
Symmetrization (J + J^T)/2 is idempotent: applying it twice is the same as applying it once.
The shear (antisymmetric) tensor is trace-free.
A residual connection gives J = I + delta, so the identity is the background and the layer adds a perturbation.
The trace is cyclic: trace(AB) = trace(BA).
The spectral/geometric facts are invariant under orthogonal similarity transforms.
All ten theorems are machine-checked in Coq and combine into one conjunction transformer_jacobian_geometry_complete.
methods_math: Jacobian matrix analysis of a single transformer layer
Frobenius inner product and orthogonality of S and A
trace-free property of the shear/antisymmetric tensor
formal verification / machine-checked proofs in Coq
visualizations: Interactive Coq proof explorer: expandable steps for each of the ten theorems
Plotly + canvas rotation-invariance demo (orthogonal similarity)
Grand-Summary view bundling all ten theorems into one conjunction
internal_tensions: The results are exact for the abstract linear layer Jacobian; their transfer to real, trained, non-linear transformer layers is asserted, not measured.
Ten individually elementary theorems are packaged as a 'complete geometry', which can overstate how much structure a single layer's Jacobian actually carries.
Formal verification certifies the stated lemmas, not the adequacy of the linear-Jacobian model as a picture of transformer dynamics.

title: Attention — Watch It Work

thesis: An interactive single-token attention flow: watch how a chosen query token aligns most with one key (smallest angle, highest weight) so its output is pulled toward that key's V vector; twisting the W_Q/W_K/W_V 'rotations' changes what counts as relevant versus what gets read.

Q, K, and V are rotations of the same 2D token embeddings, controlled by W_Q / W_K / W_V twist sliders.
The query aligns most with the key whose angle to Q is smallest, giving it the largest weight and pulling the output toward that key's V vector.
Twisting W_Q / W_K changes what counts as relevant (the matching); twisting W_V changes what gets read (the content).
The 'focus' slider acts as softmax temperature, sharpening or flattening the weights.

internal_tensions: The projection matrices are restricted to 2D rotations of hand-picked embeddings rather than learned, full-rank matrices.
A single query and single head are shown, so it illustrates the mechanics but not multi-head composition.

title: What Attention Actually Does — Geometrically
category_reason: Explains transformer self-attention (Q,K,V, softmax, multi-head) geometrically.
thesis: Attention is not a surface or simplicial complex but a data-dependent convex combination of value vectors: Q·K measures angular alignment in a query-key subspace, softmax maps the scores onto the probability simplex, and the output is a weighted centroid inside the convex hull of the V vectors.
key_claims: Attention does NOT lay a surface or a simplicial complex — it computes a convex combination of value vectors with position determined by query-key similarity.
score(i,j) = q_i·k_j/√d_k = |q_i||k_j|cos(θ_ij)/√d_k, i.e. Q·K is scaled cosine similarity (angular alignment).
The √d_k factor normalizes the dot product (variance d_k for unit-variance random vectors) so softmax does not saturate — a geometric rescaling to keep angles meaningful.
Softmax first exponentiates, amplifying differences (3 vs 1 → e³:e¹ ≈ 20:2.7), so attention is either diffuse or concentrated; the temperature is 1/√d_k.
Every attention pattern is a point on the (n-1)-simplex Δⁿ⁻¹; vertices = hard attention (copy one token), center = uniform average.
out_i = Σ_j softmax(q_i·k_j/√d_k)·v_j — a weighted centroid in the convex hull of {v_j}; attention interpolates between copying and averaging.
Multi-head = multiple independent (Q,K,V) triples in different subspaces, concatenated — attend to different things simultaneously.
visualizations: Canvas 2D, four scenes: (1) tokens with convex hull of V vectors and animated attention lines + moving output centroid; (2) unit circle in Q-K subspace with selectable query and per-key cosine bars; (3) 2-simplex (probability triangle) with the softmax point; (4) draggable V points + weight sliders tracking the output point inside the convex hull.
internal_tensions: Explicitly rejects a topological/simplicial reading of attention ('does NOT lay a surface or a simplicial complex') — directly in tension with the simplicial-complex/nerve accounts (e.g. simplicial_complex_attention4, simplicial_complex_attention*).
Uses idealized, hand-set Q/K/V and a single illustrative sentence rather than a trained model, so it is a pedagogical model of the mechanism, not empirical evidence.
Frames √d_k as 'just a geometric rescaling' — glosses over the deeper role of scaling in gradient/temperature behavior.

title: Random Hierarchy Model · Interaktives Paper-Erlebnis

Minimales Parametervolumen P* = n_c · m^L = n_c · d^(ln m/ln s) — polynomial in d (d = m^L · s^L).

Mechanismus: Zählen von Korrelationen — obere Schichten summieren über die Synonyme der unteren Schicht.
Die Skalierung erklärt, warum Tiefe für kompositorische Daten so effektiv ist: log-Verhalten statt exponentiell.
Validiert an synthetischen hierarchischen Datensätzen und (teilweise) an Bilderkennung.

title: ROME – Fakten in GPT lokalisieren und editieren
category_reason: A German-language interactive walkthrough of the ROME paper (Meng, Bau, Andonian & Belinkov 2022): locating factual associations in GPT via causal tracing (indirect effects on hidden states) and editing them with a single rank-one MLP weight update. Core transformer interpretability and model editing.
thesis: A German-language interactive walkthrough of the ROME paper (Meng, Bau, Andonian & Belinkov 2022): how to locate where GPT stores factual associations (via causal tracing — measuring indirect effects on hidden states across the layer/token grid) and how to edit them with a single rank-one weight update to an MLP layer, replacing a fact (e.g., 'Space Needle is in Seattle' → 'Paris') without destroying the rest of the model.
key_claims: A transformer's hidden states h(l,i) form a grid indexed by layer l and token position i; each cell combines an attention contribution (looking at earlier tokens) and an MLP contribution (local computation).

Causal tracing measures the indirect effect of a hidden state: corrupt the input, then patch only state h(l,i) to its clean value; the recovery of P(target token) measures how much information flows through that state.
Causal tracing identifies two 'bright zones': the 'early site' (middle layers at the last subject token, primarily in the MLP) and the 'late site' (last layers at the last token).
Factual knowledge is stored primarily in MLP layers, not attention layers — the MLP acts as a key-value memory.
ROME (Rank-One Model Editing): a single rank-one update to one MLP weight matrix W₂ can replace a fact while preserving performance on all other facts.
The edit is computed as a closed-form solution to a constrained optimization: minimize the change to the weight matrix subject to the model producing the new answer for the target fact.

evaluation plots (target fact accuracy vs. side effects)
internal_tensions: The file presents ROME as a clean 'find and replace' for facts, but the actual paper reports side effects (performance drops on related facts) and notes that the 'early site' is not always the MLP; the simplified narrative may overstate the precision and generality of the method.

title: ROME — Wo ein Sprachmodell seine Fakten aufbewahrt
category_reason: Explains a mechanistic-interpretability / model-editing paper (ROME, Meng, Bau, Andonian, Belinkov — NeurIPS 2022, arXiv:2202.05262) about locating and editing factual associations inside GPT transformers.
thesis: Factual knowledge in a transformer is stored as linear associative memories in the MLP layers (W_proj acts as a key→value store keyed by the last subject token). Causal tracing localizes each (subject, relation, object) fact to two 'hot spots' — a mid-MLP write at the last subject token and a late attention read. ROME then rewrites a single fact with a rank-1 weight edit ΔW = Λ·u·vᵀ that routes a new answer v* to the subject's key u, under a Lagrange constraint that keeps the rest of the model's behavior intact; a harmonic-mean COUNTERFACT score (five tests, including neighbor-subject generalization) verifies the edit.
key_claims: A 'fact' for the model is an association (s, r, o): subject → relation → object.
Causal tracing (three passes: no masking, mask the MLPs, mask the attention) yields a heatmap that localizes the fact to two hot spots.
Hot spot 1 (the new finding): a mid-layer MLP writing the object at the LAST subject token; hot spot 2: a late attention layer reading it.
The MLP is a linear associative memory: W_proj stores key→value pairs — the write direction is the key, the projected direction the value.
The edit is rank-1: ΔW = Λ·u·vᵀ, with the Lagrange multiplier Λ computed from the covariance matrix C of existing keys so the new key is orthogonal to 'occupied' directions.
Pipeline: choose k* (the subject's layer/token), optimize v* for the new answer, then insert via a single rank-1 update — about 2 seconds per fact.

COUNTERFACT (21 919 entries with neighbor subjects) separates generalization from specificity; the overall score S is a harmonic mean over the test dimensions (one failing test tanks the score); neighbor-subject generalization is the key trick.
ROME works on GPT-2 XL (zsRE and COUNTERFACT) and scales across model sizes; Figure 5 confirms the mechanism. On neighbor subjects ROME scores 89.2 vs the next best 66.9 (MEND-CF drops to 5.5).
Compositionality tests (Appendix G) and human evaluation mostly pass; a counter-probe shows editing the attention instead of the MLP does not work as well.
methods_math: Representation engineering / causal tracing (total effect TE, average indirect effect AIE).
Linear algebra: the MLP as a key→value associative memory; rank-1 matrix updates; covariance matrix of keys.
Constrained optimization: Lagrange multipliers (Λ) for the rank-1 edit under a 'do-not-disturb' constraint.
Least squares as the best-compromise solution.
Scoring via a harmonic mean over the COUNTERFACT test dimensions.
visualizations: Interactive sliders/cliques throughout (~30 <canvas> plots, ~16 Plotly references).
'Build your own memory' — a playable linear associative memory.
A self-generated causal-tracing heatmap (three passes).
Transformer-as-a-lattice (residual-stream) diagram with an MLP-block zoom.
Step-through rank-1 derivation (Appendix A) and Λ computation.
ROME three-step pipeline animation (k*, v*, insert).
internal_tensions: Claims to locate WHERE facts are stored, yet also admits the model 'keeps guessing — convincingly and wrong' after an edit.
Presents the MLP-as-key-value-store as a clean mechanism while conceding facts are only one kind of association (directed, factual) and edits are applied one at a time.
The 'two hot spots' localization is robust for typical facts but explicitly 'not always the last subject token' (App. B.4) — the clean story has exceptions.
Raises the misuse potential (editing is dual-use) while championing the technique's elegance.
Human evaluation surfaces an 'honest weakness', tempering the otherwise strong quantitative results.

title: Conceptors für Semantic Steering – Interaktive Reise
category_reason: Erklärt das Paper 'Conceptors for Semantic Steering' (Triantafyllopoulos et al., 2026, NYU & UPenn): Conceptor-Matrizen als weiche Projektionen auf Konzept-Unterräume, um Hidden States zu steuern. Klare KI-Kopplung (Representation Engineering).
thesis: Konzepte in Sprachmodellen sind Unterräume (keine einzelnen Pfeile), und man kann den Hidden State gezielt darauf steuern, indem man ihn mit einer Conceptor-Matrix weich auf den Konzept-Unterraum projiziert (mit einer 'Blende' α); Conceptors ermöglichen Boolesche Konzept-Komposition (NOT/AND/OR auf Matrizen), schlagen additive Baselines und ersetzen teures Probe-Training als Layer-Wegweiser.
key_claims: Ein Hidden State ist ein Vektor im Bedeutungssraum; Steering mit einem einzelnen Vektor (z. B. DiffMean) ist der einfache Fall.
Konzepte sind Unterräume (aus einer Datenwolke + Korrelationsmatrix & Eigenwerten), keine einzelnen Richtungen.
Der Conceptor ist eine weiche Projektions-Matrix C (aus R gebaut), die den State auf den Top-Unterraum des Konzepts projiziert (Capture(Δv̄, Top-Unterraum)).
α ist die 'Blende'/Aperture des Conceptors und steuert, wie viel Signal durchgelassen wird (steuert die Ellipse).
Bipolar > Unipolar: bipolare Conceptor-Matrizen sind leistungsfähiger.
Die Conceptor-Quota dient als Layer-Wegweiser (Pearson r bis 0.96 mit Probe-AUC) und ersetzt teures Probe-Training.
Boolesche Algebra (NOT/AND/OR) auf den Matrizen erlaubt Konzept-Komposition; Subspace-Overlap entscheidet, wann welche Operation funktioniert.
Ergebnis: Conceptors schlagen additive Baselines (Degenerate Outputs 13 % vs. 58 %; Win-Ratio pro Layer).
visualizations: 12 Canvases (Hidden State bewegen, DiffMean, Punktwolke→Unterraum, Korrelationsmatrix/Eigenwerte, weiche Gates, Aperture, bipolar, Quota, Boolean-Mixing, Overlap-Regime, Win-Ratio)
Plotly: Gating, Quota vs. AUC, Win-Ratio, MCQ
internal_tensions: Die 'Boolesche Algebra auf Matrizen' ist eine analoge Näherung — keine echte Mengen-/Logik-Algebra, sondern eine Projektions-Komposition.
Die Zahlen (r=0.96, 13 % vs. 58 %) stammen aus dem Paper; die Robustheit über Modelle/Tasks wird hier nicht re-evaluiert.
'Conceptors schlagen additive Baselines' ist an spezifischen Konzepten/Tasks gezeigt — die allgemeine Überlegenheit ist nicht bewiesen.

title: Simplicial Complexes & The Attention Mechanism

Thresholding attention weights at ε and taking the clique complex gives a filtration as ε varies from 1 to 0
Persistent homology tracks which topological features (β₀ components, β₁ loops, β₂ voids) persist across the filtration
Each attention head defines a different simplicial complex over the same vertex set (tokens)
Topological invariants of the attention complex provide interpretability: β₀ = attention clusters, β₁ = cyclic dependencies, β₂ = missing higher-order relations

attention_weight_graph
filtration_animation
multi_head_overlay
persistent_barcode
internal_tensions: The attention weights are soft (continuous) while simplicial complexes are combinatorial (discrete) — the thresholding step is arbitrary

title: Simplicial Complexes — Visual Explorer (mit Attention-Tab)
category_reason: Algebraische Topologie/TDA (Simplicial Complexes, Vietoris–Rips, persistente Homologie) explizit auf Transformer-Attention (Simplicial Attention Networks) angewandt
thesis: Interaktiver 3D-Explorer für Simplexe (Vertex→Edge→Triangle→Tetrahedron→Pentachoron) und den Aufbau von Simplicial Complexes (Vietoris–Rips), mit einem 'Attention'-Tab, der argumentiert, dass standard Transformer-Attention nur 1-Simplexe (paarweise Kanten) erfasst, während Simplicial Attention (SAN/topologisches message passing) höherdimensionale (2-/3-Simplex)-Interaktionen einfängt, die paarwise Attention verfehlt
key_claims: Ein 1-Simplex (Kante) ist genau das, was standard Attention berechnet — ein Gewicht zwischen jedem Token-Paar (softmax(QKᵀ/√d)); der Graph aller paarweisen Attention-Scores ist ein 1-dimensionaler Simplicial Complex
Ein 2-Simplex (gefülltes Dreieck) erfasst eine Dreier-Beziehung, die nicht auf Paare reduzierbar ist; Simplicial Attention (SAN) modelliert diese höherdimensionalen Interaktionen explizit

Ein Simplicial Complex muss alle Faces jedes Simplex enthalten (Closure-Eigenschaft); der Vietoris–Rips-Complex baut Simplexe aus einem Distanz-Schweller, und bei wachsendem Schwellwert erscheinen höherdimensionale Simplexe und offenbaren die Topologie der Daten

Simplicial Attention erfasst nicht-dekomponierbare Mehrwege-Abhängigkeiten (z.B. 'on' hängt simultan von 'cat', 'sat' und 'mat' ab); Architekturen: Simplicial Transformers, SAN, topologisches message passing
TDA-Pipelines (persistente Homologie) bauen diese Simplexe aus Daten, um hochdimensionale 'Shapes' in Feature-Räumen zu detektieren
visualizations: Interaktiver 2D-Canvas mit Custom-3D-Projektion (Drag-Rotation + Wheel-Zoom) jedes Simplex mit Build-Slider (Edges/Faces/Tets progressiv)
Complex-Build-Szene (Vietoris–Rips-Threshold-Slider zeigt V/E/F/T-Zähler live)

Die gezeigten Token-Attention-Gewichte sind simuliert/hartkodiert, nicht von einem echten Modell

title: Attention = Nerve + Sheaf (Simplicial Complex of Self-Attention)
category_reason: Math FOR AI: frames transformer self-attention as constructing a simplicial complex (nerve) plus a sheaf (value transport) — topology/sheaves applied to attention.
thesis: Self-attention has exactly two roles: a boundary operator (the bilinear form Q·Kᵀ, i.e. a metric tensor G=(W_Q)ᵀW_K) that defines a weighted simplicial skeleton (the nerve of semantic overlap), and a sheaf (V) that assigns a stalk to each token and, via the attention weights as restriction maps, transports meaning so the output is a 'global section'; RoPE is a connection (parallel transport) on a vector bundle with only relative position m−n mattering (gauge invariance).
key_claims: Attention = Nerve + Sheaf: Q·Kᵀ defines the simplicial skeleton (which tokens form vertices/edges/triangles), purely combinatorial; V transports meaning along it.
The nerve condition: a k-simplex exists iff all its (k−1)-faces exist (downward-closure axiom); an edge {i,j} exists iff min(α_ij, α_ji) > ε.
The attention output s_i = Σ_j α_ij·v_j is 'literally a weighted average of sheaf stalks' — a smoothed global section over the complex.
Q and K are not separate objects — two halves of a single bilinear form B(x_i,x_j) = x_iᵀ G x_j where G=(W_Q)ᵀW_K is a learned metric tensor on the embedding space.
RoPE is a connection on a vector bundle: <R_m q, R_n k> = qᵀ R_{m−n} k, so only the relative position (m−n) matters — gauge invariance.
Triangles (2-simplices) are where three tokens jointly compose/reconcile meaning, not just pairwise.
Betti numbers (β₀ components, β₁ loops) are computed and displayed for the attention complex.
methods_math: simplicial complexes / nerve construction & downward-closure axiom
bilinear form / learned metric tensor G
RoPE as connection / parallel transport / gauge invariance
visualizations: Plotly 3D (scatter3d + mesh3d): tokens as points in a 3D semantic space (X=Gender, Y=Being animal/human/divine, Z=Power) with green edges (restriction maps), gold triangles (2-simplices), red sheaf-flow arrows to the output points; a Plotly attention-matrix heatmap; a 2D 'sheaf transport' plot (input embeddings → output). Editable embedding table, metric tensor G, and W_V; sliders for temperature τ, threshold ε, RoPE base b; 5 sentences.
internal_tensions: Directly CONTRADICTS qkv2.html, which insists attention 'does NOT lay a surface or a simplicial complex' but is merely a convex combination of V vectors — same mechanism, opposite topological reading.

The 'two things, not three' claim (Q,K = one bilinear form; V = the content) is an interpretive framing; real attention uses separate, independently-trained W_Q, W_K, W_V per head, so G is not explicitly a chosen metric.

Embeddings are hand-authored 3D vectors (Gender/Being/Power) and the complex is built on a tiny set of sentences — illustrative of the formalism, not evidence that real models build such nerves/sheaves.
The 'sheaf-consistency problem' is asserted but the restriction maps α_ij·v_j are not actual sheaf morphisms satisfying the sheaf axioms — an analogy dressed as structure.

title: Attention Creates Simplicial Complexes
category_reason: Builds a simplicial complex (with Betti numbers) directly from transformer attention scores.
thesis: Type a sentence and each word gets a 3D embedding; attention scores (dot product) decide which words connect (edges) and which form triangles (2-simplices) — a simplicial complex that even yields Betti numbers, showing how meaning focuses locally.
key_claims: Each word maps to a 3D embedding [gender, being, power] in [-1,1] x [-1,1] x [0,1].
Attention is the dot product (a bilinear form with the identity), softmaxed row-wise with a sharpness (inverse temperature).
An edge is a pair whose mutual attention exceeds threshold epsilon; a triangle is three tokens all mutually connected.
Betti numbers are computed: beta_0 (connected components, via union-find) and beta_1 (loops) approximated as edges - (n - beta_0) - triangles.
Triangles mark where attention jointly composes three tokens into a single semantic focus — words 'thought about together'.
visualizations: Plotly 3D (3D scatter markers with labels, edge lines, mesh3d triangles), a token-embedding table, a simplicial-complex panel listing vertices/edges/triangles and Betti numbers with a meaning interpretation, and sliders for threshold epsilon and sharpness with live sentence input.
internal_tensions: The beta_1 formula is a rough approximation (edges - cyclomatic - triangles), not a proper homology computation.
A single simplified head (identity weights) is used, so the topological 'meaning' is heuristic.

title: Q·K → Simplex, V → Meaning Flow — How Attention Builds Simplicial Complexes
category_reason: Applies simplicial-complex / topological-data-analysis ideas to transformer self-attention (edges/triangles from attention, Betti numbers).
thesis: A Plotly interactive showing how attention builds a simplicial complex: Q·K attention scores above a threshold create 1-simplices (edges) and mutually attending triples create 2-simplices (triangles), through which V vectors carry 'meaning'; Betti numbers are reported.
key_claims: Words are 0-simplices: embeddings in a 3D semantic space whose axes are Male/Female, Animal/Divine, Weak/Strong (from a fixed toy lexicon).
An edge {i,j} exists iff min(alpha_ij, alpha_ji) > epsilon; a triangle exists iff all three mutual attention weights exceed epsilon.
Q = X·W_Q ('what am I looking for'), K = X·W_K ('what do I offer'), V = X·W_V (content that flows); scores = Q·K^T/sqrt(d), softmax -> attention; output = weighted sum of V.
Betti numbers are computed via union-find: beta_0 = connected components, beta_1 = loops (edges - (n - components) - triangles).
W_Q, W_K, W_V are user-editable 3x3 matrices; threshold epsilon and softmax sharpness are sliders.
methods_math: Betti numbers beta_0, beta_1 via union-find / loop counting
hash-based fallback embedding for out-of-lexicon words
visualizations: Plotly 3D scatter/mesh: embedding points, Q (diamond) and K (square) vectors, edges (lines), triangles (mesh3d), dotted Q->K lines, V-output (cross) markers; epsilon-threshold and sharpness sliders; editable W_Q/W_K/W_V matrix inputs; sentence text input; info panel listing vertices/edges/triangles + Betti numbers
internal_tensions: The semantic 3D space is a hand-authored toy lexicon (gender/being/power), not a real LLM embedding.
The beta_1 formula is a rough approximation (assumes triangles fill loops), not a true homology computation.
'V flows meaning along simplices' is a narrative metaphor, not the actual linear weighted-sum computation.

title: Attention = Points That Pull Each Other Closer
category_reason: Models transformer attention as point motion and reads its output as a simplicial complex of meaning.
thesis: Attention makes each word (a point in meaning-space) move toward the points it finds relevant; the simplicial complex (edges and triangles) that forms shows where words clump together — that clumping is the 'meaning' attention composes.
key_claims: Each word is a point in a 3D semantic space with axes [gender, being, power].
Relevance score(i,j) is the dot product (the Q-K part), treated as a similarity measure.
Each word then moves to the weighted center of all words weighted by relevance — the V part of attention.
An edge means the two found each other interesting (mutual weight above epsilon); a triangle means three all found each other interesting, forming a tight group.
The 'party' analogy: each person looks (Q) at name-tags (K) and walks toward those whose tags match; the friend-groups that form are the simplices.
A triangle is where meaning gets 'composed' — three words pulled into one region form one combined concept.
methods_math: simplicial complex of 1- and 2-simplices via threshold epsilon
visualizations: Plotly 3D (3D scatter markers with labels, edge lines, and mesh3d triangles) with an eased animation interpolating words from their original to post-attention positions; sliders for sharpness and threshold epsilon; live sentence input; a simplex/edges/triangles info panel and a 'biggest move' readout.
internal_tensions: The 'attention' uses the identity as W (no learned projections), so it is a toy single-head model.
The claim that triangles = 'composed meaning' is a heuristic interpretation, not a demonstrated representational fact.

title: Attention: Q, K, V — Geometrisch erklaert (Simplicial Complex)
category_reason: Explains QKV attention geometrically and builds a simplicial complex (edges/triangles) from mutual attention weights between word embeddings.
thesis: Attention is a geometric projection story: each word has an embedding point X; Q (W_Q·X, the 'spotlight'/question) and K (W_K·X, the 'sign'/offer) are two projections of X; the score is how parallel Q_i is to K_j; and words that mutually attend above a threshold epsilon form a simplicial complex (edges = pairs, triangles = 'meaning clumps').
key_claims: Each word has a fixed 3D embedding along (informally) a gender / being / power axis.
Q = W_Q·X is the word's 'question' (whom am I looking for?), K = W_K·X its 'offer' (here I am, find me); both are linear warps (rotations/scalings) of X.
Score = Q_i·K_j (/sqrt(3)); geometrically it is how parallel the two vectors are; softmax -> attention weights alpha.
The output of word i = sum(alpha_ij * V_j), a point lying geometrically 'between' the V-points it strongly attends to.

If two words attend to each other above epsilon (both alpha_ij and alpha_ji), they form a 1-simplex (edge); three pairwise-connected words form a 2-simplex (triangle) = a 'Bedeutungsklumpen' (coherent concept).
Uses a hand-crafted ~60-word lexicon (king/queen/lion/goddess/power/etc.) with fixed W_Q, W_K, W_V; unknown words get a hash-based embedding.
methods_math: simplicial complex from a mutual-attention threshold (Vietoris-Rips style)
visualizations: Plotly 3D: embedding points, X->Q and X->K projection lines, Q·K attention lines, output points, plus mesh3d triangles and line edges of the simplicial complex; live sentence input + epsilon / sharpness sliders + toggle checkboxes and a step-by-step info panel
internal_tensions: The simplicial-complex 'meaning clump' is built from a threshold on a symmetric (min) of attention — a TDA-style move on attention, but the embedding and W matrices are hand-authored, so the structure found is partly an artifact of the toy lexicon.
Attention is asymmetric in real models; using min(alpha_ij, alpha_ji) to make edges symmetric is a simplification.

title: Metric Space Explorer — Deep Algorithm Visualizer
category_reason: Main subject is how neural-network layers transform metric spaces (distances between data points), with 'strain maps' and 'layers' — the geometric effect of deep learning on data geometry.
thesis: Each layer of a deep neural network acts as a map between metric spaces that systematically distorts distances — compressing directions the network deems irrelevant and expanding directions it deems informative; the cumulative 'strain' across layers is what makes a high-dimensional, entangled input space into a cleanly separable representation.
key_claims: A neural-network layer is a (generally non-linear) map between metric spaces; its effect can be measured by how it stretches or compresses pairwise distances.
Early layers tend to preserve local geometry (small strain), while later layers perform large-scale reorganization (high strain) that separates classes.
The 'strain map' — a visualization of local distance distortion — reveals which regions of input space are being compressed and which are being expanded.
The composition of many mildly-distorting layers produces a globally dramatic transformation, analogous to how small rotations compose into large rotations.
visualizations: canvas animations showing point-clouds deforming through layers
strain-map heatmaps
interactive layer-depth slider
internal_tensions: The 'strain' picture is a local, linear approximation (Jacobian-based) and can miss global topological effects — e.g., a layer can have small local strain everywhere yet still fold the space in a way that changes its topology.

title: Layer als Raumkrümmung (A Layer Curves Space)
category_reason: Explains a neural layer as a nonlinear warp that makes non-separable data separable.
thesis: A neural network layer is a bending of space: a 2D dataset that is not linearly separable (inner core vs outer ring) becomes linearly separable once a layer lifts it into R^3 as phi(x,y) = (x, y, x^2 + y^2) and a plane slides between the classes — after which the plane collapses to a line and the space 'falls to a number'.
key_claims: Two classes (an inner point cloud and an outer ring) are not linearly separable in R^2 — no single straight cut separates them; topology forbids it.
Add a dimension: the old picture becomes the floor and a new z-axis stands up (embedding R^2 into R^3, no curvature yet).
The layer curves the space: phi(x,y) = (x, y, x^2 + y^2) — it bends, not tears; inner points sink, outer points rise into a shell.
A flat plane then slides cleanly between the classes in R^3, a linear separation w^T phi(x) + b = 0 that was impossible in 2D.
The plane is then squashed along the viewing direction into a line, and the space 'falls to a number' R^3 -> R, where a single point separates the classes.
methods_math: feature map / embedding into higher dimension
visualizations: A full-screen custom-projection canvas running a 7-step animated walkthrough (top view to side view camera moves, grid warping, the separating plane appearing and collapsing to a line, then a 1D score axis); navigate with arrow keys, drag to rotate, R to reset.
internal_tensions: It presents the canonical 'deep nets learn to warp space' story with a specific quadratic example, which is suggestive but not general (most real feature maps are far richer).
The 'plane becomes a line becomes a number' collapse is a visualization device that can overstate how a single scalar score is produced.

title: Origami in N Dimensionen — Interaktive Reise durch Keup & Helias (2022)
category_reason: Keup & Helias (2022, arXiv:2203.11355): Feedforward-Netzwerke machen lineare Trennbarkeit durch 'Falten' der Datenverteilung in freie (höhere) Dimensionen — ReLU als Hammer, Fold-and-Cut-Analogie; ReLU-Netze.
thesis: Das primäre mechanistische Werkzeug, mit dem ein Feedforward-Netz lineare Trennbarkeit herstellt, ist progressives Falten (Origami) der Datenverteilung in ungenutzte, höhere Dimensionen: ein ReLU ist der 'Hammer' (drückt die halbe Ebene auf die Faltlinie), eine affine Abbildung die Positionierung (gelernte Rotation), und die letzte Schicht macht einen einzigen 'Schnitt' (Hyperebene) — analog zum Fold-and-Cut-Theorem; empirisch bestätigt durch bimodale Tuning-Kurven.
key_claims: Eine Schicht = affine Transformation (dreht/skaliert/schert, Homöomorphismus — ändert Trennbarkeit NICHT) + elementweiser ReLU (Hammer — erste echte topologische Verformung).

Falten in freie Dimensionen (Schicht breiter als die Daten) ist injektiv und verliert keine Information — das zentrale Macht-Feature; Scheren ohne Extra-Dimensionen ist ineffizient (braucht tiefe, schmale Netze).
Kreis-im-Kreis (nicht linear trennbar) wird durch Heben in eine 3. Dimension (N ReLU-Neuronen als N-Eck-Wanne) linear trennbar.

Fold-and-Cut-Analogie: die Schichten falten die Daten so, dass alle Klassengrenzen übereinanderliegen; der letzte 'gerade Schnitt' (Hyperebene) schneidet die ganze Form — erklärt Universal-Approximation.
Bimodale Tuning-Kurven (zwei Peaks mit Tal bei x̃=0) im Poker-Hand-Netz sind der empirische Fingerabdruck einer Faltkante; Neurone mit großem 'Dip' sind die wichtigsten.
Konsequenzen: Schichten müssen breiter als die Datendimensionalität sein; 'Mixed Selectivity' ist kein Bug, sondern ein Feature des Faltmechanismus.
visualizations: Canvas 2D (Motivation, Affin, ReLU, Hammer, 2D-Ei, Rotation, 1D-Falte, Fold-and-Cut Papier, Shear-Animation, Tuning-Kurven)
Plotly 3D (Ei-Lift, N-Eck-Wanne, 3D-Neuronen)
Temml Mathematik (live aus den Reglern)
Slider/Buttons
internal_tensions: 'Effizienteste Operation = Falten' ist eine These mit empirischer Stütze (bimodale Kurven), aber kein vollständiger formaler Beweis über alle Architekturen.
Die Fold-and-Cut-Analogie ist heuristisch: die letzte Schicht 'schneidet', aber die vorherigen müssen die Grenzen exakt übereinanderlegen — in echten Netzen unvollständig.
Bimodale Tuning-Kurven sind in einem spezifischen (Poker-)Netz beobachtet; die Übertragbarkeit auf große Netze/Modelle ist offen.

title: Support Vector Machines — interaktiv verstehen
category_reason: Interactive teaching page on the SVM, a core ML classifier (max-margin, kernel trick, SMO training).
thesis: A library-free HTML/CSS/JS interactive explaining the SVM: the classifier that finds the widest-margin separating hyperplane, plus the kernel trick and a live SMO playground.
key_claims: The SVM picks the separating hyperplane farthest from both classes; margin = 2/||w||, so maximizing the margin is minimizing ||w||.
Only the support vectors determine the decision boundary; deleting every other point changes nothing.
Kernel trick: points need never be transformed explicitly — a kernel K(a,b) computes inner products in the high space directly (RBF exp(-gamma*||a-b||^2), poly (a^T b + 1)^d).
Soft margin: slack variables xi_i allow violations, and C controls how expensive they are; large C -> overfitting risk, small C -> smoother boundary tolerating outliers.
Optimization problem: min 1/2||w||^2 + C*sum xi_i subject to y_i(w^T x_i + b) >= 1 - xi_i, xi_i >= 0.
A simplified SMO (Sequential Minimal Optimization) is implemented to train live and redraw the decision-region heatmap.
visualizations: canvas 2D margin demo: draggable separating line (angle/offset), margin corridor, animated 'find optimum' search
canvas pseudo-3D 'kernel lift' (z = x^2+y^2) morph showing a flat plane separates rings in 3D
canvas live playground: click to add +1/-1 points, SMO retrain, bilinear-smoothed decision heatmap, margin contours, linear/RBF/poly tabs and C/gamma sliders
internal_tensions: Claims 'no framework, no libraries' yet ships a hand-rolled numerical SMO that may not fully converge (maxPass=12, tol=1e-3).
The 3D 'a flat plane separates the rings' is an illustrative analogy, not the literal linear SVM in that lifted space.

title: Symmetrie in Sprachstatistik · Interaktiver Erklärer
category_reason: Erklärt, warum Sprachmodelle (word2vec bis LLMs) Monate auf Kreisen, Jahre auf gewellten Linien und US-Staaten auf Landkarten anordnen: die Translationssymmetrie der Kookkurrenzstatistik macht M* zirkulant, und zirkulante Matrizen haben Fourier-Moden als Eigenvektoren (Karkada et al., ICML 2026).
thesis: Die Geometrie der Wortrepräsentationen in Sprachmodellen ist die Fourier-Transformierte der Kookkurrenzstatistik: Translationssymmetrie → zirkulante Matrix → Fourier-Eigenvektoren → Sinus/Kosinus-PCA-Achsen → Kreis (2 Achsen), Rippel (3+ Achsen), Lissajous-Figuren (Achsenpaare).
key_claims: Kookkurrenzstatistik M*_ij hängt fast nur vom Abstand |i−j| ab (Translationssymmetrie, gemessen an 2,72 Mrd. Wikipedia-Wörtern).
Zirkulante Matrizen werden immer von diskreten Fourier-Moden diagonalisiert (universell, kernunabhängig).
Korollar 2: Für exponentiellen Kern C(Δ) = exp(−|Δ|/σ) sind die PCA-Achsen a_n·sin(k_n·x + φ) mit a_n = √(2σ/(1+σ²k_n²)) — geschlossene Formel.
Offene Randbedingungen (Jahre): Quantisierungsbedingung für k_n (Fixpunkt-Gleichung, Proposition 3); Frequenzen sind nicht ganzzahlig.
Lissajous-Figuren: Jede Kombination zweier PCA-Achsen ergibt eine Lissajous-Kurve — empirisch in echten Wortvektoren bestätigt.
Lineares Dekodieren: Dekodierfehler ε² ~ r^(−1/D) (Proposition 4); Double Descent bei r = n_train.
Robustheit: Der Kreis überlebt die Löschung aller Monat-Monat-Kookkurrenzen, weil saisonale Helferwörter (Top-100) die Symmetrie kollektiv tragen; Eigenlücken wachsen ∝ N (Weyl/Davis-Kahan).
Architekturunabhängigkeit: Dieselbe Geometrie in word2vec, EmbeddingGemma und Gemma 2 2B.
visualizations: Monat-Kreis in PCA (Plotly)
Jahres-Mannigfaltigkeit 3D
US-Staaten-Landkarte (Heatmap auf Gitter)
Kookkurrenz-Fenster-Animation (Canvas)
Zirkulante Matrix-Konstruktion interaktiv
Fourier-Moden addieren (Plotly)

3D Kalender-Pringle (Plotly surface)
Ablation-Spielzeug (Monat-Monat löschen)
