2D-Plane-Waves (Trommelfell-Moden)
internal_tensions: Theorie gilt rigoros für Wort-Einbettungsmodelle; für LLMs nur empirisch belegt, nicht bewiesen.
LLMs können kontextabhängig umstrukturieren (Polysemie, z.B. 'May' als Monat vs. Modalverb) — Theorie beschreibt nur die kontextfreie Basisgeometrie.
Ausblck auf Gitterzellen im Gehirn (Entorhinalkortex) ist spekulativ, nicht belegt.
Die Translationssymmetrie ist eine Näherung: reale Texte brechen sie (Weltkriegsjahre, Polysemie).

title: Talking Heads · Interaktive Erklärung
category_reason: Mechanistische Interpretierbarkeit / Modell-Editierung eines NeurIPS-2024-Papers (Merullo, Eickhoff, Pavlick, arXiv:2406.09519) ueber die Kopff-zu-Kopf-Kommunikation in der Transformer-Attention.
thesis: Transformer-Kopfe kommunizieren ueber die Attention-Map: die QK^T-Matrix laesst sich per SVD in rank-1-Komponenten zerlegen, und einzelne Komponenten sind messbare 'Kommunikationskanael' zwischen Kopfpaaren (Composition Score). Diese Kanael koennen isoliert bearbeitet, gesteuert und — wenn ein Circuit beschmadigt wurde — genutzt werden, um die Schmaedigung zu reparieren.
key_claims: Attention ist nicht nur token-zu-token, sondern kopf-zu-kopf: Kopfe tauschen ueber die Attention-Map Informationen aus.
Die QK^T-Interaktionsmatrix laesst sich per SVD in rank-1-Komponenten zerlegen.
Der Composition Score (Spitze einer Komponente) massst die Staerke eines Kopfpaar-Kanals.
Bestimmte Komponenten sind statistisch auffaellig (z.B. ein Kopf bei ~5 sigma) und damit echte Kommunikationsspur.
Isolierte Komponenten koennen ueber Gewichts-Editing bzw. Steering gezielt verstmaerkt oder unterdrueckt werden.
Die Kommunikation hat eine 3D-Unterraum-Geometrie (kompatibler Quell-/Ziel-Unterraum).
Beschmadigte Circuits lassen sich ueber die identifizierten Komponenten reparieren.
methods_math: SVD-Zerlegung der Attention-Interaktionsmatrix QK^T in rank-1-Komponenten
visualizations: Plotly + Canvas-Demos der Komponentenzerlegung
Composition-Score-Heatmap ueber Kopfpaare
3D-Unterraum-Darstellung der Kommunikationskanael
Steering-/Editing-Demo vor/nach
Circuit-Reparatur-Animation
internal_tensions: Kopf-zu-Kopf-Kommunikation wird als strukturierter Kanal gerahmt, ist aber eine SVD-Abstraktion der Attention-Map — die 'Kanael' sind keine expliziten Einheiten des Netzes.
Die 5-sigma-Komponente ist ein Ausreiuer; ob die uebrigen schwmaecheren Komponenten Kausalitaet tragen, bleibt offen.
Repair/Steering funktioniert an der isolierten Komponente, uebertragbar auf ganze Aufgaben bleibt aber begrenzt.

title: How LLMs Store Information — Deep Interactive Demonstrator
category_reason: Tiefer interaktiver Demonstrator, wie LLMs Information speichern: Residual Stream (Concept-Geometrie), MLP als Key-Value-Memory, Superposition (Features über Dimensionen hinaus), polysemantische Neuronen, Live-Training, Mini-Transformer-Forward-Pass. Klare KI-Kopplung (Repräsentationsgeometrie/Interpretierbarkeit).
thesis: LLMs speichern Information als Geometrie im Residual Stream: der Stream ist ein Vektorraum, in dem Konzepte Richtungen sind; das MLP agiert als Key-Value-Memory, Superposition packt mehr Features als Dimensionen (mit Interferenz), polysemantische Neuronen mischen Feature-Richtungen, und man kann per Live-Training zusehen, wie Wissen als geometrische Struktur entsteht.

title: Transformer Attractor Dynamics
category_reason: Transformer-Modelle als nicht-autonome dynamische Systeme mit Attraktoren: Layer als Euler-Schritte, Attention + FFN als Kräfte, LayerNorm als Sphären-Projektion, Basin-of-Attraction-Dynamik, Superposition.
thesis: Ein Transformer ist ein nicht-autonomes dynamisches System, bei dem jeder Layer ein Euler-Schritt ist (h^(ℓ+1) = h^(ℓ) + f_ℓ(h^(ℓ))); Tokens sind Teilchen auf einer Hypersphäre S^(d-1) (aufgezwungen durch LayerNorm), die durch Attention (Kontext-Kraft zwischen Tokens) und FFN (assoziative Attraktor-Kraft) gegen stabile Attraktoren konvergieren, die den Output-Tokens entsprechen; die Konvergenz ist progressiv (breite → scharfe Bassins), und die finale Decodierung erfolgt über die Unembedding-Matrix.
key_claims: Jeder Transformer-Layer ist ein Euler-Schritt: h^(ℓ+1) = h^(ℓ) + f_ℓ(h^(ℓ)), f_ℓ = Attention + FFN (analog zu Chen et al. 2018 für ResNets).
LayerNorm projiziert alle Repräsentationen auf eine Hypersphäre S^(d-1); Attraktoren liegen auf der Kugeloberfläche, nicht frei im ℝ^d.
Attention erzeugt 'Kontext-Kräfte' zwischen Tokens (relationale Verschiebung): es verschiebt Tokens zueinander, nicht zu Attraktoren.
FFN erzeugt 'Attraktor-Kräfte' (assoziatives Nachschlagen): W₁ ist ein Pattern-Matcher, W₂ gibt den Wissensinhalt zurück (Geva et al. 2021: FFN als Key-Value-Memory).
Die Konvergenz ist progressiv: frühe Layer haben breite, überlappende Bassins; späte Layer schärfen die Grenzen; ‖f_ℓ(h)‖ nimmt mit ℓ ab.
Zwischen Layer 8–12 (bei 24 Layern) liegt ein Saddle Point: die Entscheidung ist instabil, kleine Perturbationen können den Token in ein anderes Basin kippen.
Superposition: in d Dimensionen können ≫d fast-orthogonale Konzept-Richtungen untergebracht werden; die 'Entscheidung' zwischen zwei Attraktoren passiert oft nur in wenigen kritischen Dimensionen.
Fünf offene Fragen: Punkt-Attraktoren vs. Mannigfaltigkeiten, fraktale Basin-Grenzen, Limit Cycles, Kontext-Abhängigkeit der Attraktor-Landschaft, Berechenbarkeit der Bassins aus den Gewichten.
visualizations: Canvas 2D (Trajektorien, Attention-Weight-Matrix, FFN-Aktivierungen, Basin-Grenzen, Superposition, Output-Distribution)
Canvas 2D 3D-Projektion (Sphäre mit Attraktoren, 3D-Trajektorien)
Interaktive Slider (Layer, Temperatur, Dimensionen, Auflösung)
Animationen (Layer-Durchlauf, Trajektorien-Playback)
internal_tensions: Die Attraktor-Interpretation ist heuristisch und nicht formal bewiesen — es gibt keinen Theorem, der die Existenz stabiler Attraktoren in trainierten Transformers garantiert.
Die Simulationen sind synthetisch (feste Trajektorien, keine echten Gewichte); die visualisierten Dynamiken sind Illustrationen, keine Messungen.
Die Superposition-Argumentation (≫d Konzepte in d Dimensionen) ist ein Hochdimensionalitäts-Phänomen, das in der 2D/3D-Visualisierung nicht direkt darstellbar ist.
Der Saddle-Point bei Layer 8–12 ist eine heuristische Beobachtung, keine messbare Invariante.

title: Die mathematische Theorie des Deep Learning — Eine interaktive Reise
category_reason: A math textbook FOR machine learning: it explains why deep neural networks work via approximation, optimization, and generalization theory. Entirely about neural-net learning.
thesis: Deep learning works because three pillars line up at once: (1) approximation — ReLU nets are universal and, via Yarotsky's sawtooth trick, can build polynomials and thus approximate smooth functions exponentially efficiently in depth; (2) optimization — the loss landscape is non-convex but benign (high loss is likely a saddle; very wide nets become linear / Gaussian-process-like); (3) generalization — despite the overparameterization paradox, data structure (low Barron norm, compositionality, manifolds) plus Lipschitz regularization resolve double descent. The curse of dimensionality is a genuine hard limit that real-data structure sidesteps.
key_claims: Universal approximation holds, and depth is exponentially more economical than width (sawtooth / piece-count budget argument).
Yarotsky's sawtooth plus the polarization identity lets ReLU nets compute multiplication → monomials → polynomials → all smooth functions.
The curse of dimensionality is a genuine hardness barrier, but real data escape it via low Barron norm, compositionality, or manifold structure.
High-loss points in the landscape are overwhelmingly saddles rather than bad local minima; backprop makes training feasible.
Very wide nets behave like linear models / Gaussian processes, which rescues optimization.
One cannot optimize over the function space (non-star-shaped with few centers, no ε-convexity, no best approximation → exploding weights).
Double descent is real (the interactive Runge experiment); the peak is explained by singular values and resolved by Lipschitz regularization.
Adversarial examples (the panda that becomes a wombat) stem from high dimension; Lipschitz bounds and Interval-Bound Propagation give certified defenses.

Architecture chapters cover ResNets (skip connections vs vanishing gradients), CNNs (translational equivariance + locality), and Transformers (global dependence via attention; sinusoidal positional encoding).
methods_math: Approximation theory: universal approximation, Hölder convergence rates, Barron norm.
Yarotsky sawtooth + polarization identity for constructing multiplication / polynomials.
Optimization: saddle-point structure of loss landscapes; Gaussian-process view of wide nets.
Statistical learning: error decomposition, covering numbers, VC dimension, approximation-complexity tradeoff.
Double descent via singular-value analysis; Lipschitz regularization.
Certified adversarial robustness via Lipschitz bounds and Interval-Bound Propagation.
visualizations: Per-section interactive sliders/buttons (KaTeX math, ~25 <canvas> plots, ~37 Plotly references, a little d3).
Step-by-step sawtooth / polynomial-construction diagrams.
Loss-landscape and saddle-point interactive 'games'.
Interactive Runge double-descent curve.
Adversarial panda→wombat demo plus an IBP forward-pass certificate.
A final interactive overall map and a side-by-side table of all convergence rates.
internal_tensions: Presents deep learning as 'explained' by three pillars while repeatedly flagging hard limits (curse of dimensionality, non-convexity, no best approximation) — explanation coexists with open questions.
Tension between the idealized 'benign landscape' narrative and the explicit warning that the landscape is non-convex and convergence is not guaranteed.
The 'magic activation' used for clean approximation is a warning shot: the theory leans on activations that real nets do not use.
Ends with an 'open questions' section, undercutting the confident three-pillar framing.

title: Die mathematische Theorie des Deep Learning — Einfach erklärt
category_reason: Main subject is the mathematical theory of deep learning: approximation, optimization, and generalization of neural networks — core ML theory.
thesis: The mathematical theory of deep learning rests on three pillars — approximation (what can a network represent?), optimization (how do we find good weights?), and generalization (why does it work on unseen data?) — and the unifying insight is that depth, not width, is the source of neural networks' expressive power: chaining ReLU kinks multiplies the number of piecewise-linear regions exponentially, while adding them only grows linearly.
key_claims: A ReLU network is a piecewise-linear function: each neuron adds one kink, and the network's representational power is bounded by the number of linear regions it can form.

Telgarsky's bound: a ReLU network of depth L and width w has at most (2w)^L piecewise-linear regions; with 30 neurons arranged deep-and-narrow (w=3, L≈10), this reaches ~60 million regions vs ~31 for a single wide layer.

Yarotsky's 2017 result: the piecewise-linear interpolant of x² at 2ⁿ knot points can be built with only O(n) parameters (not O(2ⁿ)), via a telescoping sum of the sawtooth function — giving exponential accuracy at linear cost.
Vanishing gradients: with sigmoid (max σ′ = 0.25), the gradient after n layers shrinks as 0.25^n ≈ 10⁻²⁴ at n=40; ReLU (σ′ ∈ {0,1}) avoids this, which is why it enabled modern deep learning.
Double descent: in the overparameterized regime (more parameters than data points), the test error decreases again after the interpolation point, contradicting the classical bias-variance tradeoff.
Adversarial examples are not a bug but a necessity: any smoothly classifying function in high dimensions must have decision boundaries that can be crossed by arbitrarily small perturbations.

canvas: vanishing gradient — (max σ′)^n readout for sigmoid vs ReLU
canvas: universal approximation — piecewise-linear interpolant of target functions (zigzag, Runge, step)

canvas: piece-count budget — (2w)^L vs depth allocation for fixed 30 neurons

internal_tensions: The page explicitly flags its own limitations in the 'Grenzen' section: the exponential region bounds are not achieved by randomly-initialized networks (expected region count grows only linearly in depth per Hanin & Rolnick), and Yarotsky's optimal weights are discontinuous — no stable training algorithm can reach them.
The 'Honesty corner' acknowledges that all diagrams are 1D/2D pedagogical reconstructions, not the actual high-dimensional phenomena.

title: Die mathematische Theorie des Deep Learning — Ganz einfach erklärt
category_reason: A very simple German-language interactive explanation of the three pillars of deep learning theory: approximation (universal approximation, depth vs. width), optimization (gradient descent, saddle points), and generalization (double descent, neural tangent kernel). Directly about why neural networks work.
thesis: A very simple German-language interactive explanation of the three great pillars of deep learning theory with five hands-on experiments: (1) the central tension — the model must be complex enough to capture the truth but simple enough to find it (bias-variance tradeoff); (2) approximation — neural nets are piecewise-linear 'folded cards' and depth multiplies the number of pieces while width adds them; (3) optimization — gradient descent on a rugged loss landscape, where saddle points (not local minima) are the real obstacle in high dimensions; (4) generalization — the double-descent phenomenon where test error drops again after overparameterization, explained by the neural tangent kernel making overparameterized nets behave linearly.
key_claims: The entire theory of deep learning is one tension: the model must be large enough to represent the truth and small enough to find it. Set 'very complex' (degree 12) with only 8 training examples: training error → 0, but true (test) error explodes — the model memorized, it did not understand.

A neural network is a piecewise-linear function: a chain of 'weights times input plus shift' with a kink function (ReLU) between each layer. Each kink creates a sharp edge in the output; the network is a 'folded card' of many small flat pieces.
Universal approximation: every continuous function can be approximated arbitrarily well by a neural network with enough neurons — but the theorem says nothing about how many neurons are needed.

Depth multiplies, width adds: a 'hat' function h₁ from 2 ReLUs has 2 kinks; chain it n times → 2ⁿ⁻¹ kinks with only linearly growing size. With 30 neurons: 1 layer → ~31 pieces; 10 layers of 3 → up to 6¹⁰ ≈ 60 million pieces. Same budget, millions-fold reach. This is why nets are built deep.

In high dimensions, saddle points (points that go uphill in one direction and downhill in another) dominate over true local minima. With suitable architectures (very wide nets), the loss landscape becomes nearly convex — there is essentially only good and bad valley, no deceptive fake minimum.

Double descent: the classical prediction is that test error rises once the model has more parameters than data points (the 1.0 mark). In practice, test error drops again (the 'second descent'). The reason: very wide nets become surprisingly linear during training (Neural Tangent Kernel theory) — gradient descent then systematically finds a solution that generalizes.

The interpolation paradox is resolved: overparameterized nets can fit the training data perfectly (interpolate) AND generalize well, because the NTK makes the training dynamics linear and the found solution is the minimum-norm interpolant.
methods_math: bias-variance tradeoff (fit the data vs. generalize)
piecewise-linear functions, ReLU activations, kink counting
depth vs. width: piece count grows exponentially in depth, linearly in width
gradient descent, learning rate, loss landscape
saddle points, Hessian eigenvalues, high-dimensional optimization
double descent (test error as a function of model size)
Neural Tangent Kernel (NTK) theory, overparameterized linearization
visualizations: Experiment 1 — Outfitting Game: green dashed = true rule, red curve = model fit; adjust training examples and model complexity (polynomial degree); watch training error and true (test) error; 'Neue Stichprobe ziehen' (draw new sample) button

Experiment 2 — Knuckle Builder: green dashed = target curve, red = folded card from n neurons; adjust width (number of neurons); watch the kinks get denser and the curve approach the target; 'Zickzack', 'Runge-Funktion', 'Stufensprung' target selections

Experiment 3 — Sawtooth Telemetry: chain a 'hat' function n times; watch the kinks double per layer (2ⁿ⁻¹) while the network size grows linearly; 'Stücke-Budget' panel: fixed 30 neurons, different depth/width splits, log-scale piece count

Experiment 4 — Gradient Descent: a white dot descends a rugged 2D loss landscape (dark = low error); learning rate slider controls step size; 'Ein Schritt' (one step) for frame-by-frame; 'Zurücksetzen' (reset)

Experiment 5 — Double Descent: grey dashed = classical prediction (error rises after 1.0 mark), solid = actual (second descent); slider for model size (parameters/data points); watch the test error drop again in the overparameterized regime
internal_tensions: The file is explicitly 'ganz einfach erklärt' (very simply explained) and 'nur Schulmathematik' (only school math), which means the NTK theory and double descent are heavily condensed; the reader gets the intuition but not the mathematical content (e.g., the NTK is a specific kernel that depends on the initialization, not just 'the net becomes linear').

The 'depth multiplies, width adds' claim is the most striking but also the most easily misread: the piece-count argument assumes the kinks are all in 'general position' (no two kinks coincide), which is not guaranteed in practice; the actual expressive power of deep vs. wide nets is more subtle.

The saddle-point discussion is important but brief: the file states that saddle points dominate in high dimensions and that wide nets make the landscape 'nearly convex,' but does not explain WHY (the connection to the Hessian eigenvalue distribution and the NTK regime is only hinted at).

The double-descent visualization is a 2D plot of test error vs. model size; the real phenomenon is that the double descent depends on the training algorithm (gradient descent finds the minimum-norm solution, while other algorithms may not), and this dependence is not captured in the visualization.

title: Token-Embeddings verletzen die Manifold-Hypothese — Interaktiv
category_reason: Geometrie der Embeddings: statistischer Test, ob die Token-Eingabematrix realer LLMs ein glattes Manifold (bzw. Fiber Bundle) ist — Ergebnis: nein (Robinson, Dey, Chiang, NeurIPS 2025).
thesis: Die Token-Embeddings realer Sprachmodelle liegen nicht auf einem glatten Manifold (und meist nicht einmal auf einem Fiber Bundle); sie enthalten Singularitäten, die Prompt-Fragilität erklären und in die Ausgabe hineinwandern.
key_claims: Manifold-Hypothese wird für alle vier getesteten Modelle (GPT2, Llemma7B, Mistral7B, Pythia6.9B) hochsignifikant verworfen (p bis 3×10⁻⁸ nach Holm-Bonferroni).
Fiber-Bundle-Hypothese wird für drei von vier Modellen verworfen (Pythia6.9B nicht).
Der Test misst Dimension als Steigung im log-log-Plot (Volumen ≈ Punktzahl im Radius r); Krümmung = Korrekturterm, Singularität = Knick nach oben.
GPT2-Embedding ist Mischverteilung mit drei Dimensionsgipfeln (~20, ~389, ~531); es gibt sogar Tokens mit Dimension 0 (isolierte Punkte).
Irreguläre Tokens sind Wortanfangstokens, Homonyme (affect, monitor, wins, aunder) und Tokens, die Sprach-Manifolds unterschiedlicher Dimension verkleben.

title: Token-Embeddings verletzen die Manifold-Hypothese - Einfach erklaert
category_reason: It is a simple German explainer of Robinson, Dey & Chiang (2025, arXiv:2504.01002) testing the manifold hypothesis on the token-embedding spaces of real LLMs (GPT2, Llemma7B, Mistral7B, Pythia6.9B) — topology/geometry applied directly to language-model embeddings.
thesis: A simple German 9-station interactive explainer of Robinson, Dey & Chiang (2025, NeurIPS, arXiv:2504.01002): it builds a per-token statistical test of the assumption that data live on a smooth manifold by reading local dimension as the slope of a log-log (volume vs radius) curve and detecting *kinks* (not mere bends), and shows that the token-embedding spaces of four real LLMs all reject the manifold hypothesis (and three of four reject the milder fiber-bundle hypothesis) — i.e. their 'thought space' has bruchkanten (singularities).
key_claims: The manifold hypothesis — that (almost) every ML work tacitly assumes — is that data lie on a smooth curved surface where each point has a neighborhood like a flat patch of R^d; the paper tests it per token and finds it *false* for real LLM token inputs, which instead have bruchkanten (singularities).

The core trick: count the neighbors in radius r (the 'volume'), which grows like r^d in d dimensions, so the slope of log(Volume) vs log(r) is the dimension d (the volume is estimated by point-counting / Monte-Carlo).

The test detects *kinks* (sudden slope changes), not *bends*: a smooth bend can come from curvature (Gray 1974's ball-volume correction K*r^d + (...)r^{d+1}), but an upward kink cannot come from any smooth surface, so it signals a genuine singularity.

Fiber-bundle hypothesis (Satz 1, the milder model): each neighborhood looks like base space x fiber, so the log-log curve is piecewise linear with slopes that may only *fall* as r grows (fiber dimension -> base dimension); an *upward* kink is impossible and refutes the bundle.

The machinery: distance matrix -> per-token sorted distances (volume = rank) -> log-log slopes via 3-point differences -> sliding-window t-test -> p-values -> Holm-Bonferroni (multiple-testing correction for 50,257 tokens); the Manifold test is two-sided (any slope change) and the Bundle test one-sided (only rising).

Validation on three known shapes: the sphere (true 2D manifold — not rejected), the cusp z^8 + x^2 + y^2 = 0 (manifold rejected at the tip, bundle not — exactly the mathematical truth), and the lollipop (1D stem + 2D ball — both rejected); the cusp is the discriminative proof, and edge points are missed (sensitivity costs specificity).

Results on four real LLMs (~12 h CPU each, mostly the distance matrix): all four reject the manifold hypothesis (min p down to ~3e-8); GPT2's dimension ranges from 20 (numbers, months, weekdays) to 531 (word-fragments), i.e. not constant; Llemma7B (median dim 4096) vs Mistral7B (median dim 48) share a 32,016-token vocab but differ wildly — a 'gDNA' training fingerprint; singular tokens include affect, monitor, aunder, ember, Xan, *.

Lemma 1 (product/quotient) plus Satz 2: more context does not permanently heal the singularities (for every window size a longer one re-exposes them); singularities can reach the output whenever 2d < ell (d = ambient dimension, ell = latency), i.e. when m > 2*w*d/ell and w >= m is satisfiable.
methods_math: manifold and manifold-with-boundary definitions, singularities (cusp, dimension jump), and the reach tau
local dimension via the log-log slope: log V = log K + d * log r (volume ~ K * r^d)
Gray (1974) ball-volume expansion K*r^d + (...)r^{d+1} as the curvature correction
the fiber-bundle hypothesis: base space x fiber, piecewise-linear log-log with only-falling slopes
3-point-difference slope estimation and a sliding-window t-test
multiple-testing correction via step-down Holm-Bonferroni (compare sorted p_(k) to alpha/(n-k+1))
Lemma 1 (product/quotient) and the Satz-2 reach-to-output condition m > 2*w*d/ell with w >= m (equivalently 2d < ell)
visualizations: a 9-station scroll page with a sticky nav, a progress bar, and per-station Canvas 2D demos (all 2D; this 'simple' version replaces the original's three.js/CDN 3D plots)
Station 1: a 'two identical prompts, two answers' scatter — a stable cloud A vs cloud B that fragments as a 'naehe zur Bruchkante' slider pushes it toward a bruchkante
Station 2: a zoom-explorer switching shapes (circle / segment / cusp / lollipop) with a position slider that magnifies a local neighborhood and verdicts it smooth / edge / cusp / dimension-jump
Station 3: a build-your-own log-log curve with left/right slope and kink-point sliders, flagging 'Steigung STEIGT -> Bruchkante!'
Station 4: a bend-vs-kink plot (base slope + curvature + a 'Knick einbauen' toggle) with a note on the reach-tau limitation
Station 5: a fiber-bundle 'strip' demo — a ball of radius r inside/outside a strip of fiber-width, reading slope ~ 2 (fiber) vs ~ 1 (base)
Station 6: a Holm-Bonferroni plot (sorted p-values vs the step-down threshold plus a Bonferroni line) with a tests-n slider and false-positive / pass counts
Station 8: a Satz-2 playground (latency ell, dimension d, window w sliders) plotting m_min(d) = 2*w*d/ell against the w bound to test whether singularities survive to the output
a validation table (sphere / cusp / lollipop), a four-model results table, and a 6-question self-test quiz
internal_tensions: The 'simple' version explicitly replaces all 3D/three.js plots with 2D Canvas and calls the synthetic point-clouds 'Nachbauten' (reconstructions), not model weights — so the interactive demos are didactic, and only the reported p-values and dimensions come from the paper.

The test has an admitted limitation: it cannot say *which* singularity (cusp vs pinch vs jump) and it misses edge/boundary points (a sensitivity-vs-specificity trade-off); moreover non-rejection does not mean 'is smooth' (Pythia6.9B could be a bundle or just high curvature).

The reach tau (only radii below it are valid) is 'hard to estimate', so the practical validity of each per-token test is itself uncertain; and the method requires open-weight embedding-matrix access, limiting it to a subset of models.

Satz 2's claim that singularities 'reach the output' is a conditional theorem (2d < ell) recast as a practical 'always satisfiable' rule — a strong extrapolation from the static embedding space all the way to generation.

title: Bruchkanten im Gedankenraum — ganz einfach erklärt
category_reason: Explains a 2025 result on the geometry of LLM token-embedding spaces (manifold hypothesis violation) — a question about ML models.
thesis: A no-math, plain-language version of Robinson, Dey & Chiang (2025, NeurIPS): token-embedding spaces of real LLMs are NOT smooth manifolds — they have 'Bruchkanten' (singularities / break-edges), which is why near-identical prompts can yield wildly different answers.
key_claims: Most AI work silently assumes model 'thoughts' lie on a smooth curved surface (manifold); this paper tests that and finds it false for real LLMs.
The test: zoom in at a point — if the neighborhood looks like a flat disc it is smooth, otherwise it is a singularity (Bruchkante).
Dimension trick: count neighbors in a ball — volume ~ K*r^d, so the log-log slope = dimension; a suddenly RISING slope signals a break-edge.
On 4 real models (~12 h compute each): 4/4 reject the manifold hypothesis; 3/4 also reject the milder fiber-bundle hypothesis; min p-value 3e-8 (GPT2); GPT2's dimension ranges 20-531 (not constant).
GPT2's dimension distribution has three peaks (~20 for numbers/months/days, ~389 single words, ~531 word-fragments); some words have dimension 0 (isolated points).

Prompts aren't portable: Llemma7B vs Mistral7B (same 32,016-token vocab) have very different geometry (median dim 4096 vs 48); longer context does not 'heal' singularities; singularities can reach the output.

Honesty corner: non-rejection is not evidence of smoothness; the test detects but does not classify the kind of break-edge; validity is limited to radii below the hard-to-estimate 'reach'; boundary points are missed (sensitivity vs specificity).
methods_math: local dimension estimation via volume scaling V(r)~K*r^d (log-log slope)
visualizations: canvas demo 1: two prompt answer-clouds — a 'Bruchkante' slider splits cloud B into clusters (prompt fragility)
canvas demo 2: zoom-test on a circle (smooth) vs a cusp (singularity) with position + zoom sliders and a 'flache Scheibe' vs 'Singularität' verdict
canvas demo 3: build a log-log volume curve with two slopes (left/right of a kink) — rising slope -> 'Bruchkante!' verdict
big-number stat cards (4/4, 3/4, 3e-8, 20-531)
internal_tensions: An explicit 'honesty corner' — a non-rejection is not evidence of smoothness, and the test neither classifies singularities nor is valid above the 'reach'.
The demo clouds/shapes are didactic rebuilds, not real model weights; all figures are quoted from the paper's tables/figures.

title: Die Topologie tiefer neuronaler Netze — Interaktiv erklärt
category_reason: Explains a paper (Naitzat, Zhitnikov, Lim — arXiv:2004.06093, 2020) about how deep neural networks change the topology of their data — squarely machine learning + topological data analysis.
thesis: A deep network is not a function approximator but a 'shape-transformation machine': layer by layer it untangles a topologically knotted data manifold until the Betti numbers collapse to their minimum (β₀ = 1, βₖ = 0 for k ≥ 1). title: Tropische Geometrie tiefer Netze — Einfach erklärt
category_reason: Applies tropical geometry (piecewise-linear structure) to deep neural networks; the main subject is neural network architecture understood through a mathematical lens.
thesis: Deep neural networks with piecewise-linear activations (ReLU) define tropical rational maps; the tropical geometry of the weight space, in particular the hyperplane arrangements and tropical varieties, controls the network's piecewise-linear complexity, capacity, and identifiability.

The number of linear regions (piecewise-linear complexity) is the network's geometric capacity
Tropical geometry provides the algebraic framework: the network map is a tropical rational map in the (max,+) or (min,+) semiring
Identifiability, when two weight configurations compute the same function, is governed by the combinatorics of the tropical arrangement
Deeper networks have exponentially more linear regions than wider shallow networks of the same parameter count
methods_math: Tropical geometry, piecewise-linear maps, hyperplane arrangements, tropical rational maps, semiring algebra

internal_tensions: The tropical framework assumes exact piecewise-linearity; real networks often use smooth approximations (GELU, sigmoid) that break the combinatorial structure; the 'simple' framing may understate the algebraic complexity of the full picture.

title: Die geheime Rechenkunst hinter neuronalen Netzen (Tropical Geometry of Deep NNs, very simple)
category_reason: Explains (via Zhang, Naitzat & Li 2018) that ReLU nets are exactly tropical geometric objects and why depth beats width — math for understanding neural nets.
thesis: Replace + with max and * with + and you get tropical mathematics — and ReLU nets are exactly its objects: a ReLU net (with integer weights) is precisely a continuous piecewise-linear function, precisely a 'tropical rational function'. This explains, geometrically, why depth wins: each layer 'folds' the existing pieces, so the number of linear regions grows exponentially in depth (while width only grows it linearly).
key_claims: Tropical math swaps the operations: instead of + and * it uses max(x,y) and x+y; ReLU(x) = max(x, 0) is literally a tropical operation, so a ReLU net is 'identical' (not merely similar) to a tropical object.
A 1D ReLU net draws a piecewise-linear ('knicked') line; each neuron contributes one kink; the 'intelligence' is where and how many kinks (linear regions) there are.

Equivalence (the paper's main point): ReLU nets with integer weights = continuous piecewise-linear functions with integer slopes = tropical rational functions (differences of 'max-of-lines'); you can switch between them losslessly, and the family is closed under tropical add/mul/div (an algebra).

Depth beats width: a flat net makes ~#neurons regions, but a deeper net stacks folds so regions grow as k^L (exponential in depth) while neurons grow only as L*k (linear) — e.g. 1024 regions with just 20 neurons (k=4, L=5).

Honesty corner: only piecewise-linear activations qualify (ReLU, Leaky-ReLU, abs, Max-Pool — but NOT tanh/Sigmoid); integer weights are required for the tropical geometry (not just cosmetic); it explains why depth wins but NOT why nets generalize (that stays open); Theorem 6.3 reformulates, not improves, the Raghu et al. (2017) bound.
methods_math: convex geometry / zonotopes (Maclagan-Sturmfels duality, Gritzmann-Sturmfels zonotope vertex theorem)
visualizations: two canvas 2D demos: (1) a 1-D 'Knick-Maschine' — three ReLU neurons whose kink position/strength you slide, counting kinks and linear regions live; (2) a 'Falt-Experiment' — applying a k-tooth fold L times, showing regions = k^L exploding while neurons = L*k stay small
internal_tensions: The equivalence holds only for piecewise-linear activations and integer weights, so it does not cover the tanh/sigmoid nets many people picture as 'the' neural net — a real scope limit the file flags.
It is explicit that the tropical view explains the depth/width expressiveness advantage but leaves the central generalization question unanswered — a language to pose the question, not an answer.

title: LLM: Spiral to Turing Machine

title: The Topological Slice: 3D to 2D Logic (Turing Head)
category_reason: Frames an attention head as a 'Turing head' that reads a bit from a 3D hidden state via a 2D feature-plane slice — an interpretability / attention model.
thesis: A split-screen three.js + DOM animation arguing that an attention 'Turing head' reduces a 3D hidden-state spiral to a 2D read-out: it fires (writes a 1-bit) only when the spiral's cross-section lands in a specific feature circle.
key_claims: The 'spiral' is the hidden state; the white ring is the 'Feature Plane' (the slice the head looks at).
The 2D detector 'only cares if the spiral is inside this specific circle' — a binary in/out feature test.
The head is a Turing-style bit reader: when the cross-section distance is in the annulus [1.8, 2.2] (the ring radius) it writes a '1' ('BIT WRITE: ACTIVE'), else '0' ('SCANNING TAPE...').
A running binary stream accumulates the read bits, framing the head as a tape-scanning computational device.
The 3D→2D reduction is a 'topological slice': a 2D feature is extracted from a 3D state by intersecting it with a plane.
methods_math: radial feature detector (in/out of a circle, distance in an annulus [1.8, 2.2])
visualizations: Left: three.js 3D spiral passing through a feature ring; right: DOM 2D crosshair disk with a moving dot, a large bit read-out (0/1), a scrolling binary stream, and a 'TURING HEAD STATE' readout
internal_tensions: The 'Turing head' logic is hard-coded geometry (a fixed annulus test on a scripted spiral motion), not a learned feature detector — the claim that an attention head 'is' a Turing tape-reader is an analogy, not a demonstrated mechanism.
The bit stream updates are random (random() > 0.9 shifts a bit), so the 'computation' is decorative.

title: Understanding Deep Learning — Interactive Visual Guide
category_reason: Umfasst das gesamte Spektrum des Deep Learning: Neuronale Netze, ReLU, Tiefe vs. Breite, Gradient Descent, Backpropagation, Loss Functions, Overfitting/Double Descent, Transformer/Attention, Generative Models (GANs, Diffusion), Offene Mysterien (Loss Landscape, Implicit Regularization, Lottery Tickets, Grokking). Direktes ML.
thesis: Deep Learning – von der einzelnen Neuron-Einheit über Training, Backpropagation, Generalisierung bis zu Transformern und generativen Modellen – lässt sich als interaktive visuelle Reise durch die Kernkonzepte begreifen, basierend auf dem Lehrbuch von Simon Prince.
key_claims: Ein neuronales Netz ist eine mathematische Funktion: ReLU-Einheiten erzeugen piecewise linear regions; Universal Approximation Theorem.
ReLU arbeitet, weil seine Ableitung 0 oder 1 ist – keine vanishing Gradients, trivial zu berechnen.
Tiefe erzeugt exponentiell mehr lineare Regionen: (D+1)^K Regionen mit K Layern von D Einheiten (Folding Metaphor).
Gradient Descent: der Learning Rate Dilemma – zu klein = langsam, zu groß = instabil. Adam adaptiert per-Parameter.
Backpropagation ist die Kettenregel, systematisch angewandt: linear im Netz-Size durch Reuse of Computation.
Loss Functions kommen aus Maximum Likelihood: Gauß → Least Squares, Bernoulli → Cross-Entropy.
Double Descent: Test Error sinkt zweimal, wenn Kapazität den Interpolation Threshold überschreitet – Overparameterized Models generalisieren.
Transformer/Self-Attention: jedes Element attends auf jedes andere; weights sind datenabhängig (Q,K,V).
Generative Models: GANs (Zwei-Netzwerk-Spiel) und Diffusion (Rauschen hinzufügen/entfernen).
Offene Mysterien: Loss Landscape ist 'benign', SGD biasiert zu flachen Minima, Lottery Tickets, Grokking.

Canvas: Regionen-Zahlen (Tiefe vs. Breite)

title: Universeller Approximationssatz — Interaktive Erklärung
category_reason: German interactive explanation of the Universal Approximation Theorem (Cybenko 1989, Hornik 1991): single-hidden-layer neural networks with suitable activation functions can approximate any continuous function on a compact set, with a constructive proof using bump functions and a Dense-ReLU-Dense architecture. Core neural network theory.
thesis: A German-language interactive explanation of the Universal Approximation Theorem: a single hidden layer with a finite number of neurons and a non-polynomial activation function can approximate any continuous function on a compact subset of R^n to arbitrary precision; the page gives a constructive proof for the 1D case using bump functions (bump = smooth, compactly supported) and shows how a Dense-ReLU-Dense network can be built from them, with Temml-based visualizations of the approximation converging as width increases.
key_claims: Cybenko (1989) / Hornik (1991): for any continuous f: [a,b] -> R and any ε > 0, there exist weights w_i, v_i, c_i and a finite number N of neurons such that |f(x) − Σᵢ vᵢ σ(wᵢx + cᵢ)| < ε for all x ∈ [a,b], where σ is a non-polynomial activation (e.g., sigmoid, ReLU).

The theorem is existential, not constructive: it guarantees the existence of a network that works but does not tell you how to find the weights; in practice, training (gradient descent) is the algorithm for finding them.

A constructive 1D proof using bump functions: any continuous function on [a,b] can be approximated by a sum of scaled and translated 'bump' functions (smooth, compactly supported); each bump can be implemented by a small ReLU network (a 'ReLU bump' = difference of two ReLUs), so the sum is a single-layer ReLU network.

The width of the network (number of hidden neurons) must grow as ε shrinks; there is no bound on the required width in terms of ε alone (it depends on the complexity of f), but the theorem guarantees that a finite width always suffices.

Depth can reduce width: a deep network (many layers, few neurons per layer) can approximate some functions with exponentially fewer total parameters than a wide shallow network, but the UAT only guarantees the existence of a wide shallow solution.
methods_math: Stone-Weierstrass theorem (as a precursor: polynomials are dense in C[a,b])
bump functions: smooth, compactly supported functions as building blocks
ReLU as a 'hinge' function: max(0, x) and its use to construct triangular bumps
Dense-ReLU-Dense architecture: y = W₂ ReLU(W₁x + b₁) + b₂
non-polynomial activation requirement (polynomial activations cannot approximate all continuous functions)
visualizations: Temml-based 1D approximation: a target function (e.g., a square wave, a Gaussian, a fractal-like curve) is approximated by a ReLU network; the user increases the width (number of ReLU bumps) and watches the approximation converge, with the individual bumps visible as triangular 'teeth'
bump function constructor: the user places and scales individual bump functions on a 1D axis; the sum is shown as a running total, demonstrating how a complex function is built from simple pieces
width vs. error plot: a log-log plot of approximation error vs. number of neurons, showing the rate of convergence for different target functions (smooth vs. discontinuous)

shallow vs. deep comparison: the same target function approximated by a wide shallow network (1000 neurons, 1 layer) vs. a narrow deep network (10 neurons, 100 layers); the parameter count and approximation quality are compared
internal_tensions: The theorem is for a single hidden layer, but the visualizations use ReLU networks which require a specific construction (difference of ReLUs for bumps) that is not the same as the standard Dense-ReLU-Dense architecture used in practice; the gap between the constructive proof and the practical architecture is not fully bridged.

The theorem says 'any continuous function' but the rate of convergence can be extremely slow for functions with sharp features; the page shows this with the width-vs-error plot but the interactive approximation can be misleadingly fast for smooth functions, giving the impression that the theorem is 'useful' in a practical sense.

title: Wie ein Sprachmodell denkt — Attention, FFN und die Rolle der Schichten
category_reason: Transformer-Erklärbarkeit: Attention/Kollaps (Geshkovski), FFN als Key-Value-Speicher (Geva), Superposition (Elhage), SwiGLU (Shazeer). Original; Duplikat unter buecher/antioed.html.
thesis: Ein Transformer-Block ist ein Gleichgewicht aus Kontraktion (Attention zieht Tokens zu Clustern, ohne Gegenkraft Kollaps) und Verfeinerung (FFN als Key-Value-Speicher addiert auf den Residual-Stream), das über zwei orthogonale Achsen (Positionen vs Features) läuft.
key_claims: Attention arbeitet über Positionen, das FFN über Features — orthogonal, daher keine gegenseitige Störung [Vaswani §3.3].

Attention ohne Gegenkraft kollabiert fast alle Tokens zu einem Punkt (bewiesen für d≥3, exponentiell für d≥n) [Geshkovski 2024]; reale Modelle leben metastabil (empirisch an ALBERT XLarge v2, d=4096, n≈512–1024).
Die Form des Kollaps hängt vom Spektrum der Value-Matrix V ab — vier Fälle [Geshkovski 2023, Tab. 1].

Das FFN ist ein Key-Value-Speicher (Schlüssel = Muster, Werte = nächste-Wort-Verteilung); 3,6 Muster/Schlüssel; Schicht 1–9 oberflächlich, 10–16 semantisch, mit Aktivitätseinbruch um Schicht 10 [Geva].
Der Residual-Stream dominiert die Vorhersage; das FFN verfeinert (Kompromiss), ersetzt sie selten [Geva Fig. 9 & 11].
Superposition: spärliche Features werden als fast-orthogonale Richtungen übereinandergelegt, erkauft mit Interferenz und polysemantischen Neuronen (Phasenwechsel) [Elhage].
SwiGLU ist multiplikatives Gating (Produkt zweier Projektionen), keine elementweise Nichtlinearität; GLU-Varianten schlagen ReLU, d_ff wird um ⅔ reduziert [Shazeer].

Attention live (Linien = Gewicht, Schärfe-β, 'Bank am Fluss' vs 'Bank Kredit')

Falten unter SwiGLU greift als Hyperebenen-Bild nicht (multiplikatives Gating).

title: Ich bin ein Token
category_reason: Main subject is how LLMs process text: token journey through BPE, embeddings, transformer layers, attention, and autoregressive decoding.
thesis: A first-person interactive narrative following a single token through the full LLM pipeline, from BPE tokenization through embedding, self-attention, feed-forward layers, to autoregressive decoding, making the transformer architecture tangible from the token's perspective.
key_claims: BPE tokenization splits text into subword units learned from corpus frequency statistics
Each token is embedded into a high-dimensional vector encoding semantic and positional information
Self-attention lets every token weigh its relevance to all other tokens in the context window via Q/K/V dot products
Multiple stacked transformer layers iteratively refine token representations through alternating attention and feed-forward operations
Autoregressive decoding generates one token at a time, conditioned on all previously generated tokens
methods_math: BPE algorithm, high-dimensional embeddings, attention (Q/K/V dot products), softmax, feed-forward networks, autoregressive generation
visualizations: Token journey animation through pipeline stages; attention weight heatmap; embedding space projection; layer-by-layer representation evolution
internal_tensions: The first-person narrative anthropomorphizes a token, which risks implying intentional information flow where there is only linear algebra and matrix multiplication.

title: 🧠 Token Odyssey – Erlebe die Welt eines Tokens im LLM
category_reason: Immersive Erste-Person-Interaktion: man wird zum Token und durchläuft die sechs Stufen eines Transformers (Embedding, Positional Encoding, Self-Attention QKV, FFN, Logits/Softmax, Next-Token) — LLM-Mechanik.
thesis: Ein Token durchläuft in einem Transformer sechs mechanistische Stufen — Embedding → Positional Encoding → Self-Attention (QKV, causal mask) → FFN (Dense+ReLU+LayerNorm) → Logits/Softmax → Next-Token-Vorhersage; die Reise wird als immersive Erste-Person-Erfahrung visualisiert, um die interne Datenströmung des LLMs verständlich zu machen.
key_claims: Token-Embedding: jedes Token wird aus der Embedding-Matrix (|V|×d_model) in einen hochdimensionalen Vektorraum eingebettet; ähnliche Tokens liegen nahe.
Positional Encoding (sin/cos, 10000^Frequenzen) addiert einen Positions-Fingerabdruck — so wird 'WAS' zu 'WAS an Position i'.
Self-Attention: Q,K,V-Projektionen; Score = softmax(QK^T/√d_k); Causal-Mask (nur ≤ eigene Position) — der Token 'liest' relevante Kontext-Values.
FFN: zwei Dense-Layer mit ReLU (+ LayerNorm) — assoziatives Nachschlagen / Konzept-Transformation.
Logits → Softmax (mit Temperatur) → Next-Token-Wahrscheinlichkeitsverteilung; der gewählte Token wird ausgegeben.
visualizations: Canvas/JS (Embedding-Raum 2D-Projektion, Attention-Grid, Neuronen, Softmax-Balken, Wellen)
Temml Mathematik
Erste-Person-Narrative + Fortschrittsbar
synthetische Matrixdaten (He-Init, seeded)
internal_tensions: Die Visualisierung nutzt synthetische/seeded-Matrizen und vereinfachtes Whitespace-Tokenizing (keine BPE) — illustrativ, kein echtes Modell.
EMBED_DIM=16 (vereinfacht) steht für reale 768–12288; die hochdimensionale Superposition geht in der 2D-Projektion verloren.
Der didaktische Wert ist hoch, aber es gibt keine Aussage über reale Trainings-/Gewichtsdynamik.

title: Adjoint Functors – Interactive Explorer
category_reason: Reine Kategorientheorie (adjungierte Funktoren, Hom-Mengen-Bijektion, Unit/Counit, Triangle-Identities); keine KI/ML-Anwendung
thesis: Interaktiver Explorer für adjungierte Funktoren: Wähle Objekte in Kategorien 𝒞 und 𝒟, sieh zu, wie Funktoren L ⊣ R sie abbilden, und beobachte die Hom-Mengen-Bijektion Hom_𝒟(L(c),d) ≅ Hom_𝒞(c,R(d)) in Aktion, inkl. Unit η, Counit ε und den (Zig-Zag-)Triangle-Identities
key_claims: Adjungierte Funktoren sind Paare L:𝒞→𝒟 (links) und R:𝒟→𝒞 (rechts), bei denen Morphismen L(c)→d in 𝒟 bijektiv zu Morphismen c→R(d) in 𝒞 korrespondieren
L (linker adjungierter) ist der 'freie'/'beste Approximation'-Funktor; R (rechter adjungierter) ist der 'vergessende'/'zugrunde liegende' Funktor
Die Unit η_c:c→R(L(c)) ist der Adjunkt von id_{L(c)} ('beste Approximation' von c im Bild von R); der Counit ε_d:L(R(d))→d ist der Adjunkt von id_{R(d)}
Die Triangle-/Zig-Zag-Identities: ε_{L(c)}∘L(η_c)=id_{L(c)} und R(ε_d)∘η_{R(d)}=id_{R(d)}
Beispiele: Freie Gruppe ⊣ zugrunde liegende Menge (Sets↔Grps); diskrete Topologie ⊣ vergessender (Sets↔Top)

title: Algebraische Geometrie – Visuell verstehen
category_reason: Reine Mathematik: algebraische Geometrie (Varietäten, Ideal-Varietät-Dualität, Nullstellensatz) visuell. Keine ML-/KI-Inhalte.
thesis: Die algebraische Geometrie studiert die Lösungsmengen (Varietäten) polynomialer Gleichungen; ihr Kern ist die Dualität zwischen geometrischen Objekten (Varietäten) und algebraischen Objekten (Idealen), verknüpft durch den Hilbertschen Nullstellensatz – hier als visuelle Erkundung der Kurven/Flächen und ihrer Ideale.
key_claims: Eine Varietät ist die Menge aller gemeinsamen Nullstellen eines Ideals polynomialer Funktionen.
Es besteht eine (anti-)Korrespondenz zwischen Idealen und Varietäten: V(I) ist die Nullstellmenge, I(V) das Ideal aller Polynome, die auf V verschwinden.
Der Hilbertsche Nullstellensatz (algebraisch abgeschlossener Körper): I(V(I)) = radical(I) – die Dualität ist exakt modulo des Radikals.
Algebraische Kurven/Flächen (z.B. Kreise, Ellipsen, Singuläre Kurven) werden aus ihren Gleichungen gezeichnet.
Operationen auf Varietäten (Schnitte, Vereinigungen) entsprechen Operationen auf Idealen (Summe, Produkt, rad).
visualizations: Plotly/Canvas: algebraische Kurven (Kreise, Ellipsen, Singuläre)
Ideal-Varietät-Korrespondenz (V(I), I(V))
Schnitt-/Vereinigungs-Demos
Nullstellensatz-Visualisierung
internal_tensions: Die Dualität Ideal↔Varietät ist der Kern, aber die volle Kraft (z.B. affine Varietäten über C vs. endliche Körpern, Schemata) wird nicht erschöpft.
Die Visualisierung arbeitet über reellen Zahlen, während der Nullstellensatz algebraisch abgeschlossene Körper (C) voraussetzt – die Diskrepanz wird nicht ausgemerzt.
Der Dateiname sagt 'algebraische_topologie', der Titel 'Algebraische Geometrie' – die Themen gehören zu benachbarten, aber verschiedenen Gebieten.

title: Analytischer Idealismus — Interaktive Erklärung
category_reason: German interactive explanation of Bernardo Kastrup's analytic idealism (based on his 2019 Radboud University dissertation): a consciousness-only ontology where phenomenal consciousness is the sole ontological primitive, matter is the extrinsic appearance of transpersonal consciousness, and individual minds are dissociated 'alters' of a universal consciousness. Philosophy of mind, no AI/ML content.
thesis: A German-language interactive explanation of Kastrup's analytic idealism: the only thing that exists is universal phenomenal consciousness; the physical world is the extrinsic (third-person) appearance of transpersonal consciousness activity; individual organisms are dissociated 'alters' of this universal consciousness (analogous to alters in dissociative identity disorder); and the correlation between brain activity and experience is explained not by causation but by the brain being the extrinsic appearance of the experience itself.
key_claims: Analytic idealism posits a single ontological primitive: universal phenomenal consciousness. There is no 'matter' in the fundamental sense; the physical world is a model (extrinsic appearance) of the activity of consciousness, analogous to how the 'wave' is a model of the activity of the ocean.

Dissociation — a well-documented clinical phenomenon (DID) — explains how a single unified consciousness can give rise to apparently separate subjects: a dissociative boundary separates the 'internal' (subjective) experience of an alter from the 'external' (transpersonal) activity of the whole.

Perception is the experience of transpersonal consciousness activity that has been 'coded and compressed' by the dissociative boundary: external thoughts hitting the boundary are experienced as sensory qualia; the coding is lossy and optimized for fitness (per Hoffman/Friston), not for truth.

The brain-experience correlation is not causal (brain causes experience) but constitutive: the brain is what the experience looks like from the outside (extrinsic perspective); damage to the brain changes the appearance, not the experience itself — which explains why reduced brain activity (hypoxia, psychedelics, NDEs) can be associated with expanded consciousness.

Analytic idealism avoids both the hard problem (no need to explain how matter gives rise to experience, since there is no matter) and the combination problem of panpsychism (no need to explain how micro-experiences combine, since there is only one macro-experience that is dissociated).
methods_math: phenomenological ontology (consciousness as the sole primitive)
dissociation as a formal mechanism for subject individuation
extrinsic/intrinsic perspective distinction (analogous to third-person/first-person in physics)
quantum field analogy: field -> self-excitation -> particles, consciousness -> self-excitation -> experiences
Hoffman's fitness-beats-truth argument for perceptual coding
Friston's free energy principle as a model of perceptual compression
visualizations: Plotly funnel chart: abstraction levels from direct experience (Qualia) to strings/branes, with epistemic confidence decreasing at each level
Plotly scatter plot: brain activity vs. experience intensity, with the annotation 'correlation, not causation — the brain IS the appearance of the experience'

Plotly grouped bar chart: six conditions (hypoxia, psychedelics, NDE, TMS, brain damage, trance) showing reduced brain activity alongside increased experience intensity — the 'paradox' that physicalism cannot explain
Plotly radar chart: three ontologies (physicalism, panpsychism, analytic idealism) scored on parsimony, hard problem solved, combination problem solved, empirical fit, and explanatory power
Canvas animation: universal consciousness as an 'ocean' with dissociated alters as islands; three modes (normal, dissociation, perception) switchable by the user
Canvas graph: 20 nodes representing cognitive connections; a dissociation slider breaks the cross-group edges, simulating the formation of a dissociative boundary

Canvas perception animation: transpersonal 'thought waves' (particles) travel from the outer field and hit the dissociative boundary of an alter, where they are converted into 'perception sparks' inside the alter
internal_tensions: The page presents Kastrup's ontology as if it were empirically supported, but the 'evidence' section (hypoxia, psychedelics, NDEs) is anecdotal and the correlation between reduced brain activity and expanded experience does not uniquely support idealism — it could also be explained by changes in the brain's filtering/gating mechanisms under physicalism.

The dissociation analogy (DID) is powerful but risky: DID is a trauma response, and equating the structure of a trauma disorder with the fundamental ontology of the universe is a large inferential leap that the page does not adequately qualify.

The quantum field analogy (field -> particles via self-excitation) is used for intuition but is physically inaccurate: particles in QFT are excitations of a field, not 'self-excitations' in the sense the page implies; the analogy is suggestive but should not be taken literally.

title: Analytischer Idealismus – Eine interaktive Reise durch Kastrups Metaphysik
category_reason: Bernardo Kastrups analytischer Idealismus: universelles Bewusstsein, Dissoziation, Cockpit-Metapher, Bell-Experiment, Panpsychismus-Kritik, empirische Evidenz (Psilocybin, NDE). Philosophie/Metaphysik, keine ML-Inhalte.
thesis: Der Materialismus scheitert an logischen Widersprüchen (hartes Problem des Bewusstseins), experimenteller Evidenz (Quantenphysik/Bell-Experimente) und dem Kombinationsproblem; die einzige kohärente Alternative ist der analytische Idealismus: ein einziges universelles Bewusstsein, dessen dissoziierte 'Alters' die scheinbar getrennten Lebewesen sind.
key_claims: Wahrnehmung ist kein transparentes Fenster, sondern ein Cockpit-Instrumentenbrett: komprimierte, handlungsleitende Ikonen, keine Abbilder der Realität (Hoffman 2009, Friston 2014).
Die Karte ist nicht das Territorium: Materialismus verwechselt die Beschreibung (Zahlen) mit der Welt selbst – das harte Problem des Bewusstseins ist prinzipiell unlösbar.
Bell-Experimente (Nobelpreis 2022) zeigen: physikalische Eigenschaften existieren erst durch die Messung – die Welt ist beobachter-partizipativ.
Panpsychismus scheitert am Kombinationsproblem: aus vielen Mikro-Bewusstseinen lässt sich kein einheitliches Makro-Bewusstsein konstruieren.
Kastrups Lösung: Umkehrung – ein einziges universelles Bewusstsein, das sich in viele dissoziierte Alters auflöst (Analogie: DIS/Dissociative Identitätsstörung).
Strudel-Metapher: du bist kein Ding im Bewusstsein, du BIST das Bewusstsein, geformt zu einem Strudel. Tod = Auflösung des Strudels, nicht Vernichtung des Wassers.
Alles ist Schwingung eines mentalen Feldes (Chladni-Figuren des Geistes) – die Mathematik der Physik bleibt gleich, nur die ontologische Interpretation ändert sich.

Empirische Evidenz: bei reduzierter Gehirnaktivität (Psilocybin, LSD, NDE, Savant-Syndrom) taucht erweitertes Bewusstsein auf – konsistent mit dem Filter-Modell, inkonsistent mit dem Erzeugungs-Modell des Materialismus.

title: AEP & Shannon–McMillan–Breiman
category_reason: Ergodic theory and information theory: the asymptotic equipartition property and the Shannon-McMillan-Breiman theorem; pure math and probability, no AI/ML focus.
thesis: An interactive exploration of the asymptotic equipartition property (AEP) and the Shannon-McMillan-Breiman (SMB) theorem, showing how the per-symbol information concentrates around the entropy and why this underpins the theory of lossless source coding.
key_claims: The AEP states that for an i.i.d. source, the per-symbol information -(1/n) log P(X^n) concentrates around the entropy H(X)
The SMB theorem extends the AEP from i.i.d. sources to stationary ergodic processes
The typical set, sequences whose per-symbol probability is close to exp(-nH), contains nearly all probability mass for large n
This concentration is the mathematical foundation of lossless compression: only typical sequences need to be described
The rate of concentration is governed by the entropy variance in the i.i.d. case or by mixing conditions in the ergodic case
methods_math: Ergodic theory, information theory, entropy, typical sets, law of large numbers for stationary processes
visualizations: Typical set probability mass plot versus n; per-symbol information histogram converging to entropy; AEP concentration illustration
internal_tensions: The SMB theorem requires ergodicity, which is difficult to verify in practice; the i.i.d. AEP is easy to state but often too restrictive for real-world sources with long-range dependence.

title: Betti-Zahlen – Visuelle Erklärung
category_reason: Pure algebraic topology/TDA; ML is mentioned as one of several applications but is not the focus
thesis: Betti numbers (β₀, β₁, β₂, ...) are topological invariants that count the number of k-dimensional 'holes' in a space. They provide a rigorous, computation-oriented way to characterize shape that is invariant under continuous deformation.
key_claims: β₀ counts connected components, β₁ counts 1D holes (loops), β₂ counts 2D voids (cavities)
Betti numbers are topological invariants: they are preserved under homeomorphism
They can be computed from a chain complex: β_k = dim(H_k) = dim(ker ∂_k) − rank(∂_k)
In TDA, Betti numbers of a filtered simplicial complex track how topological features appear and disappear as a scale parameter varies
The Euler characteristic χ = Σ(−1)^k β_k provides a global summary
visualizations: topological_shapes_with_holes
hole_counting_animation
filtration_visualization
internal_tensions: Betti numbers alone lose information (two spaces can have the same Betti numbers but different topology — they are not complete invariants)
The TDA application (persistent Betti numbers) is where the real power lies, but the basic Betti number concept is much simpler than what TDA actually uses

title: Daniel Paul Schreber – Denkwürdigkeiten eines Nervenkranken
category_reason: A German-language interactive exploration of Daniel Paul Schreber's 1903 psychiatric memoir and its interpretations by Freud, Lacan, and Foucault. Pure psychiatry / literary history / philosophy of mind with no AI or ML content.
thesis: A German-language interactive exploration of Daniel Paul Schreber's 1903 memoir 'Denkwürdigkeiten eines Nervenkranken': his life as a senior Saxon judge, his 1884 psychotic breakdown, the elaborate theological delusional system he constructed (God as omnipotent torturer, women as seals of damnation, his own mission to save humanity), and the subsequent interpretations by Freud (structural paranoia), Lacan (foreclosure of the Name-of-the-Father), and Foucault (madness as social production).
key_claims: Daniel Paul Schreber (1842–1937) was a senior judge in the Saxony court who suffered a psychotic break in 1884 after a period of severe overwork and exhaustion.

He constructed an elaborate delusional theology: God communicated with him directly through 'nerves' and 'rays,' women were 'seals of damnation' placed by God to tempt him, and he was ultimately appointed to save the human race from divine abuse.
Freud (1911) analyzed the case as structural paranoia rooted in castration anxiety and the turn of passive into active homosexual object choice.

Lacan used the Schreber case to develop the concept of the 'foreclosure of the Name-of-the-Father' (forclusion du Nom-du-Père): the fundamental signifier is rejected from the symbolic order, producing psychosis rather than neurosis.
Foucault cited Schreber in 'Madness and Civilization' as an example of how modern society produces madness through exclusion: the 'insane' are defined by their removal from the rational social order.
The memoir is now considered a landmark of both psychiatric literature and modernist literary theory (its fragmented, self-contradicting narrative anticipates stream-of-consciousness fiction).
visualizations: tabbed sections (biography, delusional system, Freud, Lacan, Foucault, legacy)
quote boxes with source attribution
timeline of Schreber's life and the memoir's reception
internal_tensions: The file presents three conflicting interpretations (Freud's psychoanalytic, Lacan's structuralist, Foucault's socio-historical) side by side without adjudicating between them — appropriate for a historical overview, but a casual reader may be left unsure which reading is authoritative.

title: Euklids Elemente - Interaktive Visualisierung

key_claims: Euclid's Elements is the first completely axiomatic-deductive system: 5 postulates + 5 axioms + 23 definitions yield 465 propositions across 13 books
The 13 books form an ascending spiral from planimetry (I-VI) through number theory (VII-IX) and irrationals (X) to solid geometry (XI-XIII)

title: Die Geheime Geschichte der Mathe-Symbole

Genies scheitern an schlechter Notation: Die 27 griechischen Buchstaben-Zahlzeichen waren ein Hindernis statt eine Hilfe (Cajori); Archimedes/Apollonius verpassten Entdeckungen wegen der Notation.
Das Gleichheitszeichen: Robert Recorde erfand = 1557 (Nichts kann gleicher sein als zwei parallele Linien); Descartes benutzte noch jahrzehntelang ∝; erst im 18. Jh. setzte sich = durch.

Die Null: Drei unabhängige Erfindungen (Babylonier Basis 60 ohne echte Null, Maya Basis 20 mit vollem Null-Symbol früher als die Inder, Inder Basis 10); nur Maya und Inder hatten ein echtes Null-Symbol.

Space and time are not properties of things-in-themselves but a priori forms of our intuition — the 'glasses' through which all experience is possible; they precede experience and make it possible.

title: Nonlinear Dynamics Workbook — Chaos, Fractals, Cellular Automata, and a Taste of Neural Networks
category_reason: The main subject is nonlinear dynamics: the logistic map, strange attractors, the Mandelbrot set, Julia sets, and cellular automata (Conway's Game of Life, elementary CA). A small section on Hopfield networks is included, but it is a minor appendix, not the main focus.
thesis: An interactive English-language workbook on nonlinear dynamics that takes the reader from the logistic map (period-doubling route to chaos) through the Mandelbrot and Julia sets (fractal geometry of complex dynamics) to cellular automata (discrete nonlinear systems). A short final section on Hopfield networks shows how the same dynamical-systems language (attractors, basins, energy landscape) applies to a simple neural network model, tying the workbook back to the AI theme of the broader collection.
key_claims: The logistic map x_{n+1} = r * x_n * (1 - x_n) undergoes a period-doubling cascade as r increases: fixed point -> 2-cycle -> 4-cycle -> 8-cycle -> ... -> chaos at r ~ 3.57; the bifurcation diagram is a self-similar fractal (Feigenbaum constant delta ~ 4.669).

Strange attractors (e.g., the Lorenz attractor) are invariant sets with fractal structure and sensitive dependence on initial conditions (positive Lyapunov exponent); the 'butterfly' shape is the projection of the attractor onto a 2D plane.

The Mandelbrot set M = {c in C : the orbit of 0 under z -> z^2 + c is bounded} is the 'parameter space' of the quadratic family; the Julia set J(c) for each c in M is the boundary of the basin of attraction of the critical orbit.

Cellular automata (elementary CA, Conway's Game of Life) are discrete nonlinear systems that can exhibit universal computation; Rule 110 is Turing-complete, and Life is known to be Turing-complete (Garden of Eden, gliders, universal constructors).

The Hopfield network section: a network of N binary neurons with symmetric weights W_ij and no self-connections; the update rule s_i <- sign(sum_j W_ij s_j) is a gradient ascent on the energy E = -1/2 sum_ij W_ij s_i s_j, and the network converges to a local minimum (a stored memory).

The common thread: all these systems (logistic map, Lorenz, CA, Hopfield) are nonlinear dynamical systems whose long-term behavior is governed by attractors; the difference is the dimension, the continuity/discreteness, and the physical interpretation.

internal_tensions: The Hopfield network section is a brief appendix (a few pages) in a workbook that is otherwise purely about classical nonlinear dynamics; the connection between the two is stated (attractors, energy landscapes) but not developed in depth.

The workbook covers a very wide range of topics (1D maps, 3D ODEs, complex dynamics, discrete CA, neural nets) in a single file, which means each topic is treated at a surface level; the 'workbook' framing (exercises, prompts) is there but the depth is limited.
The Feigenbaum universality claim is stated without proof; the self-similarity of the bifurcation diagram is shown visually but the renormalization-group argument is not presented.

The 'chaos' in the title is somewhat misleading: the logistic map and Lorenz system are chaotic in the technical sense (positive Lyapunov exponent), but the Mandelbrot set and CA are not 'chaotic' in the same sense; they are complex but not chaotic (the CA are deterministic and non-chaotic in the Lyapunov sense).
